RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r1.claim: The command to seek refuge applies to every creature, not a single person, since God recounts prophets and saints doing so; Razi says all creatures must seek refuge in God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r1.anchor: أمر منه لعباده أن يقولوا ذلك وهذا غير مختص بشخص معين

RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r7.speaker: امرأة عمران
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r7.claim: Mary's mother entrusted her and her descendants to God's protection from Satan, and God accepted Mary and caused her to grow well.

RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r11.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r11.claim: Muʿādh ibn Jabal reports that two men quarreled and traded insults before the Prophet; the excerpt stops as the Prophet begins to answer.

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r1.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r1.claim: Depending on the reading of the verb, the phrase can mean God placed Mary in Zachariah's care or Zachariah took her into his care.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r1.anchor: Depending on how the verb in placed her under the care of Zachariah

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r2.claim: The account of Zachariah caring for Mary is usually read alongside the lot-casting described in 3:44.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r2.anchor: This verse is usually understood in light of v. 44:

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r3.claim: Islamic tradition makes Zachariah's wife Mary's maternal aunt or other maternal relative, not necessarily her mother's sister.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r3.anchor: In the Islamic tradition, Zachariah’s wife is Mary’s maternal

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r4.claim: God's beautiful acceptance of Mary's prayer is understood as protection for Mary and then Jesus.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r4.anchor: God accepted her prayer with a beautiful acceptance by protecting Mary, and then Jesus

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r5.claim: A Christian counterpart to Mary's Temple presentation appears in the noncanonical Protoevangelium of James, which Catholic and Orthodox traditions recognize.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r5.anchor: A possible Christian counterpart to the Quran’s narration about Mary’s life at the Temple, but one that does not appear in the Bible, is found in noncanonical literature such as the Protoevangelium of James

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r6.speaker: Protoevangelium of James
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r6.claim: The account says Mary's parents, previously childless, presented her at the Temple at age three to fulfill a vow dedicating her to God.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r6.anchor: According to this account, Mary was presented at the Temple at age three by her parents, who had previously been childless

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r7.claim: The Bible itself says almost nothing about Mary's youth.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r7.anchor: Almost nothing of Mary’s youth is to be found in the Bible itself

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r8.claim: The provision passage is inscribed over prayer niches in many mosques, but here miḥrāb means Mary's separate sanctuary rather than a wall niche.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r8.anchor: In this verse, miḥrāb is translated sanctuary, as Mary’s sanctuary would have been a separate room or area, not a niche hollowed out in a wall

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r9.claim: The miḥrāb is also where Zachariah receives news of John's birth in 3:39 and emerges to signal praise in 19:11.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r9.anchor: It is mentioned in v. 39 as the place where Zachariah is given news of his son John’s impending birth and again in 19:11 as the place from which he emerges

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r10.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r10.claim: Mary's provision may be material, spiritual, or both.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r10.anchor: The provision can be either material or spiritual, or both (IK)

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r11.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r11.claim: Some commentators say Mary received summer fruits in winter and winter fruits in summer.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r11.anchor: Some commentators say that Mary would have had the fruits of summer in winter and of winter in summer

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r12.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r12.claim: Others say the provision seemed to multiply beyond its initial amount.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r12.anchor: but others have said, rather, that what she was given seemed to multiply beyond the original amount (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r13.claim: God's provision without reckoning is limitless and uncountable, and God answers to no one for how He provides.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r13.anchor: means that God’s Provision is limitless, uncountable, and that God answers to no one for the way in which He provides for His creation

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r14.claim: Out-of-season fruit would imply that no human brought it to Mary.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r14.anchor: That the fruits were out of season would have implied that no human being could have brought them to her

STUDYQURAN:3:37/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r15.claim: The provision symbolizes both Mary and her mother conceiving out of season: Mary without a man's touch and her mother at an advanced age.
STUDYQURAN:3:37/r15.anchor: This Divine provision is also a symbol of the fact that both Mary and her

TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r1.claim: God favorably accepted Mary’s mother’s dedication of her to the church and to service of God.
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r1.anchor: إياها للكنيسة وخدمتها، وخدمة ربها بقبول حسن

TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r2.claim: قبول is a verbal noun from قبلها, expressed in a different pattern from the verb; the expected form on that pattern would be تقبلا حسنا.
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r2.anchor: والقبول: مصدر من قبلها ربها، فأخرج المصدر على غير لفظ الفعل، ولو كان على لفظه لكان: فتقبلها ربها تقبلا حسنا

TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r3.claim: Ṭabarī notes that Arabic often forms a verbal noun on the root pattern despite an augmented verb, as in تكلم كلاما rather than the expected تكلما.
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r3.anchor: أن يأتوا بالمصادر على أصول الأفعال وإن اختلفت ألفاظها في الأفعال بالزيادة، وذلك كقولهم: تكلم فلان كلاما

TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r4.claim: Abu Amr says he never heard Arabs pronounce qabul with a damma on qaf, though analogy predicts it as a verbal noun like dukhul and khuruj; he knew no other comparable word.
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي عمرو وأما، قوله: {وأنبتها نباتا حسنا} [آل عمران: 37] فإن معناه

TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r5.claim: God nurtured Mary with sustenance until she matured into a complete adult woman.
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r5.anchor: وأنبتها ربها في غذائه ورزقه نباتا حسنا حتى تمت فكملت امرأة بالغة تامة

TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God accepted what Mary’s mother intended by dedicating her to the church and rewarded her there.
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال الله عز وجل: {فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن} [آل عمران: 37] قال: «تقبل من أمها ما أرادت بها للكنيسة وآجرها فيها»

TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p344#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains her good growth as growth nourished by God.

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r1.speaker: قراء أهل الحجاز والمدينة والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r1.claim: The Hijazi, Medinan, and Basran readers lighten the fāʾ, making Zakariya the one who took Maryam into his care; they connect this wording with 3:44.

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r2.speaker: قراء الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r2.claim: The Kufan readers read the fāʾ doubled, meaning God made Zakariya Maryam’s guardian.

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the doubled fāʾ: God assigned Maryam to Zakariya by the lot and sign that made him prevail over his rivals, so his custody followed God’s judgment.
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r3.anchor: مشددة الفاء بمعنى: وكفلها الله زكريا

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r4.claim: One account says Zakariya’s lot stood still while the other lots were carried by the river, indicating that he had the strongest claim to Maryam.
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r4.anchor: فقال بعض أهل العلم: رتب قدح زكريا، فقام فلم يجر به الماء وجرى بقداح الآخرين الماء

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r5.claim: Another account says Zakariya’s lot went upstream while the others flowed downstream and disappeared, marking him as the one entitled to her.
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل صعد قدح زكريا في النهر، وانحدرت قداح الآخرين مع جرية الماء وذهبت

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r6.claim: Whichever account of the lots is correct, al-Ṭabarī says God decreed Maryam’s custody for Zakariya over the other claimants; Zakariya took her by God’s award.
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r6.anchor: وأي الأمرين كان من ذلك فلا شك أن ذلك كان قضاء من الله بها لزكريا على خصومه

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r7.claim: The appeal to the light reading of 3:44 does not prove that this verse must also be light: one can say that God made Zakariya her guardian by His judgment in the lot.
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r7.anchor: فحجة دالة على ضعف احتيال المحتج بها

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r8.speaker: قراء المدينة
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r8.claim: The general Medinan readers lengthen the name Zakariyya, while the general Kufan readers shorten it; al-Ṭabarī calls both established languages and readings with the same meaning.
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r8.anchor: قرأته عامة قراء المدينة بالمد، وقرأته عامة قراء الكوفة بالقصر

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r9.claim: Both long and short forms of Zakariya are sound, widespread readings and do not differ in meaning, so either is correct.
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r9.anchor: وهما لغتان معروفتان وقراءتان مستفيضتان في قراءة المسلمين، وليس في القراءة بإحداهما خلاف لمعنى القراءة الأخرى

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r10.claim: With the lengthened form, Zakariyya is accusative without nunation as a foreign proper name; on al-Ṭabarī’s doubled-fāʾ reading, it is the direct object of the verb.
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r10.anchor: اسم من أسماء العجم لا يجرى

TAB-FULL:v5p345/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r11.claim: A third form, Zakariy without the long vowel and silent yāʾ, is not recitable because it conflicts with the Muslim codices, though Arabic treats it like a nisba form and declines it.
TAB-FULL:v5p345/r11.anchor: وفي زكريا لغة ثالثة لا تجوز القراءة بها لخلافها مصاحف المسلمين وهو زكري

TAB-FULL:v5p347/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r1.claim: The rajaz line uses kāfil for one who gathers stray animals and takes them into his care; the alternate wording evokes straying or fleeing animals.

TAB-FULL:v5p347/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r2.claim: The Arabic question “Why do you take every stray?” illustrates kafala as taking a stray animal in and keeping it.
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r2.anchor: يقال منه للرجل: ما لك تكفل كل ضالة؟ يعني به: تضمها إليك وتأخذها

TAB-FULL:v5p347/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r3.claim: Ikrima reports that the lots flowed with the current except Zakariya’s pen, which rose upstream, and he consequently became Maryam’s guardian.
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم}

TAB-FULL:v5p347/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r4.claim: Al-Rabi explains that Zakariya took Maryam in; the contestants cast staffs toward the current, and Zakariya’s staff faced it and defeated theirs.
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r4.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، قوله: {وكفلها زكريا}

TAB-FULL:v5p347/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r5.claim: Al-Suddi relates that Torah scribes used lots to choose who would raise a child brought to them; Zakariya, whose wife was Maryam’s aunt, won the contest and took her into his house, the sanctuary.
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r5.anchor: عن السدي، قال الله عز وجل: {فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن

TAB-FULL:v5p347/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r6.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as Zakariya taking Maryam in with him.
TAB-FULL:v5p347/r6.anchor: عن قتادة: {وكفلها زكريا} [آل عمران: 37] يقول: «ضمها إليه»

TAB-FULL:v5p351/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r1.claim: Mujahid says Zakariya’s lot was determined by his own pen.

TAB-FULL:v5p351/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r2.claim: Qatada says Maryam was the daughter of their chief and prayer leader; the scholars contested custody, drew lots, and Zakariya, her sister’s husband, raised her in his home.
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " كانت مريم ابنة سيدهم وإمامهم

TAB-FULL:v5p351/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r3.claim: Ikrima recounts that Maryam’s mother dedicated her daughter to the temple; after the leaders disputed custody and drew lots with their Torah pens, Zakariya prevailed and took her.
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: " ثم خرجت بها يعني أم مريم

TAB-FULL:v5p351/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Zakariya placed Maryam with him in his sanctuary.
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " جعلها زكريا معه في محرابه

TAB-FULL:v5p351/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains that “kahin” in their speech means a learned person.
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r5.anchor: قال حجاج: قال ابن جريج: الكاهن في كلامهم: العالم

TAB-FULL:v5p351/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r6.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq’s report through Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr stresses that Maryam was orphaned after both her father and mother, then recounts her and Zakariya’s story.
TAB-FULL:v5p351/r6.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير: {وكفلها زكريا}

TAB-FULL:v5p353/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Maryam was with Zakariya, who placed her in his sanctuary.
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله: {وكفلها زكريا}

TAB-FULL:v5p353/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the people drew lots over Maryam, Zakariya won, and he became her guardian.
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وأنبتها نباتا حسنا}

TAB-FULL:v5p353/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r3.claim: An alternative account says Zakariya first cared for Maryam without a contest, keeping her with her aunt after her parents died; much later, hardship led others to draw lots to divide her maintenance, not from rivalry for her.
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r3.anchor: غير أن القول متظاهر من أهل التأويل بالقول الأول

TAB-FULL:v5p353/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r4.speaker: شعيب الجبئي
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r4.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾi reports that Yahya’s mother, Maryam’s aunt, was named Ashiʿ.
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r4.anchor: عن شعيب الجبئي، " أن اسم أم يحيى: أشيع

TAB-FULL:v5p353/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r5.claim: Although the no-lot account would support the light reading if true, al-Ṭabarī prefers doubling the fāʾ because the dominant exegetical account places the lots before Zakariya’s custody and says he won over his rivals.
TAB-FULL:v5p353/r5.anchor: غير أن القول متظاهر من أهل التأويل بالقول الأول أن استهام القوم فيها كان قبل كفالة زكريا إياها

TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains that whenever Zakariya entered the sanctuary where he had placed Maryam, he found provision from God for her nourishment; reports identify it as fruit out of season.
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r1.anchor: وفاكهة الصيف في الشتاء ذكر من قال ذلك

TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the provision as grapes in a basket, found outside their season.
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وجد عندها رزقا} [آل عمران: 37] قال: «وجد عندها عنبا

TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the provision was grapes appearing out of season.
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r3.anchor: عن عطاء، عن سعيد، في قوله:

TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim glosses the provision as fruit appearing outside its season.
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {وجد عندها رزقا}

TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says Maryam had summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك، «أنه كان يجد عندها فاكهة الصيف في الشتاء

TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says Zakariya found grapes at Maryam’s place in their off-season.
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: «كان يجد عندها العنب في غير حينه»

TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r7.claim: Mujahid also describes the gift as summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وجد عندها رزقا}

TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r8.claim: Qatada says they used to relate that Maryam received winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
TAB-FULL:v5p353#2/r8.anchor: قال: «كنا نحدث أنها كانت تؤتى بفاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

TAB-FULL:v5p357/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r1.claim: Qatada says Maryam was found with fruit outside its usual season.

TAB-FULL:v5p357/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says Zakariya placed seven doors around Maryam and found summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer when he entered.
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r2.anchor: عن الربيع، قال: «جعل زكريا دونها عليها سبعة أبواب

TAB-FULL:v5p357/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Zakariya kept Maryam in the sanctuary and found each season’s fruit at the opposite time of year.
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: «جعلها زكريا معه في بيت وهو المحراب

TAB-FULL:v5p357/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says Zakariya found summer fruit in winter.
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله: {وجد عندها رزقا}

TAB-FULL:v5p357/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the provision as fruits of Paradise, with summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا}

TAB-FULL:v5p357/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from some learned authorities that Zakariya found winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r6.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: ثني بعض أهل العلم

TAB-FULL:v5p357/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r7.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says the provision came from heaven and not from people; the report reasons that if Zakariya knew its source, he would not have asked Maryam about it.
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r7.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: " كان زكريا إذا دخل عليها - يعني على مريم - المحراب وجد عندها رزقا من السماء من الله، ليس من عند الناس

TAB-FULL:v5p357/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r8.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r8.claim: Another view says the provision was an excess beyond what Maryam’s appointed caretaker brought her, rather than food appearing miraculously from heaven.
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك أن زكريا كان إذا دخل إليها المحراب وجد عندها من الرزق

TAB-FULL:v5p357/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r9.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r9.claim: Ibn Ishaq relates that during famine Zakariya could no longer maintain Maryam; the Israelites also struggled, so they drew lots to assign her maintenance, and the lot fell to a carpenter named Jurayj.
TAB-FULL:v5p357/r9.anchor: محمد بن إسحاق، قال: " كفلها بعد هلاك أمها، فضمها إلى خالتها أم يحيى

TAB-FULL:v5p358/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r1.claim: In Ibn Ishaq’s account, the carpenter Jurayj brought food from his earnings, but God increased it inside the sanctuary; Maryam urged him to trust God, and Zakariya found the extra provision and asked its source.
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r1.anchor: قال: فعرفت مريم في وجهه شدة مؤنة ذلك عليه، فكانت تقول له: يا جريج، أحسن بالله الظن

TAB-FULL:v5p358/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī defines the mihrab as the foremost and most honored place in an assembly or prayer place, including a mosque; its plural can be maḥārib as well as maḥārīb.
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r2.anchor: وأما المحراب فهو مقدم كل مجلس ومصلى، وهو سيد المجالس وأشرفها وأكرمها

TAB-FULL:v5p358/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r3.claim: The line by ʿAdī ibn Zayd compares ivory figures in mihrabs with bright eggs in a flowered meadow, illustrating the word’s sense of honored prayer places.
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r3.anchor: كدمى العاج في المحاريب أو كال … بيض في الروض زهره مستنير

TAB-FULL:v5p358/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī gives both al-maḥārīb and al-maḥārib as plurals of mihrab.
TAB-FULL:v5p358/r4.anchor: والمحاريب جمع محراب، وقد يجمع على محارب

TAB-FULL:v5p359/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r1.claim: Zakariya asks Maryam where or by what means she got the provision he sees; she answers that God sent and gave it to her.
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r1.anchor: يعني بذلك جل ثناؤه: قال زكريا يا مريم: أنى لك هذا؟ من أي وجه لك هذا الذي أرى عندك من الرزق

TAB-FULL:v5p359/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says Zakariya shut seven doors, entered, and repeatedly found fruit out of season, prompting his astonished question to Maryam.
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r2.anchor: أنه كان فيما ذكر لنا يغلق عليها سبعة أبواب، ويخرج ثم يدخل عليها، فيجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

TAB-FULL:v5p359/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits a similar account: Zakariya was amazed to find the seasons’ fruits reversed and asked Maryam where they came from.
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: ثني بعض أهل العلم، فذكر نحوه

TAB-FULL:v5p359/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Zakariya found fresh fruit with Maryam when no one else had any, so he asked her where it came from.
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {يا مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله}

TAB-FULL:v5p359/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r5.claim: God provides whoever He wills without measure: giving does not diminish His store or change His dominion, and unlike a limited giver, He neither fears depletion nor lacks knowledge of what He gives.
TAB-FULL:v5p359/r5.anchor: فخبر من الله أنه يسوق إلى من يشاء من خلقه رزقه بغير إحصاء ولا عدد

TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r1.claim: Her good growth means God gave Mary and her descendants guidance, purity, and a life untouched by Satan's whispering and temptation.
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r1.anchor: والمراد بإنباتها نباتا حسنا إعطاء الرشد والزكاة لها ولذريتها وإفاضة الحياة لها

TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r2.claim: The good acceptance and growth correspond to God's choosing and purifying Mary in 3:42; her and Jesus' later distinction fulfills the statement that the male is not like the female.
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r2.anchor: وهذان أعني القبول الحسن الراجع إلى الاصطفاء والنبات الحسن الراجع إلى التطهير هما اللذان يشير إليهما

TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r3.claim: Zechariah became Mary's guardian when the lot fell to him after the disputants agreed to draw lots, as 3:44 relates.
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r3.anchor: وإنما كفلها بإصابة القرعة حيث اختصموا في تكفلها ثم تراضوا بينهم بالقرعة

TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r4.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r4.claim: Rāghib lists explanations of miḥrāb: a place to combat Satan and desire, a place free of worldly distraction, or a room's front modeled on the mosque's; he favors the last account.
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r4.anchor: قال الراغب ومحراب المسجد قيل سمي بذلك لأنه موضع محاربة الشيطان والهوى

TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r5.claim: Some identify this miḥrāb with the Christian altar or sanctuary, an elevated enclosed chamber at the temple's front; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī traces the Islamic prayer enclosure to this form.
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r5.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن المحراب هنا هو ما يعبر عنه أهل الكتاب بالمذبح وهو مقصورة في مقدم المعبد

TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r6.claim: A reported example of Mary's unusual provision is winter fruit appearing in summer and summer fruit in winter.
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r6.anchor: كما قيل إنه كان يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف وفاكهة الصيف في الشتاء

TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r7.claim: The indefinite “provision” signals unfamiliar food; if it were ordinary food, visitors to the mosque might have brought it, so Mary's answer would not rule out a human source.
TABATABAI:3:36-37#3/r7.anchor: إشعار بكونه رزقا غير معهود كما قيل إنه كان يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r2.speaker: أحدهما
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r2.claim: Another report says the child was vowed to serve worshippers; Mary served them until she grew up, when Zakariya was ordered to put a screen between her and the worshippers.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r2.anchor: وفيه عن أحدهما نذرت ما في بطنها للكنيسة أن يخدم العباد وليس الذكر كالأنثى في الخدمة

TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r5.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r5.claim: Al-Qummi's account says Mary lived behind a screen in the sanctuary and Zakariya found summer fruit with her in winter and winter fruit in summer; she said it came from God.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r5.anchor: وكان يدخل عليها زكريا المحراب فيجد عندها فاكهة الصيف في الشتاء وفاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r7.claim: Some commentators object that the reports about revelation to Imran, Mary's out-of-season fruit, and Zakariya's request for a sign lack support from scripture, the Prophet, reason, or reliable history.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#7/r7.anchor: بعض المفسرين شدد النكير على ما تضمنته هذه الروايات كالوحي إلى عمران ووجود الفاكهة في محراب مريم

TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i answers that the dismissal is unargued: although solitary reports with weak chains need not be accepted as proof, reflection on the verses makes the Ahl al-Bayt reports plausible and none is irrational.
TABATABAI:3:35-41#8/r1.anchor: وهو منه كلام من غير حجة والروايات وإن كانت آحادا غير خالية عن ضعف الطريق لا يجب على الباحث الأخذ بها

TABRISI:3:37/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37/r1.claim: Kufans read kaffalahā with a doubled fāʾ and others with a light fāʾ; the light form is supported by 3:44, where the guardianship is attributed to its subject.
TABRISI:3:37/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة كفلها بالتشديد والباقون بالتخفيف

TABRISI:3:37/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37/r2.claim: Kufans except Abū Bakr read the name in its shortened form; others lengthen it. Abū Bakr alone uses accusative with the long form; others use nominative.
TABRISI:3:37/r2.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر زكريا مقصورا والباقون بالمد

TABRISI:3:37/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:3:37/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the light reading through 3:44, where the guardianship verb is active and its subject is the one who takes Mary into care; doubling makes the Lord the subject and Zechariah the object.

TABRISI:3:37/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37/r4.claim: The name is read with shortening by Kūfans other than Abū Bakr and with lengthening by the other readers.
TABRISI:3:37/r4.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر زكريا مقصورا والباقون بالمد

TABRISI:3:37/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37/r5.claim: The verbal noun qabūl is used instead of taqabbul because the verb carries the sense of accepting, just as takarrum takes karam because it means being generous.
TABRISI:3:37/r5.anchor: إنما جاء مصدر تقبلها على القبول دون التقبل لأن فيه معنى قبلها

TABRISI:3:37/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:3:37/r6.claim: Abū ʿAmr says qabūl with fatḥa has no parallel among verbal nouns, whose normal pattern has ḍamma.
TABRISI:3:37/r6.anchor: ولا نظير لقبول في المصادر بفتح فاء الفعل

TABRISI:3:37/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r7.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:3:37/r7.claim: Sībawayh lists five verbal nouns on the open fuʿūl pattern: qabūl, wuḍūʾ, ẓuhūr, wulūgh, and waqūd, though waqūd is usually closed when it is a verbal noun.
TABRISI:3:37/r7.anchor: جاءت خمسة مصادر على فعول بالفتح قبول ووضوء وظهور

TABRISI:3:37/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r8.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:3:37/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj permits qabūl with ḍamma and explains qabīl as a guarantor or surety.
TABRISI:3:37/r8.anchor: وأجاز الزجاج في قبول الضم والقبيل الكفيل وهو الضامن

TABRISI:3:37/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37/r9.claim: Kafala forms include kafaltuhu, akfuluhu, kaflan, kufūlan, and kafālan; a kāfil undertakes someone’s expenses and care.
TABRISI:3:37/r9.anchor: يقال كفلته أكفله كفلا وكفولا وكفالا فأنا كافل إذا تكفلت مؤنته

TABRISI:3:37/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37/r10.claim: In legal terminology the one whose debt is guaranteed owes it, the beneficiary is owed it, the guaranteed thing is the debt, and the guarantor becomes liable.
TABRISI:3:37/r10.anchor: والمكفول عنه في الفقه هو الذي عليه الدين والمكفول له هو الذي له الدين

TABRISI:3:37/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37/r11.claim: A cited report calls the Prophet the best one to be cared for in childhood and raised until maturity.
TABRISI:3:37/r11.anchor: أحق من كفل في صغره وأرضع حتى نشأ

TABRISI:3:37/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37/r12.claim: Miḥrāb is the imam’s place in a mosque and originally the most honored, elevated place in an assembly; al-Zajjāj calls it a lofty, noble place.
TABRISI:3:37/r12.anchor: والمحراب مقام الإمام من المسجد وأصله أكرم موضع في المجلس وأشرفه

TABRISI:3:37/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37/r13.claim: A cited poem uses miḥrāb for a high place reached by a ladder.

TABRISI:3:37#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#2/r1.claim: God accepted Mary despite her being female, approving Ḥanna’s vow to dedicate her to service in the Jerusalem sanctuary, where no female had previously been accepted for this purpose.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r1.anchor: مع أنوثتها ورضي بها في النذر الذي نذرته حنة للعبادة في بيت المقدس ولم يقبل قبلها أنثى

TABRISI:3:37#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:3:37#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the acceptance as God taking charge of Mary’s upbringing and affairs.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه تكفل بها في تربيتها والقيام بشأنها عن الحسن

TABRISI:3:37#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#2/r3.claim: Another explanation says she never suffered illness at any time, day or night.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r3.anchor: وقبوله إياها أنه ما عرتها علة ساعة من ليل أو نهار

TABRISI:3:37#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:3:37#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the good acceptance as God setting her on the path of the blessed.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r4.anchor: وقيل معناه سلك بها طريق السعداء عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:3:37#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#2/r5.claim: God gave Mary good growth and a sound form.

TABRISI:3:37#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:3:37#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says she grew in one day as much as another person grows in a year.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r6.anchor: وقيل سوى خلقها فكانت تنبت في يوم ما ينبت غيرها في عام عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:3:37#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TABRISI:3:37#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God supplied her with nourishment until she became a fully grown woman.

TABRISI:3:37#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:3:37#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that at nine Mary fasted by day, prayed at night, and devoted herself to worship until she surpassed the scholars.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما بلغت تسع سنين صامت النهار وقامت الليل وتبتلت حتى غلبت الأحبار

TABRISI:3:37#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#2/r9.claim: With the doubled reading God assigns Mary to Zechariah, who becomes her guardian; with the light reading Zechariah takes her into his care and undertakes her affairs.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r9.anchor: بالتشديد معناه ضمها الله إلى زكريا وجعله كفيلها

TABRISI:3:37#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r10.speaker: ابن إسحاق وجماعة
TABRISI:3:37#2/r10.claim: Ibn Isḥāq and others say Mary’s mother brought her wrapped to the sanctuary; priests competed for her, and Zechariah claimed priority because her aunt was his wife. They decided to draw lots among twenty-nine men.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق وجماعة وقيل بل ثبت قلم زكريا

TABRISI:3:37#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r11.speaker: ابن إسحاق وجماعة
TABRISI:3:37#2/r11.claim: In Ibn Isḥāq’s account, the pens were cast into flowing water; Zechariah’s stood upright above the water while the others sank, so he won.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r11.anchor: فألقوا أقلامهم في الماء فارتز قلم زكريا وارتفع فوق الماء ورسبت أقلامهم

TABRISI:3:37#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r12.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:3:37#2/r12.claim: Al-Suddī gives another sign: Zechariah’s pen stood up as if in clay, while the others were swept along with the current.

TABRISI:3:37#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#2/r13.claim: Zechariah won the lot and was head of the priests and their prophet.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r13.anchor: فسهمهم زكريا وقرعهم وكان رأس الأحبار ونبيهم

TABRISI:3:37#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#2/r14.claim: The lot account concludes by identifying Zechariah as the one who took Mary into his care.

TABRISI:3:37#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#2/r15.claim: Miḥrāb also means a mosque; another proposed etymology links it to war because Satan is fought there.
TABRISI:3:37#2/r15.anchor: ويقال للمسجد أيضا محراب ومنه ما يشاء من محاريب أي مساجد

TABRISI:3:37#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#3/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TABRISI:3:37#3/r1.claim: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq says Zechariah first placed Mary with his wife, her maternal aunt; when Mary reached puberty, he built her a secluded upper room in the sanctuary, accessible only by a ladder, and brought her supplies daily.
TABRISI:3:37#3/r1.anchor: فقال محمد بن إسحاق ضمها إلى خالتها أم يحيى حتى إذا شبت وبلغت مبلغ النساء

TABRISI:3:37#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي
TABRISI:3:37#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī say Zechariah found fresh summer fruit with Mary in winter and winter fruit in summer.
TABRISI:3:37#3/r2.anchor: غضا طريا عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي

TABRISI:3:37#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:3:37#3/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Mary was never nursed and her provision came from Paradise.
TABRISI:3:37#3/r3.anchor: وقيل إنها لم ترضع قط وإنما كان يأتيها رزقها من الجنة عن الحسن

TABRISI:3:37#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#3/r4.claim: Zechariah asks in astonishment how and from where she obtained this provision.
TABRISI:3:37#3/r4.anchor: يعني قال لها زكريا كيف لك ومن أين لك هذا كالمتعجب منه

TABRISI:3:37#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#3/r5.claim: Mary says the provision is from God, that is, from Paradise; the extraordinary gift honors her.
TABRISI:3:37#3/r5.anchor: أي من الجنة وهذه تكرمة من الله تعالى لها وإن كان ذلك خارقا للعادة

TABRISI:3:37#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#3/r6.claim: The author holds that extraordinary signs may appear through people who are not prophets, including the saints.
TABRISI:3:37#3/r6.anchor: فإن عندنا يجوز أن تظهر الآيات الخارقة للعادة على غير الأنبياء والأصفياء

TABRISI:3:37#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#3/r7.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:3:37#3/r7.claim: Al-Balkhī, representing those Muʿtazilites who deny miracles for non-prophets, says the provision established Jesus’ prophethood.
TABRISI:3:37#3/r7.anchor: أحدهما: أن ذلك كان تأسيسا لنبوة عيسى عن البلخي

TABRISI:3:37#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#3/r8.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:3:37#3/r8.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the provision came through Zechariah’s prayer and was therefore his miracle.
TABRISI:3:37#3/r8.anchor: والآخر: أنه كان بدعاء زكريا لها بالرزق في الجملة وكانت معجزة له عن الجبائي

TABRISI:3:37#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:37#3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:37#3/r9.claim: If Mary’s statement continues through “without reckoning,” it means God gives freely without payment earned by works; alternatively, God’s statement begins anew.
TABRISI:3:37#3/r9.anchor: ووجه اتصالها بما تقدم أن يكون حكاية لقول مريم وعلى هذا يكون معنى قوله بغير حساب

THALABI:v3p56/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p56/r1.claim: God accepted Mary from Hanna and approved her in place of the consecrated boy; the verb can mean to accept what one approves. Some instead understand the acceptance as undertaking her care.
THALABI:v3p56/r1.anchor: فتقبلها: أي تقبل الله من حنة مريم ورضيها مكان المحرر

THALABI:v3p56/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو الكسائي والأئمة
THALABI:v3p56/r2.claim: They explain قبول as the verbal noun with fatḥa, an exceptional form whose expected pattern would have ḍamma, like دخول and خروج.
THALABI:v3p56/r2.anchor: والقياس الضم مثل الدخول والخروج، قاله أبو عمرو الكسائي والأئمة

THALABI:v3p56/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r3.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v3p56/r3.claim: Some say God’s acceptance meant that He undertook Mary’s upbringing and care.
THALABI:v3p56/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: معنى التقبل: التكفل في التربية والقيام بشأنها

THALABI:v3p56/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v3p56/r4.claim: Hasan says God accepted Mary by never punishing her at any time, day or night.
THALABI:v3p56/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: قبوله إياها أنه ما عذبها ساعة من نهار ولا ليل

THALABI:v3p56/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p56/r5.claim: The wording بقبول حسن uses a verbal noun of a different form from the verb; al-Farra compares it to تكلمت كلاما, with poetry offered as parallel usage.
THALABI:v3p56/r5.anchor: وهذا النوع يقال له: المصدر على غير المصدر

THALABI:v3p56/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p56/r6.claim: The phrase continues the verbal-noun pattern with نباتا after أنبتها.
THALABI:v3p56/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: مثل قولك تكلمت كلاما.

THALABI:v3p56/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p56/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says God guided Mary among the blessed and formed her without excess or defect; she grew in a day as much as an ordinary child grows in a year.
THALABI:v3p56/r7.anchor: جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس: فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن يقول

THALABI:v3p56/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
THALABI:v3p56/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God nourished and provided for Mary until she matured into a full adult woman.
THALABI:v3p56/r8.anchor: ابن جريج: أنبتها ربها في غذائه ورزقه نباتا حسنا

THALABI:v3p56/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r9.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v3p56/r9.claim: The commentators say Hanna carried newborn Mary to the sanctuary and presented her to the priests, who contested guardianship because she was the daughter of their imam and keeper of offerings; they agreed to draw lots, and twenty-nine men went to a flowing river.
THALABI:v3p56/r9.anchor: قال المفسرون: أخذتها أم مريم حين ولدتها

THALABI:v3p56/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r10.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v3p56/r10.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the river where they cast lots as the Jordan.
THALABI:v3p56/r10.anchor: قال السدي: هو نهر الأردن، فألقوا أقلامهم في الماء

THALABI:v3p56/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r11.speaker: ابن إسحاق وجماعة
THALABI:v3p56/r11.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others say Zakariyya’s pen rose above the water while the others sank.
THALABI:v3p56/r11.anchor: فارتفع قلم زكريا فوق الماء وانحدرت أقلامهم [ورسبت] في النهر، قاله ابن إسحاق وجماعة

THALABI:v3p56/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r12.speaker: السدي وجماعة
THALABI:v3p56/r12.claim: An alternative account says Zakariyya’s pen stood upright as if fixed in clay while the others flowed away with the water, so he won the lot.
THALABI:v3p56/r12.anchor: وقال السدي وجماعة: بل ثبت قلم زكريا وقام فوق الماء كأنه في طين

THALABI:v3p56/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p56/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p56/r13.claim: Zakariyya, their chief priest and prophet, took Mary into his household and assumed her care.
THALABI:v3p56/r13.anchor: وكان رأس الأحبار ونبيهم فذلك قوله تعالى: وكفلها زكريا

THALABI:v3p57/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p57/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
THALABI:v3p57/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Zakariyya placed Mary with her maternal aunt, Yahya’s mother, arranged a wet nurse, then built her a chamber in the mosque with a high entrance accessible only by a ladder; he brought her food, drink, and oil daily.
THALABI:v3p57/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: فلما كفلها زكريا ضمها إلى خالتها أم يحيى

THALABI:v3p57/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p57/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p57/r2.claim: The provision was fruit out of season: summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer, fresh and ripe.
THALABI:v3p57/r2.anchor: كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا: يعني وجد زكريا عندها فاكهة

THALABI:v3p57/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p57/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p57/r3.claim: When Mary was asked about the provision God gave her, she answered that it came from God, who provides without measure.
THALABI:v3p57/r3.anchor: فإنها كانت إذا رزقها الله شيئا وسألت عنه قالت هو من عند الله

THALABI:v3p57/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p57/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
THALABI:v3p57/r4.claim: Jabir reports that, after days without food, the Prophet visited Fatima; she had none, but a neighbor later sent bread and meat. Fatima saved it for him despite her family’s hunger, and the covered dish was miraculously full; she used Mary’s words, and the Prophet praised her resemblance to the leader of Israelite women.
THALABI:v3p57/r4.anchor: أخبرنا عبد الله بن حامد بإسناده عن جابر بن عبد الله: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقام أياما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r1.claim: Taqabbala and qabula both mean to approve and accept; qabūl is used because it shares the meaning of taqabbul.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r1.anchor: التقبل، والقبول، معناهما سواء، وهو: أن ترضى بالشيء، وتأخذه؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r2.claim: Al-Farra says Arabic can replace a verb's own verbal noun with another verbal noun of the same meaning despite differences in form, as in تكلمت كلاما; this is a verbal noun other than the expected one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r2.anchor: قال الفراء (¬2): والعرب قد تترك المصدر للفعل المذكور، وتأتي بمصدر آخر في معنى الأول،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r3.claim: Abu Amr says this is the only verbal noun on faʿūl with a fatḥa and that he had not heard it with ḍamma.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r3.anchor: قال أبو عمرو بن العلاء (¬3): وليس في المصادر (فعول) بفتح الفاء،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r4.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r4.claim: Sibawayh lists five verbal nouns on faʿūl: qabūl, wuḍūʾ, ṭahūr, walūʿ, and waqūd, though waqūd is more often with ḍamma as a verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r4.anchor: قال سيبويه (¬1): خمسة (¬2) مصادر، جاءت على (فعول): (قبول)، و (وضوء) (¬3)، و (طهور)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r5.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r5.claim: Al-Farra and Al-Zajjaj allow qabūl to be pronounced with ḍamma.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r6.speaker: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r6.claim: Thaʿlab, citing Ibn al-Aʿrabi, gives both pronunciations qabūlan and qabūlan and says the phrase على وجهه قبول is the only other usage; a poem witnesses the expression.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r6.anchor: ثعلب، عن ابن الأعرابي (¬8): يقال: قبلته (قبولا)، و (قبولا) (¬9)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r7.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r7.claim: The exegetes say God accepted Mary in place of the consecrated male child Hanne had vowed, since no female had previously been accepted for that role.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r7.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬4): معنى قوله: {فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن} أي: رضيها مكان المحرر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Al-Dahhak's narration, explains the acceptance as setting Mary on the path of the blessed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك: معناه: سلك بها طريق السعداء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj says نباتا has a different form from أنبت but conveys that she grew well.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬1): جاء لفظ (¬2) {نباتا} على غير لفظ (أنبت)، على معنى: نبتت نباتا حسنا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the causative verb carries the sense of her growing herself; he supports meaning-based syntax with Imru al-Qays' line where رضت conveys أذللت.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p198/r10.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري (¬3): لما كان (أنبت) يدل على [نبتت] (¬4) حمل (¬5) الفعل على المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, explains Mary's good growth as righteousness, knowledge of God, obedience, and service in the mosque.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء (¬4)، في قوله: {وأنبتها نباتا حسنا}؛ يريد: في صلاح ومعرفة بالله،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Al-Dahhak, says she developed with balanced form, neither excess nor deficiency, growing in a day what a child grows in a year.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r2.anchor: وقال في رواية الضحاك (¬5): يعنى: سوى خلقها من غير زيادة، ولا نقصان،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r3.claim: God placed Mary in Zakariyya's care, and he assumed responsibility for her.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r3.anchor: أي: ضمها (¬1) إلى نفسه وقام بأمرها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses the construction as undertaking her care; a kāfil is someone who takes a person in, supports, and pays for their maintenance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬2): ومعناه في هذا: ضمن القيام بأمرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r5.claim: Zakariyya is nominative because the verb of assigning care is ascribed to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r5.anchor: و {زكريا}، رفع بفعله (¬7)، لأن الكفالة نسبت إليه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r6.claim: Zakariyya has shortened and lengthened forms; both are indeclinable because they end in the feminine alif, whose fixed presence functions like two declension-blocking causes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r6.anchor: وفيه قراءتان: القصر، والمد، وهما لغتان فيه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r7.claim: Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read with a doubled fāʾ, making Zakariyya accusative as the second object; the sense is that God entrusted her to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (وكفلها) مشددا، ومصدره: التكفيل، والتكفلة (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r8.claim: After Mary was born, Hanne brought her to the Temple custodians as her vowed offering; the priests competed for her, cast lots, and the lot fell to Zakariyya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p202/r8.anchor: وذلك أن (حنة) لما ولدت مريم، أتت بها سدنة بيت المقدس،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r1.claim: The exegetes say Zakariyya built Mary a chamber in the mosque with a high entrance reached only by a ladder, and no one besides him ascended to it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬1): لما ضم زكريا مريم إلى نفسه، بنى لها محرابا في المسجد، وبابه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r2.claim: Miḥrāb can mean the most honored assembly; Israelite miḥrābs were their places of worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r2.anchor: و (المحراب) في اللغة: أشرف المجالس. وكانت محاريب بني إسرائيل مساجدهم (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r3.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r3.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says miḥrāb means a chamber, citing the verse about people scaling the miḥrāb in 38:21; Umar ibn Abi Rabiʿa's poem uses it likewise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r3.anchor: وقال الأصمعي (¬1): (المحراب): الغرفة؛ ألا تراه يقول: {إذ تسوروا المحراب} [سورة ص: 21].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines miḥrāb as the highest room in a house or place in a mosque and says it means a chamber here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬2): (المحراب): أرفع بيت في الدار، وأرفع مكان في المسجد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda says miḥrāb is the leading, most honored assembly; a mosque's qibla and a palace are called miḥrāb because each is its foremost place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة (¬4): (المحراب) عند العرب سيد المجالس، ومقدمها، وأشرفها،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r6.speaker: امرؤ القيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r6.claim: Imru al-Qays uses the plural miḥārīb to mean palaces.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r6.anchor: قال امرؤ (¬6) القيس: كغزلان وحش في محاريب أقوال (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says Mary had a chamber where she climbed to pray night and day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p206/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء (¬2): صارت عنده لها غرفة تصعد إليها تصلي فيها الليل والنهار.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Al-Rabiʿ say Mary found winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter, brought by angels from Paradise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r1.anchor: قال (¬3) ابن عباس (¬4)، والربيع (¬5): كان زكريا كلما دخل عليها غرفتها وجد عندها رزقا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq says this provision occurred after Mary had reached adulthood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r2.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق (¬1): كان هذا كله، بعد أن بلغت مريم مبلغ النساء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says it happened in Mary's infancy: she never nursed, received food from Paradise, and spoke as a child when answering Zakariyya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن (¬2): كان هذا في صغرها، ولم ترضع ثديا قط، بل (¬3) كان يأتيها رزقها من الجنة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq makes كلما accusative through وجد; ما with دخل acts like the verbal noun, meaning every time of entering the chamber.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬5): ونصب {كلما} بقوله: {وجد} (¬6)؛ أي: يجد عندها الرزق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses this as Where did this come from? Zakariyya asked to ensure the provision came from God rather than another person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p208/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1): يريد: من أين لك هذا؟ وإنما سألها؛ لأنه خاف أن يأتيها الرزق من غير جهته،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p210/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p210/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p210/r1.claim: The closing statement may be Mary's continuation or a new sentence; the author prefers a new sentence because it does not answer Zakariyya's question.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p210/r1.anchor: وهذا يحتمل أن يكون من كلام مريم، ويحتمل أنه على (¬5) الابتداء، والأولى به الاستئناف (¬6)

QASHANI:3:35-37/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:35-37/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:35-37/r2.claim: Parents' intentions and dispositions affect a child as food affects the body: lawful food, luminous dispositions, and sincere intentions yield a believer, truthful person, saint, or prophet; forbidden food and corrupt dispositions yield a wicked or unbelieving child, since the embryo develops from that food and is nurtured by that soul.
QASHANI:3:35-37/r2.anchor: النيات وهيئات النفس مؤثرة في نفس الولد، كما أن الأغذية مؤثرة في بدنه

QASHANI:3:35-37/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:35-37/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:3:35-37/r3.claim: The Prophet says, The child is the secret of his father; Qashani connects this to Mary's truthfulness and Jesus' blessed filial descent from her truthful father.
QASHANI:3:35-37/r3.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QASHANI:3:35-37/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:35-37/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:35-37/r4.claim: Mary's provision may be spiritual knowledge, realities, and wisdom flowing from God; the wording that it was with her indicates divinely bestowed, ladunni provision.
QASHANI:3:35-37/r4.anchor: الرزق الروحاني من المعارف والحقائق والعلوم والحكم الفائضة عليها من عند الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r1.claim: God accepted Mary in place of the male temple servant her mother had vowed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r1.anchor: { فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن } أي: رضيها مكان المحرر الذي نذرته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r2.claim: God raised her in righteousness, chastity, knowledge of God, and obedience.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r2.anchor: { وأنبتها نباتا حسنا } في صلاح وعفة ومعرفة بالله وطاعة له

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r3.claim: Zachariah undertook her care and built her a sanctuary chamber accessible only by a ladder.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r3.anchor: { وكفلها زكريا } ضمن القيام بأمرها، فبنى لها محرابا في المسجد لا يرتقى إليه إلا بسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r4.claim: The mihrab here means a room.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r4.anchor: والمحراب: الغرفة، وهو قوله: { كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r5.claim: Mary had winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter, brought by angels from Paradise; seeing this extraordinary provision gave Zachariah hope for a child despite his barren wife.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r5.anchor: { كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا } أي: فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف، وفاكهة الصيف في الشتاء تأتيها به الملائكة من الجنة،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r6.claim: Seeing her extraordinary seasonal fruit gave Zachariah hope for a child from his barren wife by extraordinary means.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:37/r6.anchor: على خلاف مجرى العادة طمع في رزق الولد من العاقر على خلاف العادة

ELMALILI:3:35-37/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r2.claim: A report names Jesus’ maternal grandmother, Imran’s wife, as Hanne bint Fakuza; Hanne’s sister—or, in another report, Maryam’s sister—was Iysha, wife of Zakariya and mother of Yahya. The Prophet is reported to call Yahya and Jesus cousins, sons of maternal aunts.
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r2.anchor: Rivayet olunuyor ki Hazret-i Îsâ’nın ninesi zevce-i İmrân’ın ismi “Hanne binti Fâkuza”

ELMALILI:3:35-37/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r4.claim: Mihrab normally means the mosque’s front place where the imam stands; by part-for-whole usage it can mean the mosque, and it can also name its most honored, foremost place.
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r4.anchor: mescidlerin ön tarafında imamın duracağı mevki‘-i mahsustur. Zikr-i cüz, irâde-i kül tarîkiyle mescide

ELMALILI:3:35-37/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r5.claim: Here Elmalılı takes mihrab to mean a raised chamber in the mosque, reached by stairs, where Zakariya placed Maryam and kept her under his care.
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r5.anchor: burada “mihrab”dan murad, mescidde merdivenle çıkılır bir mahfil olduğu beyan ediliyor ki Hazret-i Meryem

ELMALILI:3:35-37/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r6.claim: Maryam, orphaned from her father while still in the womb, was born with a sacred spiritual nature and received special divine nurture in the mihrab.
ELMALILI:3:35-37/r6.anchor: rahm-i mâderde babasından yetim kalan Hazret-i Meryem böyle kudsî bir rûhâniyetle doğmuş ve böyle bir mihrabda min ‘indillah mazhariyyet-i mahsûsa ile perverişyâb olmuştu.

QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r6.claim: God's acceptance brought Mary beyond what her mother had hoped for.
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r6.anchor: حيث بلغها فوق ما تمنت أمها

QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r7.claim: God singled Mary out for worship and cared for her as He cares for His friends, astonishing her contemporaries despite her being a girl.
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r7.anchor: ويقال تقبلها بقبول حسن حتى أفردها لطاعته ، وتولاها بما تولى به أولياءه

QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r8.claim: God accepted and nurtured her despite knowing that enemies would make ugly claims about Him because of her; He did not heed their blame.
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r8.anchor: ويقال القبول الحسن حسن تربيته لها مع علمه - سبحانه - بأنه يقال فيه بسببها ما يقال

QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r9.claim: Poetry portrays blame as sweet when it comes from love of the beloved's mention.
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r9.anchor: أجد الملامة في هواك لذيذة . . . حبا لذكرك فليلمني اللوم

QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r10.claim: Her good acceptance included protected upbringing, reflected in her seeking refuge in the Merciful from a visitor if he feared God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r10.anchor: ويقال القبول الحسن أن رباها على نعت العصمة حتى كانت تقول : { إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا }

QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r11.claim: Her good growth was steadfast obedience and preference for God's pleasure at all times, culminating in Jesus as her fruit.
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r11.anchor: حتى استقامت على الطاعة ، وآثرت رضاه - سبحانه - في جميع الأوقات

QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r12.claim: Part of her acceptance and growth was that God appointed the prophet Zechariah to care for and protect her.
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r12.anchor: ومن القبول الحسن والنبات الحسن أن جعل كافلها والقيم بأمرها وحفظها نبيا

QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r13.speaker: الله
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r13.claim: God revealed to David: if you see someone seeking Me, become that person's servant.
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r13.anchor: وقد أوحى الله إلى داود عليه السلام : إن رأيت لي طالبا فكن له خادما

QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r14.claim: A sign of Mary's acceptance was that she was found in the prayer niche; one whose home and place of worship is the niche is a cherished servant.
QUSHAYRI:v1p144/r14.anchor: من إمارات القبول الحسن أنها لم تكن توجد إلا في المحراب ، ومن كان مسكنه وموضعه الذي يتعبد فيه

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r1.claim: God did not leave all Mary's care to Zechariah: her food appeared so servants know He does not shift a saint's entire burden onto others.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r1.anchor: من القبول الحسن أنه لم يطرح أمرها كله وشغلها على زكريا عليه السلام

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r2.claim: Serving a friend of God is itself a source of ease through that friend's blessing, not a hardship imposed because of the friend.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r2.anchor: ومن خدم وليا من أوليائه كان هو في رفق الولي لا إنه تكون عليه مشقة لأجل الأولياء

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r3.claim: Those who serve the poor should recognize that they themselves receive ease through the poor.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r3.anchor: وفي هذا إشارة لمن يخدم الفقراء أن يعلم أنه في رفق الفقراء

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r4.claim: Zechariah asked not because he thought Mary unworthy, but because he feared another might surpass him in caring for her.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r4.anchor: لأنه لم يكن يعتقد فيها استحقاق تلك المنزلة ، وكان يخاف أن غيره يغلبه وينتهز فرصة تعهدها

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r5.claim: Mary's answer that the provision came from God, not a creature, gave Zechariah two comforts: witnessing her rank and knowing no one had preceded him in her care.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r5.anchor: وكانت مريم تقول : هو من عند الله لا من عند مخلوق

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r6.claim: “Whenever” signals repetition: Zechariah checked on Mary every day and at every time.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r6.anchor: فلفظة كلما للتكرار وفي هذا إشارة : وهو أن زكريا عليه السلام لم يذر تعهدها - وإن وجد عندها رزقا - بل كل يوم

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r7.claim: Zechariah continued checking despite finding provision because a saint's marvels are not necessarily continuous.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r7.anchor: لأن كرامات الأولياء ليست مما يجب أن يدوم ذلك قطعا ؛ فيجوز أن يظهر الله ذلك عليهم دائما ، ويجوز ألا يظهر

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r8.claim: A miracle seen today may not appear tomorrow; God is not obliged to make a saint's marvels permanent.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r8.anchor: فما كان زكريا عليه السلام يعتمد على ذلك فيترك تفقد حالها ، ثم كان يجدد السؤال عنها بقوله

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r9.claim: No provision is owed by God: today's gift may not arrive as yesterday's did, since nothing is obligatory upon Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r9.anchor: لجواز أن يكون الذي هو اليوم لا على الوجه الذي كان بالأمس ، فإنه لا واجب على الله سبحانه

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r10.claim: The verse clarifies pure unity: God's provision follows His will and is not caused by people's obedience or worship.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r10.anchor: وقوله : { إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب } إيضاح عن عين التوحيد

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r11.claim: Seeing God's grace toward Mary increased Zechariah's certainty and hope, leading him to ask for a son despite old age; the answer overturned custom.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r11.anchor: أي لما رأى كرامة الله سبحانه معها ازداد يقينا على يقين ، ورجاء على رجاء ؛ فسأل الولد على كبر سنه

QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r13.claim: Zechariah saw summer fruit with Mary in winter and winter fruit in summer, then asked for a son in old age as a sign.
QUSHAYRI:v1p145/r13.anchor: وكان زكريا عليه السلام يرى الفاكهة الصيفية عند مريم في الشتاء ، وفاكهة الشتاء عندها في الصيف

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r1.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r1.claim: One interpretation of God’s gracious acceptance is that He accepted the prayer for Mary to be under His protection and safe from Satan.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r1.anchor: Allah, Meryem’in kendi himayesine bırakılması ve şeytanın şerrinden korunması hakkındaki duayı kabul buyurdu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r2.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r2.claim: A second interpretation is that God accepted the unusual vow to dedicate a girl to temple service.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r2.anchor: alışılagelmiş uygulama dışında kalan bir adağı, yani bir kız çocuğunun mâbed hizmetine verilmesini kabul etti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r3.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r3.claim: A third interpretation is that God arranged the rabbis’ contest for Mary’s care and ultimately entrusted her to Zechariah, as detailed in 3:44.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r3.anchor: Meryem’in bakımı için –44. âyette açıklanacağı üzere– hahamların birbirleriyle yarışmalarını sağladı ve sonunda bu görevi Hz. Zekeriyyâ’ya verdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r4.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r4.claim: Some commentators take the phrase literally as God raising her like a beautiful plant and, drawing on reports, explain it through extraordinary features of Mary’s biological development.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r4.anchor: “Onu güzel bir bitki gibi yetiştirdi” şeklinde mânalandıran ve bunu bazı rivayetlerden hareketle Meryem’in biyolojik gelişimindeki olağan üstü durumlarla açıklayan müfessirler vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r5.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r5.claim: Some commentators explain the phrase as God making Mary the mother of a great prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r5.anchor: Bazı müfessirler ise bu cümleyi “onu büyük bir peygambere anne kılmak suretiyle” diye açıklamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r6.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r6.claim: Zamakhsharī reads the expression metaphorically: Mary was raised in a healthy educational environment and endowed with moral virtues.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r6.anchor: mecazi bir ifade olduğu görüşüyle (bk. Zemahşerî, I, 187)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r7.speaker: Reşîd Rızâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r7.claim: Rashīd Riḍā explains the upbringing as attentive care in a good environment for education and sustenance, promoting both bodily and spiritual well-being.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r7.anchor: yani hem ruh hem beden sağlığı bakımından özenle yetiştirildiği yorumu (bk. Reşîd Rızâ, III, 292)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r8.claim: The author prefers the figurative, sound-upbringing account over extraordinary biological development or the claim that the phrase only means making Mary the mother of a prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r8.anchor: gerek eğitimi gerekse rızkının temini açısından iyi bir ortamda büyüdüğü, yani hem ruh

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r9.speaker: rivayet
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r9.claim: A report says Zechariah was married to Mary’s maternal aunt; the following verse and 3:44 discuss Zechariah and his guardianship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r9.anchor: Hz. Zekeriyyâ’nın Hz. Meryem’in teyzesinin kocası olduğu rivayet edilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r10.claim: Mihrab can mean the front or raised section of an assembly, or a special elevated room for worship and prayer, usually reached by stairs; in Islamic usage it also names the imam’s place at the front of a mosque.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r10.anchor: Toplantı mahallinin ön kısmına veya yüksekçe yapılmış özel bölümüne, ibadet ve dua için kapanılan ve genellikle merdivenle çıkılan özel mekâna “mihrap” denir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r11.claim: Given Qur’anic usage and historical information, the mihrab here is a special elevated room at Bayt al-Maqdis.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r11.anchor: Kelimenin Kur’an-ı Kerîm’deki kullanımları (Âl-i İmrân 3/37, 39; Meryem 19/11; Sâd 38/21) ve konuya ilişkin tarihi bilgiler göz önüne alındığında

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r12.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r12.claim: Some commentators cite reports that Mary refused breast milk, was sustained by divine gifts, and spoke in the cradle like Jesus; they infer that she stayed in the temple from infancy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r12.anchor: “Meryem’in meme kabul etmeyip ilâhî ikramlarla beslendiği ve Hz. Îsâ gibi beşikteyken konuştuğu” şeklindeki bazı rivayetlerle destekleyerek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r13.speaker: karşı görüşte olan müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r13.claim: Other commentators infer from the verse that Mary was brought to the temple after she reached the age of speech, rather than as an infant.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r13.anchor: karşı görüşte olanlar ise âyetten Meryem’in konuşma çağına eriştikten sonra mâbede verildiğinin anlaşıldığını ileri sürmüşler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r14.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r14.claim: Some commentators take the passage and reports of Zechariah finding out-of-season fruit as evidence of a miracle-like wonder for Mary, and regard the verse as proof that saintly wonders are real.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r14.anchor: Hz. Zekeriyyâ’nın Meryem’in yanında o mevsimde yetişmeyen meyveler gördüğü yönündeki rivayetleri dikkate alan müfessirler bunu Hz. Meryem açısından bir keramet olarak değerlendirmişler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r15.speaker: bazı bilginler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r15.claim: Some scholars accept that the passage indicates an extraordinary event but explain it as a miracle belonging to Zechariah or Jesus, not Mary.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r15.anchor: bunu Hz. Zekeriyyâ’ya veya Hz. Îsâ’ya nisbetle bir mûcize şeklinde açıklamaya çalışan bilginler de mevcuttur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r16.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r16.claim: Other commentators see no extraordinary event: God provided Mary’s food through believers who wished to honor devotees of worship, and Zechariah asked its source to check that it came by an acceptable means.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r16.anchor: yüce Allah’ın Meryem’e kendini zühd ve ibadete vermiş kişilere ikramda bulunmak isteyen müminler vasıtasıyla rızık lutfettiği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r17.speaker: M. Reşîd Rızâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r17.claim: Rashīd Riḍā rejects interpretation based on information not established in Qur’an, hadith, or history; he says famine could explain Zechariah’s question, so no extraordinary event need be assumed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r17.anchor: Kur’an’da ve hadislerde açıklanmayan, tarihen de sabit olmayan bilgilerden hareketle Kur’an’a anlam verilmemesi gerektiğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r18.speaker: M. Reşîd Rızâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r18.claim: Rashīd Riḍā says the episode strengthens monotheism and shows that prophetic selection and religious development rest on God’s will; the accepted dedication of a girl prepares Mary to mother a great prophet, rebutting Jewish ethnic exclusivism and pagan objections to Muhammad as human.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r18.anchor: tevhid (Allah’tan başka tanrı olmadığı) inancını pekiştirmeyi hedefleyen sûrenin bu bölümünde peygamberlerin seçimi ve dinlerin tekâmülü konusunun da Allah’ın mutlak iradesine bağlı olduğuna dikkat çekilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r19.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r19.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr sees women’s admission to temple service and Mary’s divinely directed guardianship by Zechariah as signaling a prophet who would change many Torah rulings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r19.anchor: mâbed hizmetine kadınların kabul edilmemesi âdetinin dışına çıkılmasını ve ilâhî bildirimle Meryem’in Hz. Zekeriyyâ’nın himayesine verilmesini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r20.speaker: Zemahşerî, Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r20.claim: The final clause can be read either as Mary continuing to speak or as God’s speech.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:37/r20.anchor: Âyetin sonundaki cümleyi Meryem’in konuşmasının devamı olarak veya Allah’ın sözü olarak anlamak mümkündür (Zemahşerî, I, 187; Râzî, VIII, 32).

BAQILLANI:v1p175/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r1.claim: Other poets’ comparisons of the Pleiades equal or surpass the celebrated example, showing that this kind of poetic invention is common rather than unique.
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r1.anchor: وفي جملة ما نقلناه ما يزيد على تشبيهه في الحسن أو يساويه أو يقاربه

BAQILLANI:v1p175/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
