BAQILLANI:v1p175/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r2.claim: The word “appeared” is unnecessary in the Pleiades simile: the comparison works whether the constellation is high, rising, or setting.
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r2.anchor: فقوله تعرضت من الكلام الذي يستغني عنه لأنه يشبه أثناء الوشاح بالثريا

BAQILLANI:v1p175/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r3.claim: The sash image is confused: the poet treats the Pleiades as one piece of a sash, then describes its plural middle sections; he meant a single piece.
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r3.anchor: وفيه أن الثريا كقطعة من الوشاح المفصل فلا معنى تعرض لقوله أثناء الوشاح

BAQILLANI:v1p175/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r4.claim: The poem’s sequence is poorly ordered: it mentions the encounter’s pleasure, timing, and guards before describing the woman’s state at his arrival; “by the curtain” is filler.
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r4.anchor: انظر إلى البيت الثاني الأول والأبيات التي قبله كيف خلط في النظم وفرط في التأليف

BAQILLANI:v1p175/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī explains “what recourse do you have?” to mean that the lover has no way to approach while people are around her.
BAQILLANI:v1p175/r5.anchor: وأما البيت الثاني ففيه تعليق واختلال ذكر الأصمعي أن معنى قوله ما لك حيلة

BURHAN:v2p398/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p398/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p398/r4.claim: Zarkashi asks why a verbal noun or its pronoun is stated explicitly when the preceding verb already implies it, as in these three verses.
BURHAN:v2p398/r4.anchor: ما الحكمة في التصريح بالمصدر فيهما أو بضميره

BURHAN:v2p484/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p484/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p484/r5.claim: The first reason to repeat an explicit noun instead of using a pronoun is to magnify or honor it; examples include repeated mention of God, the Quran's dawn recitation, and Zechariah.
BURHAN:v2p484/r5.anchor: وللخروج على خلاف الآصل أسباب أحدها قصد التعظيم

BURHAN:v1p415/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p415/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p415/r8.claim: Imran's wife alone remained inwardly and outwardly joined to her husband; God gave her good offspring, honored her, and favored her.
BURHAN:v1p415/r8.anchor: وواحدة خاصة واصلت بعلها باطنا وظاهرا وهى امرأت عمران فجعل الله لها ذرية طيبة

BURHAN:v2p145/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p145/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p145/r2.claim: The world is an example of the afterlife; whoever understands God's purpose in it gives the mind and thought relief.
BURHAN:v2p145/r2.anchor: وكذلك ما خلق الله الدنيا إلى مثالا للآخرة فمن فقه عن ربه عز وجل مراده منها فقد أراح نفسه

BURHAN:v2p145/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p145/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v2p145/r3.claim: Ibn Fāris groups expressions' meanings into maʿnā, tafsīr, and taʾwīl, whose purposes are close despite their differences.
BURHAN:v2p145/r3.anchor: قال ابن فارس معاني العبارات التى يعتبر بها عن الأشياء ترجع إلى ثلاثة المعنى والتفسير والتأويل

BURHAN:v2p145/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p145/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p145/r4.claim: Maʿnā is a word's intended purpose, from ʿanā meaning to intend; the author also relates it to bringing something to light.
BURHAN:v2p145/r4.anchor: فأما المعنى فهو القصد والمراد يقال عنيت بهذا الكلام كذا أي قصدت وعمدت

BURHAN:v2p145/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p145/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p145/r5.claim: An alternative etymology derives maʿnā from the earth producing good growth.
BURHAN:v2p145/r5.anchor: وقيل مشتق من قولهم عنت الأرض بنبات حسن إذا انبتت نباتا حسنا

BURHAN:v2p145/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p145/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p145/r6.claim: أصحاب المعاني means authors of Qur'anic meaning books; al-Wāḥidī names al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj, and Ibn al-Anbārī as leading authorities.
BURHAN:v2p145/r6.anchor: أكبر أهل المعانى الفراء والزجاج وابن الأنبارى قالوا كذا كذا

BURHAN:v2p145/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p145/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p145/r7.claim: In later usage, أهل المعاني refers to authors of the distinct discipline called al-maʿānī.
BURHAN:v2p145/r7.anchor: وحيث أطلق المتأخرون أهل المعاني فمرادهم بهم مصنفو العلم المشهور

BURHAN:v2p145/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p145/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p145/r8.claim: Tafsīr means disclosure, from the water sample physicians examine to uncover illness; similarly an exegete reveals a verse's subject, story, meaning, and occasion.
BURHAN:v2p145/r8.anchor: وأما التفسير فى اللغة فهو راجع إلى معنى الإظهار والكشف وأصله فى اللغة من التفسرة وهي القليل من الماء

BURHAN:v2p145/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p145/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p145/r9.claim: Tafsīr may be a verbal noun on tafʿila, also found in tajriba and takrima.
BURHAN:v2p145/r9.anchor: وكأنه تسمية بالمصدر لأن مصدر فعل جاء أيضا على تفعلة نحو جرب تجربة وكرم تكرمة

BURHAN:v4p249/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p249/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v4p249/r4.claim: Ibn Faris says the better interpretation here is how; Ibn Qutaybah says how and from where are close in meaning.
BURHAN:v4p249/r4.anchor: قال ابن فارس والاجود إن يقال في هذا أيضا كيف

BURHAN:v4p249/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p249/r7.speaker: ابن الدهان
BURHAN:v4p249/r7.claim: Ibn al-Dahhan says أنى conveys more than أين: it means from where, as reflected in the answer هو من عند الله rather than هو عند الله.
BURHAN:v4p249/r7.anchor: وقال ابن الدهان فيها معنى يزيد على أين لأنه لو قال أين لك هذا كان يقصر عن معنى أنى لك

SULAMI:v1p98#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r6.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r6.claim: Ja'far says God accepted Mary so greatly that even prophets of high rank would marvel at her standing; Zechariah's question and her reply point to the One who accepted her.
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r6.anchor: قال جعفر : تقبلها حتى تعجب الأنبياء مع علو أقدارهم

SULAMI:v1p98#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r7.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r7.claim: Al-Wasiti distinguishes outward and inward: in religious law God attributes goodness to Mary, while in reality He protects and nurtures her Himself.
SULAMI:v1p98#2/r7.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : بقبول حسن : محفوظة

SULAMI:v1p99#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p99#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p99#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ata says God grants a servant an elevated spiritual state only through obedience, sincere worship, and remaining in the prayer niche.
SULAMI:v1p99#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ما فتح الله تعالى على عبد من عبيده حالة سنية إلا باتباع الأوامر

SULAMI:v1p99#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p99#2/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p99#2/r3.claim: Abu Uthman calls the prayer niche a doorway to every good, a place where supplication is answered, and a path to intimacy; neglecting it closes the door.
SULAMI:v1p99#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : المحراب باب كل بر وموضع الإجابة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r1.claim: Jurjānī opens with poetic examples of subtle circumstantial phrasing and calls the second example especially fine.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r1.anchor: يمشون قد كسروا الجفون إلى الوغى متبسمين وفيهم استبشار

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r2.claim: Circumstantial clauses most commonly take waw, including clauses with ليس, as in “he came with no garment” or “he had no companion.”
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r2.anchor: ومما يجيء بالواو في الأكثر الأشيع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r3.claim: A Bedouin poem shows that a circumstantial clause with ليس can also omit waw gracefully.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r4.claim: The particle كأنما allows a circumstantial clause without waw; without that particle, the clause would need waw and lose its distinctive effect.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r4.anchor: قوله : ' كأنما بني ' إلى آخره في موضع الحال من غير شبهة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r5.claim: A second circumstantial clause can follow a singular state such as سالما; removing that preceding state makes Ibn al-Rūmī’s construction fail.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r5.anchor: والله يبقيك لنا سالما برداك تبجيل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r6.claim: Differences in using waw with circumstantial clauses have causes, not arbitrary variation; Jurjānī will explain them through a principle about the predicate.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p167/r6.anchor: فلا بد من أن يكون ذلك إنما كان من أجل علل توجبه وأسباب تقتضيه

TUSTARI:3:37/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:37/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:37/r1.claim: God accepted Mary, for the Highest King is more entitled to one freed from the bondage of ego and worldly life.
TUSTARI:3:37/r1.anchor: وقال: الملك الأعلى أولى بالمحرر عن رق النفس ورق الدنيا

TUSTARI:3:37/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:37/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:37/r2.claim: Her good growth was righteous action through remembrance, bodily service to God, and the heart's knowledge of Him.
TUSTARI:3:37/r2.anchor: بالعمل الصالح في ذكر الله تعالى وجوارحها في خدمة الله وقلبها في معرفة الله عز وجل

AKHFASH:v1p215/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p215/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p215/r1.claim: Akhfash reports the forms with Zakariyyā and Zakariyyāʾ as two dialects and says his reading is Zakariyyā without hamza.
AKHFASH:v1p215/r1.anchor: {وكفلها زكرياء} و {كفلها} ايضا {زكريا} وبه نقرأ وهما لغتان

AKHFASH:v1p215/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p215/r2.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p215/r2.claim: Some read the verb with kasra on fāʾ in the form associated with Zakariyyāʾ.

AKHFASH:v1p215/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p215/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p215/r3.claim: He notes differing vocalizations of kafala and their corresponding imperfects; one cited form kafila is one he has not heard himself.

AKHFASH:v1p215/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p215/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p215/r4.claim: Rizq without reckoning is like eating without strict account: provision is not counted out narrowly or restricted.
AKHFASH:v1p215/r4.anchor: فهذا مثل كلام العرب "يأكل بغير حساب" أي: لا يتعصب عليه ولا يضيق عليه

AKHFASH:v1p215/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p215/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p215/r5.claim: The descriptions quick at reckoning and quickest of reckoners mean that the accounting involves no thought, deliberation, or recollection.
AKHFASH:v1p215/r5.anchor: و {سريع الحساب} و {أسرع الحاسبين} يقول: "ليس في حسابه فكر ولا روية

DAMGHANI:v1p447/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r5.claim: Anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan means that God nurtured Mary well in worship over the years and months.
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r5.anchor: فوجه منها : النبات الغذاء . قوله تعالى فى سورة مريم

DAMGHANI:v1p405/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p405/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p405/r7.claim: Kafala means to take responsibility for Mary's care; the related question in 3:44 means to undertake raising her.
DAMGHANI:v1p405/r7.anchor: كفل أي ضمن قوله سبحانه في سورة آل عمران

DAMGHANI:v1p202/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r6.claim: In the account of Mary, rizq means fruit from both winter and summer.
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r6.anchor: الرزق بمعنى الفاكهة خاصة قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

DAMGHANI:v1p54/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p54/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p54/r1.claim: أَنّى can mean from where, as in asking where something came from.
DAMGHANI:v1p54/r1.anchor: الثاني : أنى من أين . قولها تعالى في سورة آل عمران

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r1.claim: Nabāt is what grows from the earth; manbit is its origin or place of growth.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r1.anchor: النبات في الأصل : ما يخرج من الأرض على صفة النمو . والمنبت : الأصل .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r5.claim: Nabāt can mean upbringing or nurturing; Mary was nurtured excellently.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r5.anchor: الرابع : التربية . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Mary grew in one day as much as a child grows in a year.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه كانت تنبت في اليوم ما ينبت المولود في عام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r7.claim: Qatāda reports that Mary did not commit sins.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p581/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة في هذه الآية : حدثنا أنها كانت لا تصيب الذنوب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r1.claim: Rizq means a gift or provision; rizqa is one individual allotment.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r7.claim: Rizq can mean fruit, as in the food found with Mary.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r7.anchor: والسادس : الفاكهة . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران :

FARRA:v1p207/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p207/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p207/r4.claim: With doubled fāʾ, kaf-falahā, Zakariyyā is accusative as the one who guaranteed her; with light fāʾ it is nominative as subject.
FARRA:v1p207/r4.anchor: من شدد جعل زكرياء في موضع نصب كقولك: ضمنها زكرياء، ومن خفف الفاء جعل زكرياء في موضع رفع

FARRA:v1p207/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p207/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p207/r5.claim: Zakariyyā has three Arabic forms: shortened, indeclinable long, and a shortened form with deleted long vowel and yāʾ that declines like an Arab nisba name.
FARRA:v1p207/r5.anchor: وفي زكريا ثلاث لغات: القصر فى ألفه، فلا يستبين فيها رفع ولا نصب ولا خفض، وتمد ألفه فتنصب وترفع بلا نون

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r6.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r6.claim: The third Qur'anic sense is 'from where,' as in Mary's provision and the question of how people are turned away.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p106/r6.anchor: وذكر المفسرون أنه في القرآن على هذه الأوجه الثلاثة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r1.claim: Zakariyyā took Mary into his care.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r2.claim: Miḥrāb can mean a chamber; an exegetical report says Zakariyyā climbed to it by a ladder.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r2.anchor: و {المحراب} الغرفة. وكذلك روي في التفسير: أن زكريا كان يصعد إليها بسلم. (3)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r3.claim: Miḥrāb can also mean a mosque, as in the verse about the miḥārīb made for Solomon.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r3.anchor: والمحراب أيضا: المسجد. قال: {يعملون له ما يشاء من محاريب} (4) ؛ أي: مساجد.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines a miḥrāb as the leading, foremost, and most honored place in an assembly, and likewise in a mosque.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: (5) المحراب سيد المجالس ومقدمها وأشرفها؛ وكذلك هو من المسجد.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r5.claim: Annā laki hādhā means: where did this come from for you?
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p104#2/r5.anchor: {أنى لك هذا} أي: من أين لك هذا؟

MAJAZ:v1p90/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p90/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p90/r3.claim: The phrase means that God favored her with gracious acceptance.

MAJAZ:v1p90/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p90/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p90/r4.claim: Kaffalahā means he took her into his care; two forms occur, kafalahā yakful and kaffalahā yakful.
MAJAZ:v1p90/r4.anchor: «وكفلها زكريا» (37) أي ضمها، وفيها لغتان: كفلها يكفل وكفلها يكفل

MAJAZ:v1p90/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p90/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p90/r5.claim: Miḥrāb is the foremost and most honored place in an assembly, and can also mean a mosque.
MAJAZ:v1p90/r5.anchor: «المحراب» (37) : سيد المجالس ومقدمها وأشرفها، وكذلك هو من المساجد

MAJAZ:v1p90/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p90/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p90/r6.claim: Annā laki hādhā means “from where did you get this?” Al-Kumayt b. Zayd’s verse illustrates annā in this sense.
MAJAZ:v1p90/r6.anchor: «أنى لك هذا» أي من أين لك هذا، قال الكميت بن زيد

NAHHAS:v1p369/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p369/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v1p369/r5.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports Ibn ʿAbbās: the aged wife vowed her fetus to service, bore a girl accepted by God; priests cast pens to choose her guardian, and Zakariyyā raised Mary, found out-of-season fruit, and hoped for a son.
NAHHAS:v1p369/r5.anchor: روى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال حملت امرأة عمران بعد ما أسنت فنذرت ما في بطنها محررا

NAHHAS:v1p371/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p371/r1.claim: Qabūl is a verbal noun of taqabbala; since taqabbala and qabila share the meaning, the phrase means “He accepted her with good acceptance.”
NAHHAS:v1p371/r1.anchor: مصدر تقبل تقبل إلا أن معنى تقبل وقبل واحد فالمعنى فقبلها ربها بقبول حسن

NAHHAS:v1p371/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p371/r2.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses inṭiwāʾ after taṭawwaytu although taṭawwaytu and inṭawaytu share a sense; another example uses ittibāʿan for tatbaʿuhu.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r2.anchor: لأن معنى تطويت وانطويت وحد قال أبو جعفر الحضب الحية ومثله

NAHHAS:v1p371/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p371/r3.claim: Nabātan is used instead of inbātan because anbatahā already conveys causing growth; similarly an unattributed poem uses idhlālan, though the verbal noun of dhallat is dhull.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r3.anchor: ( وأنبتها نباتا حسنا ) ولم يقل إنباتا لأنه لما قال أنبتها دل على نبت

NAHHAS:v1p371/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p371/r4.claim: The cited poem says “a difficult matter yielded and became humbled, as if by subduing”; idhlāl witnesses a verbal noun based on the conveyed meaning rather than the exact verb form.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r4.anchor: صعبة أي إذلال ) وإنما مصدر ذلت ذل ولكنه قد دل على معنى أذللت

NAHHAS:v1p371/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r5.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v1p371/r5.claim: Mujāhid reads fa-taqabbalhā with sukūn on lām as a request or prayer.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r5.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ( فتقبلها ) بإسكان اللام على الطلب والمسألة

NAHHAS:v1p371/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p371/r6.claim: Rabbiha is analyzed as an annexed vocative in the supplicatory reading.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r6.anchor: ( ربها ) نداء مضاف ( وأنبتها ) بإسكان التاء

NAHHAS:v1p371/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r7.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v1p371/r7.claim: In Mujāhid’s prayer reading, anbithā has sukūn on tāʾ and kaffilhā has sukūn on lām; Zakariyyā is long and accusative.

NAHHAS:v1p371/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v1p371/r8.claim: The Kūfans read kaffalahā Zakariyyā, understanding that God made Zakariyyā her guardian.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r8.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون ( وكفلها زكريا ) أي وكفلها الله زكرياء

NAHHAS:v1p371/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r9.speaker: هارون بن موسى عن عبد الله بن كثير وأبي عبد الله المدني
NAHHAS:v1p371/r9.claim: Hārūn ibn Mūsā reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Madanī the form kaffalaha with kasra on fāʾ.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r9.anchor: وروى هارون بن موسى عن عبد الله بن كثير وأبي عبد الله المدني ( وكفلها زكرياء ) بكسر الفاء

NAHHAS:v1p371/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r10.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v1p371/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash Saʿīd attests kafila yakful and kafala yakful, and says he has not heard kafala with the alternate vocalization.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r10.anchor: قال الأخفش سعيد يقال كفل يكفل وكفل يكفل ولم أسمع كفل

NAHHAS:v1p371/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r11.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p371/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the Ḥijāz lengthen or shorten Zakariyyā, while Najd drops the alif and declines Zakari.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r11.anchor: قال الفراء أهل الحجاز يمدون زكرياء ويقصرونه وأهل نجد يحذفون منه الألف ويصرفونه

NAHHAS:v1p371/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r12.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p371/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash lists four forms: long Zakariyyā, short Zakariyyā, declinable Zakari with doubled yāʾ, and Zakr.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r12.anchor: قال الأخفش فيه أربع لغات زكرياء بالمد وزكريا بالقصر وزكري بتشديد الياء والصرف

NAHHAS:v1p371/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r13.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v1p371/r13.claim: Abū Ḥātim says Zakrī is indeclinable because it is foreign; al-Naḥḥās rejects him, noting that a name ending in yāʾ like this can decline.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r13.anchor: قال أبو حاتم زكري بلا صرف لأنه أعجمي وهذا غلط لأن ما كانت فيه ياء مثل هذه انصرف

NAHHAS:v1p371/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p371/r14.claim: Zakariyyā in long and short forms is indeclinable because of the feminine-ending alif; its lack of tanwīn even when indefinite is evidence.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r14.anchor: ولم ينصرف زكرياء في المد والقصر لأن فيه ألف تأنيث والدليل على هذا أنه لا يصرف في النكرة

NAHHAS:v1p371/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p371/r15.claim: Another view attributes its indeclinability to foreign origin.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r15.anchor: وقال قوم لم ينصرف لأنه أعجمي ( كلما دخل ) منصوب بوجد

NAHHAS:v1p371/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p371/r16.claim: Kullamā dakhala is governed by wajada and means each time he entered; the alif of ḥisāb may also be given imāla because of the preceding kasra.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r16.anchor: ( كلما دخل ) منصوب بوجد أي كل دخوله أي كل وقت دخوله

NAHHAS:v1p371/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p371/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p371/r17.claim: The alif of ḥisāb may be inclined in pronunciation because of the kasra on ḥāʾ.
NAHHAS:v1p371/r17.anchor: وإن شئت أملت الألف من حساب لكسرة الحاء

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r1.claim: The majority read taqabbalahā as a past form with Rabb as its subject; God accepted Mary in place of the vowed boy, since a girl was not accepted for such a vow.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r1.anchor: الجمهور على " تقبلها " فعلا ماضيا على تفعل بتشديد العين، و " ربها " فاعل به.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r2.claim: Tafaʿʿala may mean the simple verb: God accepted Mary, approving her in place of the male vow; this is the interpretation reported in tafsīr.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r2.anchor: بمعنى رضيها مكان الذكر المنذور، ولم يقبل أنثى منذورة مثل مريم، كذا جاء في التفسير،

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r3.claim: The simple-verb use of tafaʿʿala is illustrated by taʿajjaba/ʿajiba and tabarraʾa/bariʾa.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r3.anchor: وتفعل يأتي بمعنى فعل مجردا نحو: تعجب وعجب من كذا، وتبرأ وبرىء منه.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r4.claim: Tafaʿʿala may also mean istifʿala: God took Mary into His care from the outset; al-Qatami’s istqbalat witnesses this sense.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r4.anchor: فاستقبلها ربها يقال: استقبلت الشيء أي: أخذته أول مرة

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r5.claim: The idiom khudh al-amra bi-qawābilihi and pairs such as taʿaẓẓama/istaʿẓama illustrate the frequent istifʿala sense of tafaʿʿala.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r5.anchor: ومنه المثل: " خذ الأمر بقوابله ". وتفعل بمعنى استفعل كثير نحو: تعظم واستعظم، وتكبر واستكبر، وتقصيت الشيء، واستقصيته وتعجلته واستعجلته.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r6.claim: On one analysis the bāʾ is extra and qabūlan is a verbal noun with its augment omitted; the expected form with taqabbala would be taqabbulan.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r6.anchor: أنها زائدة أي: قبولا، وعلى هذا فينتصب، " قبولا " على المصدر الذي جاء على حذف الزوائد؛ إذ لو جاء على تقبل لقيل: تقبلا نحو: تكبر تكبرا.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r7.claim: Qabūl is a verbal noun on the faʿūl pattern with fatḥa, as in qabiltu al-shayʾa qabūlan.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r7.anchor: وقبول من المصادر التي جاءت على فعول بفتح الفاء، وقد تقدم ذكرها أول البقرة، يقال: قبلت الشيء قبولا.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r8.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj permit qabūl with ḍamma on qāf, by analogy with al-dukhūl and al-khurūj.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r8.anchor: وأجاز الفراء والزجاج ضم القاف من " قبول " ، وهو القياس كالدخول والخروج

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r9.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r9.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī reports both fatḥa and ḍamma as heard forms; the phrase ʿalā wajhihi qabūl is reported only with ḍamma.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r9.anchor: وحكاها ابن الأعرابي عن العرب: قبلته قبولا وقبولا فتح القاف وضمها سماعا عن العرب، و " على وجهه قبول " لا غير،

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r10.claim: An anonymously cited line uses al-qabūl with ḍamma on qāf, supporting that pronunciation.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r10.anchor: والوجه عليه القبول بضم القاف كذا حكاه بعضهم.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r11.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r11.claim: Al-Zajjāj instead makes qabūlan governed by an implicit matching verb, estimating yutaqabbilu ḥasanan and qabilahā qabūlan ḥasanan; al-Samīn considers this strained.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r11.anchor: وقال الزجاج: " إن " قبولا هذا ليس منصوبا بهذا الفعل حتى يكون مصدرا على غير الصدر، بل هو منصوب بفعل موافق له أي: مجرد قال: " والتقدير: فتقبلها يتقبل حسن وقبلها قبولا حسنا أي: رضيها وفيه بعد.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r12.claim: If the bāʾ is not extra, qabūl names a means by which something is accepted, like ladūd or saʿūṭ; it then marks Mary’s special status in place of the male vow.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37/r12.anchor: أن الباء ليست زائدة، بل هي على حالها، ويكون المراد بالقبول هنا اسما لما يقبل به الشيء نحو: " اللدود " لما يلد به، والسعوط: لما يسعط به،

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r1.claim: Nabātan may be a verbal noun not matching the verb’s form, since the expected noun is inbāt.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r1.anchor: نبات أيضا مصدر على غير الصدر؛ إذ القياس: إنبات.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, an implicit matching verb governs nabātan, estimated as fa-nabatat nabātan ḥasanan.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: بل هو منصوب بمضمر موافق له أيضا تقديره: فنبتت نباتا حسنا.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r3.claim: The Kufans read the causative doubled kaf and put Zakariyyā in the accusative; Abū Bakr lengthens the name but also reads it accusative, while the others use a light kaf and nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: { وكفلها } قرأ الكوفيون: " وكفلها " بتشديد العين، " زكريا " بالقصر، إلا أبا بكر فإنه قرأه بالمد كالباقين، ولكنه ينصبه، والباقون يرفعونه كما سيأتي.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r4.claim: With the Kufan doubled verb, Zakariyyā is the second of two objects; the short form has an understood accusative ending, while Abū Bakr’s long form shows fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r4.anchor: فأما قراءة الكوفيين فإنهم عدوا الفعل بالتضعيف إلى مفعولين، ثانيهما " زكريا " فمن قصره كالأخوين وحفص عنده مقدر النصب، ومن مده كأبي بكر عن عاصم أظهر فيه الفتحة،

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r5.claim: The other seven readers have a light verb, transitive to Mary alone, with Zakariyyā as subject; the readings do not differ in meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r5.anchor: وأما قراءة بقية السبعة فكفل مخفف عندهم متعد لواحد

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r6.speaker: أبي
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r6.claim: Ubayy reads wa-akfalahā, using the hamza causative as in akramahā.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبي: " وأكفلها " ك " أكرمها " فعلا ماضيا.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r7.claim: The hamza causative has the same two-object syntax and meaning as the Kufan doubled reading: God is subject, Mary the first object, and Zakariyyā the second.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r7.anchor: وأما قراءة " أكفلها " فإنه عداه بالهمزة كما عداه غيره بالتضعيف نحو: خرجته/ وأخرجته، وكرمته وأكرمته، وهذه كقراءة الكوفيين في المعنى والإعراب،

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله المزني
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī reads kafalahā with a light kaf and kasra on fāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله المزني " وكفلها " بكسر الفاء والتخفيف.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r9.claim: The kasra form is a dialect, kafila yakfulu, alongside the common kafala yakfulu; its syntax follows the other readers, with Zakariyyā as subject.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r9.anchor: وأما قراءة: " وكفلها " بكسر الفاء فإنها لغة في كفل

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid reads the three verbs as a supplication by Mary’s mother: rabbahā is a vocative, and Zakariyyā remains a second object as in the Kufan reading.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r10.anchor: وأما قراءة مجاهد فإنها كلها على لفظ الدعاء من أم مريم لله تعالى بأن يفعل لها ما سألته. و " ربها " منصوب على النداء

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r11.claim: Ḥafṣ and al-Akhawayn shorten Zakariyyā wherever it occurs in the Qurʾān; the other seven readers lengthen it, and both forms are common Hijazi dialects.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ حفص والأخوان: " زكريا " بالقصر حيث ورد في القرآن، وباقي السبعة بالمد، والمد والقصر في هذا الاسم لغتان فاشيتان عن أهل الحجاز.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r12.claim: Though the foreign proper name would ordinarily be indeclinable for foreignness and properness, grammarians explain its form by analogy with feminine alif; indefinite indeclinability motivated this account.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r12.anchor: وهو اسم أعجمي فكان من حقه أن يقولوا فيه: منع من الصرف للعلمية والعجمة كنظائره، وإنما قالوا: منع من الصرف لوجود ألف التأنيث فيه.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r13.claim: The argument for a feminine-alif analogy is that the name is indeclinable when indefinite; Abū Ḥātim allowed tanwīn in the indefinite, apparently treating it as foreign and proper, but was faulted.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#2/r13.anchor: قالوا: فلو كان منعه للعلمية والعجمة لانصرف نكرة لزوال أحد سببي المنع، لكن العرب منعته نكرة، فعلمنا أن المانع غير ذلك، وليس معنا هنا ما يصلح مانعا من صرفه إلا ألف التأنيث،

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r1.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī argues the final hamza cannot be an original or augment letter, so it must mark feminine alif; he applies the argument to the short form too.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r1.anchor: وقال الفارسي فأشبع فيه القول: " لا يخلو من أن يكون الهمزة فيه: للتأنيث أو للإلحاق أو منقلبة، ولا يجوز أن تكون منقلبة؛

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r2.claim: Al-Samīn accepts Abū ʿAlī’s analysis for an Arabic word with known derivation and inflection, but foreign names are treated analogically as Arabic forms.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r2.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله أبو علي صحيح لو كان فيما يعرف له اشتقاق ويدخله تصريف، ولكنهم يجرون الأسماء الأعجمية مجرى العربية

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r3.claim: Another form is zakariyy, with final doubled y and no alif; it is declinable. Abū ʿAlī explains its endings as substituted nisba yāʾs, since an original foreign ending would prevent declension.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r3.anchor: وفيه بعد ذلك لغتان أخريان، إحداهما: زكري بياء مشددة في آخره فقد دون ألف، وهو في هذه اللغة منصرف. ووجه أبو علي ذلك فقال: " القول فيه أنه حذف منه الياءان

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r4.claim: The declinable zakariyy form is a Najdi usage and is used by neighboring tribes.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r4.anchor: وهذه اللغة التي ذكرتها لغة أهل نجد ومن والاهم.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r5.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash records another form, zakar, on the pattern of ʿAmr.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r5.anchor: والثانية: " زكر " بزنة عمرو، حكاها الأخفش

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r6.claim: Kafāla originally means guarantee, then extends to taking someone in and embracing responsibility; its forms include kāfil and kafīl.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#3/r6.anchor: يقال منه: كفل يكفل، وكفل يكفل كعلم يعلم كفالة وكفلا فهو كافل وكفيل.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r1.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r1.claim: Sībawayh treats al-miḥrāb as a locative adverb after dakhala; this is exceptional because a specified place normally requires fī.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r1.anchor: أحدهما وهو مذهب سيبويه أنه منصوب على الظرف، وشذ عن سائر إخوانه

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r2.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash treats the noun after dakhala as a direct object; al-Samīn rejects this because non-place use requires fī, as in dakhaltu fī al-amr.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r2.anchor: والثاني: مذهب الأخفش، هو نصب ما بعد " دخل " على المفعول به لا على الظرف، فقولك: " دخلت البيت " كقولك: " هدمت البيت "

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines miḥrāb as the most honored and foremost seat, including such a place in a mosque.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: " هو أشرف المجالس ومقدمها، وهو كذلك من المسجد ".

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ takes miḥrāb to mean a palace because of its height and nobility.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r4.anchor: وقال ابو عمرو بن العلاء: " هو القصر لعلوه وشرفه ".

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī defines miḥrāb as a chamber; Imruʾ al-Qays uses maḥārīb for rulers’ chambers.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r5.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: " هو الغرفة " وأنشد لامرىء القيس: 1246 وماذا عليه أن ذكرت أوانسا كغزلان رمل في محاريب أقيال

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r6.claim: A verse by ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa likewise uses miḥrāb for a chamber approached by climbing a ladder.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r6.anchor: وأنشد غيره لعمر بن أبي ربعية: 1247 ربة محراب إذا جئتها لم أدن حتى أرتقي سلما

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r7.claim: For this verse, miḥrāb means the familiar mosque sanctuary; earlier definitions describe the word generally, not a disagreement about this verse.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو المحراب من المسجد المعهود وهو الأليق بالآية

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r8.claim: Miḥrāb is also said to derive from ḥarb because people compete for it.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r8.anchor: قيل: واشتقاقه من الحرب لتحارب الناس عليه.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r9.speaker: ابن ذكوان
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r9.claim: Ibn Dhakwān applies imāla to miḥrāb at two places in this sūra, where a kasra precedes and follows its alif; non-genitive uses allow imāla or tafkhīm.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#4/r9.anchor: وأمال ابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر " المحراب " في هذه السورة موضعين بلا خلاف

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r1.claim: Wajada means found, encountered, or came upon and takes one object, rizqan; ʿindahā is normally an adverbial of finding.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r1.anchor: هذه " وجد " بمعنى أصاب ولقي وصادف فتتعدى لواحد وهو " رزقا "

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows ʿindahā to be a circumstantial phrase modifying rizqan, since it could originally qualify it as an adjective and attach to an omitted predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r2.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء أن يكون حالا من " رزقا " لأنه يصلح أن يكون صفة له في الأصل،

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r3.claim: Wajada governs kullamā as a temporal adverb; Abū al-Baqāʾ calls it the conditional answer because kullamā resembles a conditional.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r3.anchor: و " وجد " هو الناصب لكلما، لأنها ظرفية، وقد تقدم تحقيقه.

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says qāla yā Maryam is a new sentence, not a substitute for wajada because their meanings differ.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r4.anchor: أحدهما: أنه مستأنف، قال أبو البقاء: " ولا يجوز أن يكون بدلا من

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also permits coordination with a deleted fāʾ, by analogy with conditional answers and a cited poem.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r5.anchor: والثاني: أنه معطوف بالفاء، فحذف العاطف، قال أبو البقاء:

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r6.claim: Al-Samīn rejects the proposed parallel with 6:121: the conditional answer there is omitted, while inna-kum la-mushrikūn answers an implicit oath before the condition.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r6.anchor: ليس كذلك، بل جواب الشرط محذوف، و " إنكم لمشركون " جواب قسم مقدر قبل الشرط

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r7.claim: The poetic example permits omission of the fāʾ only by poetic necessity and does not establish the ordinary construction.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r7.anchor: وكيف يدعي ذلك ويسويه بالبيت المذكور وهو لا يجوز إلا في ضرورة

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r8.claim: The wajada clause is circumstantial to the subject of dakhala, and qāla itself answers kullamā: whenever Zakariyyā entered having found provision, he spoke.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r8.anchor: الذي يظهر أن الجملة من قوله: " وجد " في محل نصب على الحال من فاعل " دخل "

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r9.claim: The indefinite rizqan either magnifies the provision or indicates a particular kind of it.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#5/r9.anchor: ونكر " رزقا " تعظيما له أو ليدل به على نوع ما منه

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r1.claim: Annā is a fronted predicate and hādhā a delayed subject; Abū ʿUbayda explains annā as min ayna, “from where.”
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r1.anchor: أنى خبر مقدم، و " هذا " مبتدأ مؤخر، ومعنى " أنى " هنا: من أين

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r2.claim: An alternative takes the question to ask how the provision came about; al-Kumayt’s line pairs annā with min ayna.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r2.anchor: وقيل: ويجوز أن يكون سؤالا عن الكيفية أي: كيف تهيأ لك هذا،

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r3.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ parses annā as an adverb governed by the existential sense in laka, with laka raising hādhā; al-Samīn says this is unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r3.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء في " أنى " أن ينتصب على الظرف بالاستقرار الذي في " لك "

SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r4.claim: The statement that God provides whom He wills may be independent divine speech or Mary’s speech, in which case it is accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:3:37#6/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون مستأنفا [من كلام الله تعالى، وأن يكون من كلام مريم فيكون منصوبا]

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r8.claim: God accepted Mary in the vow despite the custom against dedicating girls, as a sign connected with Jesus.
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r8.anchor: فجعل الله عز وجل من الآيات في مريم - لما أراده الله من أمر عيسى - أن جعلها متقبلة في النذر

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r9.claim: The expected form is bi-taqabbul; qabūl is the verbal noun in qabilahā qabūlan ḥasanan and can mean accepting something.
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r9.anchor: الأصل في العربية: بتقبل حسن، ولكن قبول محمول على قوله قبلها قبولا حسنا، يقال: قبلت الشيء قبولا حسنا

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r10.claim: Qabūl is used of the wind's coming; qabila bi-l-rajul can mean taking responsibility for his care.
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r10.anchor: وقبلت الريح قبولا وهي تقبل، وقبلت بالرجل أقبل قبالة، أي كفلت به،

ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r11.claim: The sponsorship sense is also reported on the faʿala pattern; the source then begins an example of watering camels.
ZAJJAJ:v1p400/r11.anchor: على مثال فعلت، ويقال: سقى فلان إبله قبلا.

ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r1.claim: Qiblan describes something seen face to face, and qabl can mean whatever faces or meets you.
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r1.anchor: عاينت قلت فيه أتاني قبلا، أي معاينة، وكل ما استقبلك فهو قبل (بالفتح).

ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r2.claim: Dhi qabl in a time expression can mean days before or days ahead; qabl also refers to days expected in the future.
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r2.anchor: وتقول لا أكملك إلى عشر من ذي قبل وقبل، المعنى قبل إلى عشر مما

ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r3.claim: For the eye, qabila means its gaze turns toward the nose.
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r3.anchor: ويقال: قبلت العين تقبل قبلا إذا أقبل النظر على الأنف.

ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r7.claim: Qibla is described as a plural of qabl, compared with a spindle whorl in a necklace.
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r7.anchor: والقبلة: جمع قبل شبيهة بالفلكة، أي بفلكة المغزل تكون في القلادة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r8.claim: God gave her good growth; nabātan is by meaning, as though the wording were nabata nabātan rather than matching anbatnā in form.
ZAJJAJ:v1p401/r8.anchor: على غير لفظ أنبت، على معنى نبت نباتا حسنا.

ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r1.claim: Zakariyyā is read long or short without declension, or as Zakariyy with the alif omitted and full declension; that third form is common Arabic.
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r1.anchor: القصر والمد في زكريا. والقراءة بهما كثيرة كما وصفنا

ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r2.claim: Names ending in feminine alif do not decline in definite or indefinite use; the alif is fused with the name, unlike feminine tāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r2.anchor: وفي (زكريا) ثلاث لغات هي المشهورة المعروفة - زكرياء بالمد وزكريا - بالقصر غير منون في الجهتين جميعا، وزكري بحذف الألف

ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r3.speaker: بعض النحويين
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r3.claim: Some grammarians say the name is indeclinable because it is foreign; al-Zajjāj rejects this explanation, since foreign names can decline when indefinite.
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r3.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين: إنه لم يصرف لأنه أعجمي، وما كانت فيه ألف التأنيث فهو سواء في العربية والعجمية.

ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r4.claim: Feminine-alif names do not decline whether Arabic or foreign because the alif is fused into the name, unlike tāʾ marbūṭa.
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r4.anchor: لأن ما كان أعجميا فهو يتصرف في النكرة، ولا يجوز أن تصرف الأسماء التي فيها ألف التأنيث في معرفة ولا نكرة

ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r5.claim: With Zakariyyā nominative he undertakes Mary's care; Abū ʿUbayda glosses it as providing for her and taking charge.
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r5.anchor: فالمعنى فيما ذكر أبو عبيدة ضمنها، ومعناه في هذا ضمن القيام بأمرها.

ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r6.claim: With Zakariyyā accusative, God caused him to care for Mary; the third dialect form is excluded from Qur'anic recitation because it conflicts with the rasm.
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r6.anchor: ومن قرأ (كفلها زكرياء) بالنصب - فالمعنى: وكفلها الله زكرياء، وأما اللغة الثالثة فلا تجوز في القرآن لأنها مخالفة المصحف

ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r7.claim: Miḥrāb is the foremost honored place in a gathering; some say their mosques were so called, and it denotes an elevated, noble place.
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r7.anchor: المحراب في اللغة الموضع العالي الشريف.

ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r8.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r8.claim: The poet's line uses miḥrāb for a distinguished place one must ascend to reach.
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر: ربة محراب إذا جئتها. . . لم ألقها

ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r9.claim: Kullamā is accusative through wajada; mā with dakhal functions as a verbal noun, meaning each time he enters the miḥrāb.
ZAJJAJ:v1p402/r9.anchor: ونصب (كلما بقوله: (وجد) أي يجد عندها الرزق في كل وقت يدخل عليها المحراب

ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r1.claim: Annā laki hādhā means “Where did this come from for you?”

ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r2.claim: Zachariah feared the provision came through another person; finding it from God confirmed it as one of Mary's signs.
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r2.anchor: وإنما سأل زكريا عن الرزق لأنه خاف أن يأتيها - من غير جهته فتبين عنده أنه من عند الله

ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r3.claim: Mary's signs included acceptance in a sanctuary vow, Jesus' creation through God's word, and sustenance delivered directly by God.
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r3.anchor: فمن آياتها أنها أول امرأة قبلت في نذر في المتعبد. ومنها أن الله أنشأ فيها عيسى - عليه السلام - من كلمة ألقاها إليها

ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r4.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r4.claim: A reported exegetical view says Mary never suckled from a breast.
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r4.anchor: وقد قيل في التفسير أنها لم تلقم ثديا قط.

ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r5.anchor: أي بغير تقتير، و (حساب). إن شئت فتحت الألف

ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r6.claim: The alif in ḥisāb may be pronounced with full opening or inclined toward kasra because the preceding ḥāʾ is kasra; both are common in Arabic.
ZAJJAJ:v1p403/r6.anchor: و (حساب). إن شئت فتحت الألف وألزمتها جهة الفتح، وإن شئت أملتها إلى الكسر، لانكسار الحاء، وذلك كثير في لغة العرب.

ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n26/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n26/r1.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n26/r1.claim: Tabari says Mary was entrusted to Zachariah, her relative and a Temple priest, after lots decided which priest would care for her because her mother's vow dedicated her to Temple service.
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n26/r1.anchor: the guardianship of Mary was entrusted to Zachariah - who was not only her relative but also a priest attached to the Temple - after lots had been drawn

ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r1.claim: Against commentators' legends, Asad finds no Qur'anic or authentic-Tradition evidence that Mary's provisions were miraculous.
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r1.anchor: there is no indication whatsoever either in the Qur'an or in any authentic Tradition that these provisions were of a miraculous origin

ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r2.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r2.claim: Tabari relates that when aged Zachariah could no longer support Mary, the community arranged for another member to provide her daily food; Asad leaves the story's authenticity unresolved.
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r2.anchor: Tabari quotes a story to the effect that when, in his old age, Zachariah became unable to support Mary by his own means

ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r3.claim: Asad reads Mary's answer as expressing her deep awareness that God is the ultimate Provider.
ASAD-NOTES:3:37#n27/r3.anchor: Mary's answer to Zachariah reflects no more and no less than her deep consciousness of God as the ultimate Provider

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p61/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p61/r2.speaker: سيبويه
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p61/r2.claim: Sībawayh’s rule is that speakers put first what matters most to them and about which they care most.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p61/r2.anchor: قاعدة نحوية: يقول سيبويه في التقديم والتأخير: يقدمون الذي هو أهمّ لهم وهم أعنى به

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p61/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p61/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p61/r3.claim: Order depends on context, not a fixed ranking; because the passage focuses on Mary rather than Zechariah or the sanctuary, it brings عليها forward.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p61/r3.anchor: والتقديم والتأخير في القرآن الكريم يقرره سياق الآيات فقد يتقدم المفضول وقد يتقدم الفاضل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p115/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p115/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p115/r2.claim: نباتاً حسناً praises Mary’s receptive nature: God made her grow, and she responded and flourished; إنباتاً would leave the action wholly on God’s side.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p115/r2.anchor: أراد تعالى أن يجمع بين الأمرين أنه تعالى أنبتها كما يشاء وأراد من باب الثناء أن يجعل لها فضلاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p646/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p646/r1.speaker: سيبويه
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p646/r1.claim: Sībawayh’s rule is that speakers put first what matters most to them and what they care about most.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p646/r1.anchor: يقول سيبويه في التقديم والتأخير: يقدمون الذي هو أهمّ لهم وهم أعنى به

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p646/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p646/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p646/r2.claim: The passage centers on Mary, not Zachariah or the sanctuary, so the preposed عليها foregrounds her as the subject of the account.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p646/r2.anchor: لذا قدّم عليها لأن الكلام كله عن مريم عليها السلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p512/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p512/r1.speaker: سيبويه
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p512/r1.claim: Sibawayh says speakers advance what matters most to them and occupies their greatest concern.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p512/r1.anchor: يقول سيبويه في التقديم والتأخير: يقدمون الذي هو أهمّ لهم وهم أعنى به

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p512/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p512/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p512/r2.claim: Because the surrounding Al Imran passage concerns Mary, not Zechariah or the mihrab, the wording foregrounds her in “عليها زكريا.”
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p512/r2.anchor: الكلام في الآية في سورة آل عمران والآيات التي سبقتها في مريم عليها السلام وليس في زكريا ولا في المحراب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p564/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p564/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p564/r2.claim: “نباتاً حسناً” credits Mary’s responsive nature and willing growth alongside God’s nurturing; “إنباتاً” would present the process solely as God’s act and omit her merit.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p564/r2.anchor: أن لها فضل في هذا ولو قال تعالى إنباتاً لكان كله عملية لله وحده وليس لمريم أي فضل

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read كفلها with a light fāʾ and Zakariyyā as a long nominative; the subject of the guardianship is Zakariyyā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر: (وكفلها) مفتوحة الفاء خفيفة

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r2.claim: In Abū Bakr's transmission from ʿĀṣim, كفلها is doubled and Zakariyyā is long and accusative; doubled kafala takes two objects, making Zakariyyā the second object and God's pronoun the subject.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر (وكفلها) مشددة و (زكرياء) نصب

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r3.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r3.claim: Ḥafṣ transmits the doubled fāʾ with the shortened name Zakariyyā throughout the Qurʾān.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r3.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم: (وكفلها) مشددا و زكريا قصرا في كل القرآن

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r4.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī also double the fāʾ and shorten Zakariyyā throughout the Qurʾān.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r4.anchor: وكان حمزة والكسائي يشددان (كفلها)، ويقصران (زكريا) في كل القرآن

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r5.claim: The light reading is supported by 3:44, أيهم يكفل مريم; كفل takes one object, and Zakariyyā is its nominative subject.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r5.anchor: حجة من خفف (كفلها) قوله تعالى : أيهم يكفل مريم

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r6.claim: With doubled kafala, the verb takes two objects: the subject is the pronoun referring to her Lord in فتقبلها ربها, and Zakariyyā becomes the second object.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r6.anchor: فإن كفلت يتعدى إلى مفعول واحد، فإذا ضاعفت العين تعدى إلى مفعولين

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r7.claim: The final hamza in the long form cannot be an augment for analogy or a substitute letter, so it is a feminine marker; the same analysis applies to the shortened form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p33#2/r7.anchor: فإذا بطل هذان، ثبت أنه للتأنيث، وكذلك القول فيمن قصر

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r1.claim: Al-Farisi explains that removing the feminine alif lets the name conform to Arabic inflectional shapes such as Zakariyya and Zakari.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r1.anchor: لما أعربت الكلمة وافقت العربية. وقد حذفوا ألف التأنيث من الكلمة فقالوا: هو يمشي الجيض والجيضى

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r2.claim: The declinable form Zakari has two nisba yāʾs added after deleting the original yāʾs; if they were original, foreign-name status would make it indeclinable like Ibrahim.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r2.anchor: فمن قال: زكري صرف، والقول فيه أنه حذف الياءين اللتين كانتا في (زكرياء) و (زكريا) وألحق الكلمة ياءي النسب

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r3.claim: Nisba yāʾs can make an otherwise indeclinable pattern declinable, as in madāʾinī and maʿāfirī.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r3.anchor: ما كان على وزن مفاعل لا ينصرف فإذا ألحقته ياءي النسب انصرف كقوله: مدائني ومعافري

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r4.claim: The two yāʾs need not convey actual affiliation, just as forms such as kursī and qamarī have no relational meaning here.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r4.anchor: ولحقت الاسم الياءان وإن لم يكن فيه معنى نسب إلى شيء كما لم يكن في كرسي وقمري وثمان معنى نسب إلى شيء

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r5.claim: Nisba yāʾs do not attach before the feminine alif, but can precede tāʾ because tāʾ behaves like a noun joined to another noun.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p35/r5.anchor: أن ياءي النسب لا تلحقان قبل ألف التأنيث وإن كانتا قد لحقتا قبل التاء من بصرية لأن التاء بمنزلة اسم مضموم إلى اسم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r1.claim: With doubled fāʾ, the verb takes Mary and Zakariya as two objects; Zakariya is accusative and the phrase coordinates with “her Lord accepted her.”
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r1.anchor: يقرأ بتشديد الفاء وتخفيفها فالحجة لمن شدد أنه عدى بالتشديد الفعل إلى مفعولين إحداهما الهاء والألف

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r2.claim: With light fāʾ, Zakariya is the subject and the attached pronoun is the object; the parallel question “which of them would care for Mary?” supports this parsing.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن خفف الفاء أنه جعل الفعل ل زكريا فرفعه بالحديث عنه وجعل ما اتصل بالفعل من الكناية مفعولا له

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r3.claim: Zakariya is diptote because it is a definite foreign proper name.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r3.anchor: وزكريا يمد ويقصر ولا يجرى للتعريف والعجمة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r4.claim: In “the angels called to her,” the tāʾ reading marks the angels as a group, supported by the feminine singular in “the angels said.”
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r4.anchor: الملائكة جماعة فدل بالتاء على معنى الجماعة والدليل على ذلك قوله

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r5.claim: The alif reading uses a masculine singular verb because the verb precedes its subject and the angels here mean Gabriel.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p108/r5.anchor: والحجة لمن قرأ بالألف أن الفعل مقدم فأثبت بالألف كما أقول رماه القوم وعاداه الرجال

NASHR:v1p18#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p18#2/r1.claim: Some imams permit mixing readings absolutely and condemn those who forbid it; Ibn al-Jazari prefers a distinction: prohibit combinations where one grammatical reading depends on another, since the hybrid may violate Arabic, as with the cited examples.
NASHR:v1p18#2/r1.anchor: والصواب عندنا في ذلك التفصيل والعدول بالتوسط إلى سواء السبيل، فنقول: إن كانت إحدى القراءتين مترتبة على الأخرى فالمنع من ذلك منع تحريم

NASHR:v1p18#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p18#2/r2.claim: When two readings are not grammatically interdependent, combining them as a transmitted narration remains impermissible as false attribution; outside a claim of transmission, reading the combination is sound and allowed, though experts are reproached for equating themselves with lay readers.
NASHR:v1p18#2/r2.anchor: فإن قرأ بذلك على سبيل الرواية، فإنه لا يجوز أيضا من حيث إنه كذب في الرواية

NASHR:v1p18#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p18#2/r3.claim: The variety of readings was sent by God through the Faithful Spirit to ease the community; requiring each reader to separate every transmission would turn intended ease into hardship.
NASHR:v1p18#2/r3.anchor: إذ كل من عند الله نزل به الروح الأمين على قلب سيد المرسلين تخفيفا عن الأمة

NASHR:v1p18#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
NASHR:v1p18#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i transmits Ibn Masud's rule that an error is not mixing parts of the Qur'an, but adding material that does not belong to it; Ibn al-Jazari calls the report sound in chain.
NASHR:v1p18#2/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي قال: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: (ليس الخطأ أن يقرأ بعضه في بعض

NASHR:v1p18#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18#2/r5.speaker: النبي
NASHR:v1p18#2/r5.claim: The Prophet instructed believers to recite whichever of the seven aḥruf was easy; the report is agreed upon and this wording is from al-Bukhari via Umar.
NASHR:v1p18#2/r5.anchor: إن هذا القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف، فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه، متفق عليه وهذا لفظ البخاري عن عمر

NASHR:v1p18#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18#2/r6.speaker: عمر
NASHR:v1p18#2/r6.claim: Al-Bukhari's report from Umar recounts hearing Hisham ibn Hakim recite al-Furqan differently from the reading Umar had learned from the Prophet.
NASHR:v1p18#2/r6.anchor: وفي لفظ البخاري أيضا عن عمر: سمعت هشام بن حكيم بن حزام يقرأ سورة الفرقان على غير ما أقرأنيها رسول الله

NASHR:v1p18#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18#2/r7.speaker: أبي
NASHR:v1p18#2/r7.claim: Muslim reports that Gabriel successively asked the Prophet to teach the community one, then two, then three aḥruf, and the Prophet asked for relief because his community could not bear the first offer.
NASHR:v1p18#2/r7.anchor: كان عند أضاة بني غفار فأتاه جبريل فقال: إن الله يأمرك أن تقرأ أمتك القرآن على حرف

NASHR:v2p239/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p239/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p239/r3.claim: The Kufans double the fāʾ in وكفلها, while the other readers pronounce it light.
NASHR:v2p239/r3.anchor: فقرأ الكوفيون بتشديد الفاء، وقرأ الباقون بتخفيفها

NASHR:v2p239/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p239/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p239/r4.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, and Hafs shorten زكريا without hamza throughout the Qur'an; the others lengthen it with hamza, and Abu Bakr makes it accusative here as a second object of وكفلها while the other light-form readers use nominative.
NASHR:v2p239/r4.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص بالقصر من غير همزة في جميع القرآن، وقرأ الباقون بالمد والهمز

NASHR:v2p63#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p63#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p63#2/r1.claim: Khalaf in his choice from Hamza uses imāla for آتيك in both places; reports differ for Khallad, but the author favors fatḥ as the sound position, supported by al-Taysir's preference and most Iraqi authorities.
NASHR:v2p63#2/r1.anchor: فأماله في الموضعين خلف في اختياره عن حمزة، واختلف عن خلاد أيضا فيهما

NASHR:v2p63#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p63#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p63#2/r2.claim: Some authorities transmit imāla for Khallad on the two occurrences of آتيك, while the Taysir permits both but says it takes fatḥ; al-Dani calls fatḥ correct after reading it to Abu al-Fath and imāla to Abu al-Hasan.
NASHR:v2p63#2/r2.anchor: وقال في جامع البيان إنه هو الصحيح عنه، وبه قرأ على أبي الفتح وبالإمالة على أبي الحسن

NASHR:v2p63#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p63#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p63#2/r3.claim: Ibn Dhakwan consistently uses imāla for the two genitive occurrences of المحراب, in Al Imran and Maryam.
NASHR:v2p63#2/r3.anchor: وأما المحراب فأماله ابن ذكوان من جميع طرقه إذا كان مجرورا، وذلك موضعان يصلي في المحراب في آل عمران وفخرج على قومه من المحراب في مريم

NASHR:v2p63#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p63#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p63#2/r4.claim: For the two accusative occurrences, some routes from al-Akhfash transmit imāla for Ibn Dhakwan, while al-Suri, Ibn al-Akhram, and the other performance authorities transmit fatḥ; several manuals record both options.
NASHR:v2p63#2/r4.anchor: كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب في آل عمران، وإذ تسوروا المحراب في ص

NASHR:v2p154/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r1.claim: The rasm joins ألا in most cases, with stated exceptions; the Naml and opening Hud examples are connected, while the Anbiya instance is disputed.
NASHR:v2p154/r1.anchor: فأما: ألا) فإنه كتب متصلا في غير العشرة المتقدمة

NASHR:v2p154/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r2.claim: إنما is joined except in al-Anam; the Nahl instance is disputed, while its spelling is joined outside al-Hajj and Luqman.
NASHR:v2p154/r2.anchor: (وإنما) كتب موصولا في غير الأنعام نحو: إنما نملي لهم

NASHR:v2p154/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r3.claim: The forms إلا أنما, كأنما, and أنما غنمتم are treated separately; the first two are joined in the stated places, and the last is disputed.
NASHR:v2p154/r3.anchor: إلا أنما أنا نذير في ص.

NASHR:v2p154/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r4.claim: إما is written joined except in al-Rad, with the cited forms إما تخافن, إما نرينك, فإما نذهبن, and فإما ترين.
NASHR:v2p154/r4.anchor: " وإما " موصول في غير الرعد نحو وإما تخافن

NASHR:v2p154/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r5.claim: أينما is joined at two places in al-Baqara and al-Nahl; its instances in al-Nisa, al-Shuara, and al-Ahzab are disputed.
NASHR:v2p154/r5.anchor: (وأينما) كتب موصولا في موضعين فأينما تولوا

NASHR:v2p154/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r6.claim: إن لم is joined in one place, the form فإلم يستجيبوا لكم in Hud.
NASHR:v2p154/r6.anchor: (وإن لم) موصول في موضع واحد، وهو فإلم يستجيبوا لكم

NASHR:v2p154/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r7.claim: أن لن is joined in two places, in al-Kahf and al-Qiyama.
NASHR:v2p154/r7.anchor: (وألن) كتب موصولا في موضعين: الكهف والقيامة كما تقدم

NASHR:v2p154/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r8.claim: عما is joined except at its al-Araf occurrence; the cited examples are عما تعملون and عما جاءك.
NASHR:v2p154/r8.anchor: " وعما " موصول في غير موضع الأعراف نحو عما تعملون

NASHR:v2p154/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r10.claim: أمن is joined outside four previously specified instances; examples include أمن يملك السمع, أمن خلق السماوات, and أمن يجيب المضطر.
NASHR:v2p154/r10.anchor: (وأمن) كتب موصولا في غير المواضع الأربعة المتقدمة نحو أمن يملك السمع

NASHR:v2p154/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r11.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r11.claim: عمن is joined except in al-Nur and al-Najm, though the author says he knows of no Quranic occurrence.
NASHR:v2p154/r11.anchor: " وعمن " موصول في غير النور والنجم

NASHR:v2p154/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r12.claim: كلما is joined outside Ibrahim; the occurrence in this verse is an example, while instances in al-Nisa, al-Araf, al-Muminun, and Tabarak are disputed.
NASHR:v2p154/r12.anchor: " وكلما " كتب موصولا في غير سورة إبراهيم نحو كلما دخل عليها

NASHR:v2p154/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r14.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r14.claim: فيما is joined outside al-Shuara, including the first instance in al-Baqara and فيما إن مكناكم فيه; ten instances are disputed.
NASHR:v2p154/r14.anchor: " وفيما " كتب موصولا في غير الشعراء نحو فيما فعلن

NASHR:v2p152/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p152/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p152/r1.claim: When words are written joined, pausing is allowed only on the final word; most authorities therefore prefer not to split ويكأن or ويكأنه despite a transmitted allowance.
NASHR:v2p152/r1.anchor: فإنه لا يجوز فصله بوقف إلا برواية صحيحة ولذلك كان المختار عند أكثر الأئمة عدم فصل ويكأن

NASHR:v2p152/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p152/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p152/r2.claim: A one-letter particle attached to a word is written with it as one unit; the author gives examples of particles and their hosts.
NASHR:v2p152/r2.anchor: كل كلمة دخل عليها حرف من حروف المعاني، وهو على حرف واحد نحو بسم الله

NASHR:v2p152/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p152/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p152/r3.claim: A word joined to an attached pronoun is written together, whether the pronoun is one or more letters and nominative, accusative, or genitive.
NASHR:v2p152/r3.anchor: كل كلمة اتصل بها ضمير متصل سواء كان على حرف واحد

NASHR:v2p152/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p152/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p152/r4.claim: The disjoint alphabetic letters at sura openings are written connected, except حم عسق, which is split between mīm and ʿayn.
NASHR:v2p152/r4.anchor: حروف المعجم المقطعة في فواتح السور سواء كانت ثنائية، أو ثلاثية، أو أكثر من ذلك

NASHR:v2p152/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p152/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p152/r5.claim: When the second word begins with a hamza represented as waw or ya for easing, the two are written joined.
NASHR:v2p152/r5.anchor: إذا كان، أول الكلمة الثانية همزة وصورت على مراد التخفيف واوا وياء

NASHR:v2p152/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p152/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p152/r6.claim: The definite article al- joins to what follows as one written word, whether the following item is a particle or a noun.
NASHR:v2p152/r6.anchor: (أما ال) فإنها إذا دخلت على كلمة أخرى كتبتا موصولتين كلمة واحدة

NASHR:v2p153/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p153/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p153/r1.claim: The vocative يا loses its alif in the codices and joins its addressee; in يابنؤم the hamza is drawn as waw and joined to nun.
NASHR:v2p153/r1.anchor: (وأما: يا) ، وهي حرف النداء فإنها حذفت الألف

NASHR:v2p153/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p153/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p153/r2.claim: The alerting particle ها likewise loses its alif and joins what follows; in هؤلاء the hamza is written as waw and joined.
NASHR:v2p153/r2.anchor: (وأما: ها) ، وهي الواقعة حرف تنبيه فإن ألفها كذلك حذفت

NASHR:v2p153/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p153/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p153/r3.claim: Interrogative ما joins a preceding preposition after dropping its final alif; with إلى, على, or حتى, the alif is written to reflect pronunciation and avoid confusion.
NASHR:v2p153/r3.anchor: (وأما: ما) الاستفهامية فإنها إذا دخل عليها حرف الجر حذف الألف

NASHR:v2p153/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p153/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p153/r4.claim: أم مع ما is joined throughout the Quran, as in أما اشتملت, أماذا كنتم, and أما تشركون.
NASHR:v2p153/r4.anchor: (وأما: أم - مع - ما) فإنها كتبت موصولة في جميع القرآن نحو أما اشتملت

NASHR:v2p153/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p153/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p153/r5.claim: The lightened kasra إن followed by لا is joined throughout the Quran, as in إلا تفعلوه and إلا تنصروه.
NASHR:v2p153/r5.anchor: (وأما إن المكسورة المخففة مع لا) فإنها كتبت موصولة في جميع القرآن نحو إلا تفعلوه

NASHR:v2p153/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p153/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p153/r6.claim: كالوهم and وزنوهم are joined in every codex, shown by deleting the alif after waw; the author prefers analyzing هم as an attached accusative pronoun, not a separate nominative.
NASHR:v2p153/r6.anchor: فإنهما كتبتا في جميع المصاحف موصولين بدليل حذف الألف بعد الواو منهما

NASHR:v2p153/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p153/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p153/r7.claim: The non-predictable joined forms include إلا, إنما, أينما, إن لم, أن لن, عما, مما, أمن, عمن, كلما, بئسما, فيما, كيلا, and يومهم.
NASHR:v2p153/r7.anchor: والكلمات التي هي غير مطردة فهي، إلا، وإنما وإن المكسورة المخففة مع ما

QIRAAT-ER:3:37:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:12#1/r1.speaker: Vr
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:12#1/r1.claim: Form I means Zakariyyā took charge of Mary himself, shifting agency from God's assignment to Zakariyyā's active guardianship.
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:12#1/r1.anchor: Form I kafala (simple): ""and he took charge of her"" — Zakariyyā is the subject who actively takes guardianship

QIRAAT-ER:3:37:12#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:12#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:12#2/r1.claim: The standard Form II causative reading makes God the agent who appoints Zakariyyā as Mary's guardian.
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:12#2/r1.anchor: Form II kaffala (causative): ""and He [God] made him [Zakariyyā] her guardian"" — standard reading

QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#1/r1.claim: The standard name form is shortened, without hamza and ending in alif maqṣūra.
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#1/r1.anchor: Standard: shortened form without hamza, ending in alif maqṣūra

QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#2/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#2/r1.claim: The extended form adds hamza and ḍamma, with nominative case marking.
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#2/r1.anchor: Extended with hamza and ḍamma: full Arabic morphological adaptation with nominative case marking

QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#3/r1.speaker: CE
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#3/r1.claim: The extended hamza form with fatḥa is accusative, distinguishing whether Zakariyyā is construed as subject or object of kaffala.
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:13#3/r1.anchor: Extended with hamza and fatḥa: case-marked accusative form — significant because it determines whether zakariyyā is subject or object of kaffala

QIRAAT-ER:3:37:17#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:17#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:17#1/r1.claim: The standard form of Zakariyyā's name is shortened.

QIRAAT-ER:3:37:17#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:17#2/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:17#2/r1.claim: The extended form with hamza and nominative ḍamma fits Zakariyyā's role as subject of dakhala.
QIRAAT-ER:3:37:17#2/r1.anchor: Extended with hamza and ḍamma: nominative, consistent with subject-of-dakhala role

IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p579/r3.claim: Ibn Hisham glosses kafalaha as taking her into one's care.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p120/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p120/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p120/r1.claim: Qatāda says the provision Mary found was fruit appearing out of season.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p120/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وجد عندها رزقا ﴾ قال وجد عندها ثمرة في غير زمانها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r8.claim: Kafala originally means guarantee; it is extended metaphorically to taking someone in and caring for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r8.anchor: الكفالة: الضمان، يقال: كفل يكفل فهو كافل وكفيل، هذا أصله ثم يستعار للضم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r9.claim: Zakariya has long and short forms in Hijazi usage, both diptote when indefinite; Abu Hatim wrongly attributes the restriction simply to foreignness and proper-name status, which would permit declension when indefinite.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r9.anchor: زكريا: أعجمي شبه بما فيه الألف الممدودة والألف المقصورة فهو ممدود ومقصور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r10.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r10.claim: Abu Ali explains Najdi dhikray, with final y and tanwin, as a declinable form made by dropping the original ending letters and adding the nisba yāʾ; al-Akhfash also reports a form dhakar like ʿUmar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r10.anchor: وهي لغة نجد، ووجهه فيما قال أبو علي: إنه حذف ياءي الممدود والمقصور، وألحقه ياءي النسب يدل على ذلك صرفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r11.claim: Abu Ubayda defines miḥrab as the foremost, noblest seats, including the distinguished place in a mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r11.anchor: المحراب: قال أبو عبيدة: سيد المجالس وأشرفها ومقدمها، وكذلك هو من المسجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r12.speaker: الأصمعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p106/r12.claim: Al-Asmaʿi glosses miḥrab as an upper chamber or room.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r1.claim: Al-Asmaʿi's definition of miḥrab as a chamber is supported by a poetic line describing chambers of rulers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines miḥrab as a lofty, noble place.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r3.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala defines miḥrab as a palace because of its height and nobility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: القصر، لشرفه وعلوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r4.claim: Other glosses identify the miḥrab as a mosque or as its customary place of prayer leadership, named for people's competition over it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p107/r4.anchor: وقيل: المسجد. وقيل: محرابه المعهود سمي بذلك لتحارب الناس عليه وتنافسهم فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the expected wording would be بتقبل حسن, but قبول is used as the verbal noun in قبلها قبولا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: الأصل فتقبلها بتقبل حسن، ولكن قبول محمول على: قبلها قبولا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r3.claim: The regular verbal-noun pattern would have ḍamma like دخول and خروج, but the attested form has fatḥa; al-Farraʾ and al-Zajjaj also allow ḍamma, as Ibn al-Aʿrabi transmits.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r3.anchor: والقياس فيه الضم: كالدخول والخروج، ولكنه جاء بالفتح، وأجاز الفراء والزجاج ضم القاف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains God's acceptance as guiding Mary along the path of the blessed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: معناه سلك بها طريق السعداء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r5.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r5.claim: Some explain the acceptance as God's undertaking Mary's upbringing and care.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r5.anchor: وقال قوم: تكفل بتربيتها والقيام بشأنها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says acceptance means she was never afflicted or punished at any hour, day or night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه لم يعذبها ساعة قط من ليل ولا نهار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r7.claim: These explanations take تَقَبَّل as استقبل, using تفعّل with the sense of استفعل: God received her at the outset of life.
