ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r7.anchor: وعلى هذه الأقوال يكون تقبل بمعنى استقبل، فيكون تفعل بمعنى استفعل، أي:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r8.claim: An unnamed poetic line witnesses استقبل as taking an affair at its beginning, supporting the sense that God received Mary from birth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r9.claim: Another view says God accepted Mary in the vow instead of the hoped-for boy and answered her mother's prayer; no girl had previously been accepted as a vow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r9.anchor: وقيل: المعنى فقبلها أي: رضي بها في النذر مكان الذكر في النذر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r10.claim: One grammatical view treats باء as extra, leaving قبول accusative as a verbal noun of a different root; another says the preposition is not extra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r10.anchor: والباء في: بقبول، قيل: زائدة، ويكون إذ ذاك ينتصب انتصاب المصدر على غير الصدر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r11.claim: قبول can mean the instrument or quality by which something is accepted, namely God's special selection of Mary; alternatively it is a verbal noun with a deleted noun, بذي قبول حسن.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p120/r11.anchor: والقبول اسم لما يقبل به الشيء: كالسعوط واللدود لما يسعط به ويلد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r1.claim: Good growth denotes excellent physical and moral formation: God raised Mary in obedience and worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r1.anchor: عبارة عن حسن النشأة والجودة في خلق وخلق، فأنشأها على الطاعة والعبادة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says that at nine Mary fasted by day and prayed by night, surpassing the scholars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما بلغت تسع سنين صامت النهار وقامت الليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r3.claim: One view says Mary never committed a sin.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r4.claim: Qatada says they were told Mary did not commit sins as other descendants of Adam do.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: حدثنا أنها كانت لا تصيب الذنوب كما يصيب بنو آدم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes her good growth to mean that her fruit, Jesus, was made extraordinary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r5.anchor: وقيل: معنى أنبتها نباتا حسنا أي: جعل ثمرتها مثل عيسى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r6.claim: نباتا is either a verbal noun from a different root or the verbal noun of an omitted verb, فنبتت نباتا حسنا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r6.anchor: وانتصب: نباتا، على أنه مصدر على غير الصدر، أو مصدر لفعل محذوف أي:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r7.claim: Good acceptance is also explained as nurturing Mary in purity, illustrated by her later seeking refuge from a man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r7.anchor: ويقال: القبول الحسن تربيتها على نعت العصمة حتى قالت: أعوذ بالرحمن منك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r8.claim: Good growth means steadfast obedience and preferring God's pleasure at every moment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r8.anchor: والنبات الحسن الاستقامة على الطاعة وإيثار رضا الله في جميع الأوقات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r9.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r9.claim: Qatada explains كفلها as Zechariah taking Mary into his household.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r10.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains it as Zechariah undertaking her care.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r10.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: ضمن القيام بها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r11.claim: God's good acceptance and growth included appointing a prophet as Mary's guardian and caretaker.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r11.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: ضمن القيام بها، ومن القبول الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r12.claim: A divine inspiration to David says that whoever seeks God should be served.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r12.anchor: أوحى الله إلى داود عليه السلام: إذا رأيت لي طالبا فكن له خادما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r13.speaker: الكوفيون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r13.claim: The Kufan readers geminate the fāʾ in وكفّلها, while the other seven readers pronounce it light.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r13.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون: وكفلها، بتشديد الفاء، وباقي السبعة بتخفيفها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r14.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r14.anchor: وأبي: وأكفلها، ومجاهد: فتقبلها بسكون اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r15.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r15.claim: Mujahid reads فتقبلها with a still lām and ربها as a vocative, and reads أنبتها and كفلها as a supplication by Mary's mother.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r15.anchor: ومجاهد: فتقبلها بسكون اللام، ربها، بالنصب على النداء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r16.speaker: عبد الله المزني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r16.claim: ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani reads كفلها with kasra on fāʾ; the author notes كفل يكفل beside كفل يكفل as a dialectal pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r16.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله المزني: وكفلها، بكسر الفاء وهي لغة يقال: كفل يكفل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r17.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r17.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi and Hafs read Zakariyya short; the other seven lengthen it, with the languages discussed earlier.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r17.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص: زكريا، مقصورا وباقي السبعة ممدودا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r18.claim: Hanah wrapped newborn Mary, took her to the Jerusalem temple priests descended from Aaron, and presented her as the vowed child; they competed because she was their imam's daughter and their leaders' descendant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r18.anchor: لفتها في خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد فوضعتها عند الأحبار أبناء هارون،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r19.claim: The priests in Jerusalem are likened to the custodians of the Kaʿba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r19.anchor: وهم في بيت المقدس كالحجة في الكعبة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r20.claim: Zechariah claimed Mary because her maternal aunt was with him; the priests insisted they draw lots, and the group went to a river.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p121/r20.anchor: فقال لهم زكريا: أنا أحق بها، عندي خالتها. فقالوا: لا، حتى نقترع عليها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r1.claim: Most identify the river where the priests cast their pens as the Jordan; another view says it was a nearby spring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r1.anchor: قيل: هو نهر الأردن وهو قول الجمهور. وقيل: في عين ماء كانت هناك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r2.claim: In one account, Zechariah's pen floated while the others sank, so he became Mary's guardian.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r2.anchor: فارتفع قلم زكريا ورسبت أقلامهم فتكفلها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says Mary was wet-nursed but never latched onto a breast.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r3.anchor: قيل: واسترضع لها. وقال الحسن: لم تلتقم ثديا قط.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r4.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r4.claim: ʿIkrima's account says the pens went into the water and Zechariah's pen swam against its current.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: ألقوا أقلامهم فجرى قلم زكريا عكس جرية الماء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r5.claim: Another account says the pens floated downstream while Zechariah's stayed upright as if fixed in clay.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r5.anchor: وقيل: عامت مع الماء معروضة، وبقي قلم زكريا واقفا كأنما ركز في طين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Zechariah married Mary's maternal aunt, and the two brothers-in-law married sisters: Zechariah's wife bore John and Imran's wife bore Mary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r6.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: إن زكريا كان تزوج خالتها لأنه وعمران كانا سلفين على أختين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r7.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r7.claim: Al-Suddi and others say Zechariah married another daughter of Imran; the report is supported by the Prophet's description of John and Jesus as maternal cousins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r7.anchor: وقال السدي، وغيره: كان زكريا تزوج ابنة أخرى لعمران.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r8.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r8.claim: The Prophet calls John and Jesus ابنا الخالة, supporting the account that their fathers married sisters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r8.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في يحيى وعيسى: ابنا الخالة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r9.claim: One view says Zechariah took charge because Mary's mother died and her father had died while she was still in the womb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r9.anchor: وقيل: إنما كفلها لأن أمها هلكت، وكان أبوها قد هلك وهي في بطن أمها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r10.claim: Another view makes Zechariah her paternal cousin and says her sister was his wife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r10.anchor: وقيل: كان زكريا ابن عمها وكانت أختها تحته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r11.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r11.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts a later famine: after Mary grew, Zechariah could not afford her upkeep, so they drew lots for who would finance her and Jureij won.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r11.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ترعرعت وأصاب بني إسرائيل مجاعة، فقال لهم زكريا: إني قد عجزت عن إنفاق مريم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r12.claim: That later lottery concerned paying her expenses, whereas the earlier one chose her guardian; on this account Zechariah cared for her from infancy without a lot.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r12.anchor: وهذا استهام غير الأول، هذا المراد منه دفعها للإنفاق عليها، والأول المراد منه: أخذها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r13.claim: The common account is that Zechariah became Mary's guardian by lot; the Qur'an names no other guardian, and he was the best choice as close paternal kin, related by marriage and a prophet protected from sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r13.anchor: والذي عليه الناس أن زكريا إنما كفلها بالاستهام، ولم يدل القرآن على أن غير زكريا كفلها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r14.claim: Zechariah is identified as son of Adhan son of Muslim, from Solomon and David's descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r14.anchor: وزكريا هو ابن أذن بن مسلم من ولد سليمان بن داود عليهم السلام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r15.speaker: أبو البركات الجواني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r15.claim: The genealogist Abu al-Barakat al-Juwani instead places John, Elisha, Elijah and Ezra among Aaron's descendants; then Zechariah is not Solomon's descendant or Mary's cousin, since Mary descends from Solomon of Judah, while Moses and Aaron descend from Levi.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p122/r15.anchor: وذكر النقيب أبو البركات الجواني النسابة: أن يحيى بن زكريا، واليسع، وإلياس، والعزير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Zechariah placed Mary with her maternal aunt, John's mother, until she matured, then built her a raised sanctuary room accessible only by a ladder.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ضمها إلى خالتها أم يحيى حتى إذا شبت وبلغت مبلغ النساء بنى لها محرابا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r2.claim: One account says Zechariah shut seven doors when he left; Muqatil says he locked her door and kept the key, bringing her home during menstruation and returning her after purification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r2.anchor: وقيل: كان يغلق عليها سبعة أبواب إذا خرج. قال مقاتل: كان يغلق عليها الباب ومعه المفتاح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r3.claim: Another view says Mary was purified from menstruation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r4.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وقتادة والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r4.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatada and al-Suddi say Zechariah found winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد، والضحاك، وقتادة، والسدي: وجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r5.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says Mary spoke in the cradle, never suckled, and received her food from Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: تكلمت في المهد ولم تلقم ثديا قط، وإنما كانت يأتيها رزقها من الجنة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r6.claim: A sound hadith names three who spoke as infants: Jesus, the companion of Jurayj, and the son of the woman; a rare route adds the child of the Ditch, making Mary's inclusion especially anomalous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r6.anchor: والذي ورد في الصحيح أن الذي تكلم في المهد ثلاثة: عيسى، وصاحب جريج، وابن المرأة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r7.claim: A rare transmission adds the companion of the Ditch among infant speakers; the author finds it particularly strange that Mary is counted with them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r7.anchor: وورد من طريق شاذ: صاحب الأخدود. والأغرب أن مريم منهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r8.claim: One account identifies Jureij as carpenter Yusuf ibn Yaʿqub, Mary's cousin; when Zechariah could not care for her, Jureij brought small amounts from his earnings that grew plentiful, prompting Zechariah to ask her about them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r8.anchor: وقيل: كان جريح النجار، واسمه يوسف بن يعقوب، وكان ابن عم مريم حين كفلها بالقرعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r9.claim: The Jureij account implies the provision episode occurred after Mary grew, which Abu Hayyan considers the likelier chronology.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r9.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن ذلك كان بعد أن كبرت وهو الأقرب للصواب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r10.claim: Another view says Mary's food came from outside their region; Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jubayr and Mujahid identify it as grapes in a basket though grapes did not grow there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان عنبا في مكتل ولم يكن في تلك البلاد عنب، وقاله ابن جبير، ومجاهد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r11.claim: Another explanation is that a righteous person brought Mary the food.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r11.anchor: وقيل: كان بعض الصالحين يأتيها بالرزق.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r12.claim: The verse's apparent sense is that Zechariah alone fostered her; God relieved him of the cost of her food and the strain of seeking it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r12.anchor: والذي يدل عليه ظاهر الآية أن الذي كفلها بالتربية هو زكريا لا غيره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r13.claim: كلما implies repetition, showing Zechariah frequently visited and checked on Mary's circumstances.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r13.anchor: و: كلما، تقتضي التكرار، فيدل على كثرة تعهده وتفقده لأحوالها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r14.claim: The wording indicates food was present whenever Zechariah entered, nourishment he did not recognize and had not brought himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r14.anchor: ودلت الآية على وجود الرزق عندها كل وقت يدخل عليها، والمعنى: أنه غذاء يتغذى به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r15.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r15.claim: Al-Raghib says رزق can also mean knowledge and wisdom bestowed without human teaching, though Abu Hayyan deems that remote and akin to esoteric exegesis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123/r15.anchor: وأبعد من فسر الرزق هنا بأنه فيض كان يأتيها من الله من العلم والحكمة من غير تعليم آدمي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r1.claim: Zechariah was surprised that food he had not brought appeared repeatedly and asked how it reached Mary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r1.anchor: استغرب زكريا وجود الرزق عندها وهو لم يكن أتى به، وتكرر وجوده عندها كلما دخل عليها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r2.claim: أنى may ask how, where or when; Abu Hayyan prefers a question about the source or direction, while allowing a question about how the food came.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r2.anchor: و: أنى، سؤال عن الكيفية وعن المكان وعن الزمان، والأظهر أنه سؤال عن الجهة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r3.claim: Abu ʿUbayda glosses أنى as من أين, from where.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r3.anchor: ولذلك قال أبو عبيدة: معناه من أين؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r4.claim: Al-Kumayt's line uses أنى with من أين, providing poetic evidence for that sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r4.anchor:
وقال الكميت:
أنى ومن أين أتاك الطرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r5.claim: Mary's answer means no human brought the food; God continuously provides it, reassuring Zechariah that no one has preempted his care and that Mary has a special station.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r5.anchor: ظاهره أنه لم: يأت به آدمي ألبتة، بل هو رزق يتعهدني به الله تعالى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r6.claim: One view says the extraordinary provision resulted from Zechariah's prayer and was therefore a special sign for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r6.anchor: وهذا الخارق العظيم، قيل: هو بدعوة زكريا لها بالرزق، فيكون من خصائص زكريا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r7.claim: Another view says the provision established the prophethood of Mary's future son Jesus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: كان تأسيسا لنبوة ولدها عيسى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan says both explanations resemble Muʿtazilite denials of miracles for nonprophets; the event is instead Mary's own karāma, since Zechariah's question rules out a sign he himself arranged and Jesus was not yet born.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r8.anchor: والظاهر أنها كرامة خص الله بها مريم، ولو كان خارقا لأجل زكريا لم يسأل عنه زكريا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj connects the extraordinary provision with God's description of Mary and her son as a sign for all worlds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج: وهذا الخارق من الآية التي قال تعالى: وجعلناها وابنها آية للعالمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r10.speaker: الجبائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r10.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi allows that it was Zechariah's miracle: he may have prayed generally for Mary's provision without tracking details, or asked whether a person had brought it improperly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p123#2/r10.anchor: وقال الجبائي: يجوز أن يكون من معجزات زكريا، دعا لها على الإجمال لأن يوصل لها رزقها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan takes إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب as Mary's speech; al-Tabari instead takes it as God's address to Muhammad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r1.anchor: والظاهر أنها من كلام مريم وقال الطبري: ليس من كلام مريم، وأنه خبر من الله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r2.speaker: جابر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r2.claim: Jabir reports that bread and meat multiplied miraculously for Fatima; when asked, she said it came from God, and the Prophet praised God and likened her to Israel's leading woman.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r2.anchor: وروى جابر حديثا مطولا فيه تكثير الخبز واللحم على سبيل خرق العادة لفاطمة بنت رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r11.claim: The passage uses paronomasia in فتقبلها بقبول, أنبتها نباتا and رزقا ويرزق.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r11.anchor: والتجنيس المغاير في: فتقبلها ربها بقبول، وأنبتها نباتا، وفي: رزقا ويرزق.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r12.claim: The explicit wording هو من عند الله signifies that only God could bring this timely food.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r12.anchor: والإشارة، وهو أن يعبر باللفظ الظاهر عن المعنى الخفي، في قوله: هو من عند الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r13.claim: Indefinite رزقا suggests provision of varied and abundant kinds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r13.anchor: وفي قوله: رزقا، أتى به منكرا مشيرا إلى أنه ليس من جنس واحد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r14.claim: The passage contains ellipses at several locations, with some meanings intelligible only when omitted material is supplied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p124/r14.anchor: والحذف في عدة مواضع لا يصح المعنى إلا باعتبارها.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r1.claim: God accepted Maryam as the vowed offering in place of the expected boy, likening the vow to a gift and divine approval to receiving it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r1.anchor: أى رضى بمريم فى النذر مكان الذكر ففيه تشبيه النذر بالهدية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r2.claim: The pronoun most properly refers to Maryam’s Lord, who brought her to the perfection fitting her.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r2.anchor: رب مريم المبلغ لها إلى كما لها اللائق بها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r3.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun as Hanna, since she was the one who spoke and called, ‘My Lord, I have delivered her.’
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r3.anchor: وقيل : الضمير لامرأة عمران بدليل أنها التى خاطبت ونادت بقولها ( رب إني وضعتها )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r4.claim: Qabūl can denote the means by which something is accepted, just as suʿūṭ and ladūd name what is used for nasal or oral administration.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r4.anchor: و القبول ما يقبل به الشئ كالسعوط واللدود ما يسعط به

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r5.claim: A good acceptance means God uniquely honored her to stand in for a male dedication, or received her from her mother at birth before she was ready for service.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r5.anchor: تقبلها بوجه حسن تقبل به النذائر وهو اختصاصه سبحانه إياها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that Hanna, fearing a girl could not be consecrated, placed Maryam by the Jerusalem priests; after successive lots with writing pens and pens thrown in the Jordan, Zakariya’s pen prevailed and he took her.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r6.anchor: فقد روى عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال : لما وضعتها خشيت حنة أن لا تقبل الأنثى محرر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r7.claim: The bāʾ may indicate association, with qabūl a verbal noun and an omitted complement: she was accepted in a state worthy of approval.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الباء للملابسة و القبول مصدر وهو من المصادر الشاذة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r8.claim: Tafaʿʿala may function like istafʿala here, so the phrase means God received and welcomed her from her first moment of life.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تفعل بمعنى استفعل كتعجل بمعنى استعجل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r9.claim: On that reading God showed a special karāma in Maryam from birth.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r10.claim: A further analysis treats the bāʾ as extra and qabūlan as an emphatic verbal noun, with the unusual form conveying complete approval and solicitude.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r10.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الباء زائدة و القبول مصدر مؤكد للفعل السابق بحذف الزوائد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r11.claim: The form tafaʿʿala ordinarily suggests effort against the agent’s nature; for God it conveys the resulting power and abundance of the act.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r11.anchor: فان صيغة التفعل مشعرة بحسب أصل الوضع بالتكلف وكون الفعل على خلاف طبع الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r12.claim: A remote reading makes the bāʾ mean ‘with’: God accepted the vow alongside Hanna’s prayer for Maryam and her descendants to be protected from Satan throughout life.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p138/r12.anchor: ويحتمل على بعد بعيد أن تكون الباء للمصاحبة بمعنى مع أى تقبل نذرها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the good growth as raising Maryam in worship and obedience to her Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r1.anchor: قاله ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما وفي رواية عنه أنه سوى خلقها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r2.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says Maryam’s form was made proportionate and she grew in one day as much as others grow in a year.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r2.anchor: وفي رواية عنه أنه سوى خلقها فكانت تشب في يوم ما يشب غيرها في عام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r3.claim: Another explanation is that God cared for her in every circumstance, figuratively like a gardener watering, protecting, and clearing weeds from a crop.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r3.anchor: وقيل : تعهدها بما يصلحها في سائر أحوالها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r4.claim: The care image is either a representational metaphor or a metonymy based on necessary association with tending a crop.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r4.anchor: فقي الكلام استعارة تمثيلية أو مجاز مرسل بعلاقة اللزوم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r5.claim: Nabatan is a verbal noun unlike the verb’s form and substitutes for inbāt.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r5.anchor: و ( نباتا ) هنا مصدر على غير لفظ الفعل المذكور وهو نائب عن إنبات

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r6.claim: Alternatively, the implied wording is ‘she grew with good growth’; nabāt and nabt are synonymous and may also refer to the plant itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r6.anchor: وقيل : التقدير فنبتت نباتا والنبات والنبت بمعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r7.claim: Zakariya was descended from Solomon son of David.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r7.anchor: على ما ذكر فى حديث ابن عباس وكل ذلك من آثار قدرته تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r8.claim: God brought Maryam to Zakariya and made him her guardian and guarantor of her interests, as in the Ibn Abbas report; this was divine power, not revelation to Zakariya.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r8.anchor: أى ضمها الله تعالى إليه وجعله كافلا لها وضامنا لمصالحها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r9.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and ʿAsim (except Ibn ʿAyyash’s transmission) geminate the fāʾ and shorten Zakariyyā, making him the object of ‘entrusted.’
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r9.anchor: وقرأ بتشديد الفاء حمزة والكسائي وعاصم وقصروا ( زكريا ) غير عاصم في رواية ابن عياش

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r10.claim: The other readers lighten the fāʾ, lengthen Zakariyyā, and place him in the nominative as the subject; two further name forms occur, with or without a final yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r10.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بتخفيف الفاء ومدوا ( زكريا ) ورفعوه على الفاعلية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r11.claim: Zakariyyā is indeclinable because it is a proper foreign name; another explanation is that it ends in the feminine alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r11.anchor: ومنعه من التصرف للعلمية والعجمة وقيل : لألف التأنيث

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r12.speaker: أبيّ
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r12.claim: Ubayy reads wa-akfalahā, ‘and He entrusted her to Zakariya.’

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r13.claim: Mujahid reads all three verbs as prayers, with rabbahā as a vocative: ‘Accept her, Lord; nurture her; appoint Zakariya her guardian.’
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r13.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد فتقبلها ربها وأنبتها وكفلها على صيغة الدعاء في الافعال الثلاثة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r14.claim: On Mujahid’s prayer reading, God answered Hanna’s requests in all three clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r14.anchor: وقد استجاب الله تعالى دعاءها في جميع ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r15.claim: The majority, supported by reports, say Zakariya cared for Maryam from the beginning; the claim that he took her only after weaning is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r15.anchor: والذي عليه الاكثرون وشهدت له الاخبار أن كفالة زكريا كانت من أول أمرها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r16.claim: The repeated-entry clause explains the acceptance just described and is therefore not joined with a conjunction.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r16.anchor: كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب بيان لقبولها ولهذا لم يعطف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the miḥrāb as Maryam’s room in Jerusalem, with a central doorway that could be reached only by a stair, like the Kaaba’s door.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r17.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي اللهع تعالى عنهما غرفة بنيت لها في بيت المقدس

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r18.claim: Others understand miḥrāb as a mosque, since their mosques were called miḥrābs.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r18.anchor: وقيل : المراد به المسجد إذ قد كانت مساجدهم تسمى المحاريب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r19.claim: Another view takes it as the mosque’s most honored front area, the imam’s place according to one opinion.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r19.anchor: وقيل : أشرف مواضعه ومقدمها وهو مقام الامام من المسجد في رأى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r20.claim: Miḥrāb may be a place-name from the emphatic pattern mifʿāl because worshippers battle their selves there, fight Satan, or compete for it; a Maghribi poet praises courage and humility with the term.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r20.anchor: وأصله مفعال صيغة مبالغة كمطعان م فسمى به المكان لان المحاربين نفوسهم كثيرون فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r21.claim: Placing the adverbial phrase before the subject highlights special concern for Maryam.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r21.anchor: وتقديم الظرف على الفاعل لاظهار كمال العناية بأمرها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r22.claim: Miḥrāb is accusative by broadening the construction, although dakhala normally takes a preposition such as bi or ilā.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139/r22.anchor: ونصب ( المحراب ) على التوسع إذ حق الفعل أن يتعدى بفئ أو بالى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r1.claim: The overt subject is said to separate the clause.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r2.claim: Kullamā is a temporal adverb: mā is either a verbal noun with ‘time’ omitted or an indefinite relative with its antecedent deleted; the answer clause governs it by consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r2.anchor: و ( كلما ) ظرف على أن ( ما ) مصدرية والزمان محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r3.claim: Some mistakenly make the protasis itself govern kullamā as semantically more fitting; al-Alusi says this needlessly adds extra pieces to the construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r3.anchor: ومن الناس من وهم فقال : إن ناصبه فعل الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r4.claim: Wajada means Zakariya found or encountered sustenance there, or found it present in her vicinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r4.anchor: أى أصاب ولقى بحضرتها ذلك أو ذلك كائنا بحضرتها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r5.speaker: الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from al-Zubayr that only Zakariya entered her; after he left, seven doors stood between them, yet he found summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r5.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن الزبير قال : إنه كان لا يدخل عليها غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r6.claim: The indefinite tanwīn in rizqan magnifies the sustenance.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sustenance consisted of fruits from Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r7.anchor: فعن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن ذلك من أثمار الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r8.claim: The majority say it compensated Maryam for nursing, since she never nursed at a breast.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r8.anchor: والذي عليه الجل أن ذلك عوض لها عن الرضاعة فقد روى أنها لم ترضع ثديا قط

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r9.claim: A report from Ibn Bishr via Ibn Abbas places this after Maryam was weaned at two: Zakariya hired a wet nurse, then left her alone behind a closed miḥrāb door and alone checked on her.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r9.anchor: ففي رواية ابن بشر عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عايهما أن زكريا عليه الصلاة والسلام استأجر لها ظئرا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r10.claim: ‘He said, Maryam’ begins an explanatory resumption.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r10.anchor: قال يمريم ( استئناف بياني ( أنى لك هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r11.claim: Zakariya asks where this sustenance came from, since it was unlike worldly food and the doors were shut around her.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r11.anchor: أى من أين لك هذا الرزق الذى لا يشبه أرزاق الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r12.claim: An alternative takes annā to ask ‘how?’ rather than ‘from where?’; two cited lines of poetry witness the respective senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r12.anchor: ومجئ ( أنى ) بمعنى من أين أو كيف تقدم الكلام عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r13.claim: The preposition min is omitted from annā, as fī is omitted with inherently locative adverbs; frequent adverbial usage permits this deletion.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r13.anchor: وحذف حرف الجر من ( أنى ) نحو حذف في من الظروف اللازمة للظرفية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r14.claim: More generally, locatives allow deletion of their common linking preposition; omission of other prepositions is limited to indeclinable adverbs because they rank below fī.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r14.anchor: والتحقيق أن الظروف محل التوسع لكثرة استعمالهم إياها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r15.claim: The extraordinary provision proves that karāmāt for saints are possible, since Maryam was not a prophet according to the majority; Sunnis and Shiʿites accept this, while Muʿtazilites deny it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r15.anchor: واستدل بالآية على جواز الكرامة للأولياء لأن مريم لا نبوة لها على المشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r16.speaker: البلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r16.claim: Al-Balkhi answers that the provision was an irhāṣ, a precursor to Jesus’ prophethood.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r16.anchor: وأجاب البلخي منهم عن الآية بأن ذلك كان إرهاصا وتأسيسا لنبوة عيسى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r17.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r17.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī instead says the provision was a miracle for Zakariya.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r17.anchor: وأجاب الجبائى ي بأنه كان معجزة لزكريا عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r18.claim: Al-Alusi objects that Zakariya’s apparent uncertainty sits poorly with al-Jubbāʾī’s miracle claim; the wording need not imply real confusion and may simply display Maryam’s wonder, while confusion about the food’s source does not rescue the claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p139#2/r18.anchor: ورد الأخير بأن اشتباه الامر عليه يأبى ذلك ولعله مبني على الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r1.claim: ‘She said’ begins a resumption, as did the preceding ‘He said.’

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r2.claim: One view takes Maryam’s answer to mean that the food came from Paradise.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r3.claim: Another reading means God provided it without human mediation, so there is no reason to marvel or deem it impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r3.anchor: وقيل : مما رزقنيه هو لا بواسطة البشر فلا تعجب ولا تستبعد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r4.claim: A view says Maryam spoke while still a child, as Jesus did; al-Suyuti’s poem names eleven infants or children reported to have spoken.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r4.anchor: وقيل : تكلمت بذلك صغيرة كعيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام وقد جمع من تكلم كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r5.speaker: جلال الدين السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r5.claim: Al-Suyuti’s list includes the Prophet, Yahya, Jesus, Abraham, Maryam, the witness in Joseph’s story, the child of the ditch, the infant who spoke about a nursing woman, and the child of Pharaoh’s hairdresser; it ends with a child in al-Hadi’s time.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r5.anchor: وقد نظمهم الجلال السيوطي فقال : تكلم في المهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r6.claim: The inward reading turns toward a servant marked by the station of servitude and wholly devoted to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r6.anchor: أو بمن اتصف بمقام العبودية وانقطع اليه بالكلية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r7.claim: The perfected lover is described through the command to follow the Prophet, the foremost of lovers, so that God will love the follower.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r7.anchor: ( قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني ) لاني سيد المحبين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r8.claim: Love’s reality is a heart consumed by longing, a spirit relishing love, senses immersed in intimacy, a purified soul, vision of the Beloved through all, and absorption beyond both worlds.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r8.anchor: وحقيقة المحبة عند العارفين احتراق القلب بنيران الشوق وروح الروح بلذة العشق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r9.claim: Love’s practical branch is conforming to all the Beloved’s wishes, receiving trials with contentment and surrender, remaining faithful, and following the Prophet’s Sunna.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r9.anchor: وأما فرعها فهو موافقة المحبوب في جميع ما يرضاه وتقبل بلائه بنعت الرضا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r10.claim: Its proper manners are leaving even permitted pleasures, keeping to seclusion and watchfulness, receiving intimations of divine attributes, and humility in every movement.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r10.anchor: وأما آدابها فالانقطاع عن الشهوات واللذات المباحة والسكون في الخلوات

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r11.claim: True love follows inner witnessing of divine beauty; love prompted by gifts is defective, since the Beloved’s essence alone should be its cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r11.anchor: لان المحبة متى كانت من تولد رؤية النعماء كانت معلولة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r12.claim: The lover does not distinguish Paradise from fire, joy from hardship, or obligation from Sunna; true love forgets all else and is absorbed in the Beloved.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r12.anchor: لا تصبح المحبة ممن يميز بين النار والجنة وبين السرور والمحنة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r13.claim: Poetry describes longing as love’s companion and compares divine love to a spark that neither flares nor dies; love must seize the whole self.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r13.anchor: يقولون إن الحب كالنار في الحشا ألا كذبوا فالنار تذكو وتخمد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r14.claim: The first kind is ordinary love from noticing a benefactor’s favors; it changes and belongs to workers who seek reward, as Abu al-Tayyib’s verse says.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r14.anchor: القسم الاول محبة العوام وهى مطالعة المنة من روية إحسان المحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r15.claim: The second kind is the elite’s love from reverence for God as worthy of love; it endures because beauty and majesty endure, as the report about Suhayb and Rabiʿa’s couplet illustrate.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r15.anchor: القسم الثاني ( محبة الخواص المتبعين للاخلاق الذين يحبونه إجلالا وإعظاما

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r16.claim: The third kind arises in the elect through divine attraction and perfect gnosis; it annihilates the lover’s self, leaving the person bewildered and intoxicated, neither living nor dead.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r16.anchor: والقسم الثالث ( محبة خواص المتبعين للاحوال وهي الناشئة من الجذبة الآلهية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r17.claim: The sounds of ḥāʾ and bāʾ hint that love must seize heart, speech, inner and outer self before it deserves the name.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r17.anchor: ويكفي في شرح الحب لفظة فانه : حاء وباء والحاء من حروف الحلق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r18.claim: God’s love for servants also differs by recipient: for ordinary people it appears in granting provision to whom He wills without reckoning.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p140/r18.anchor: وأما محبة ربه سبحانه له فمختلفة أيضا وإن صدرت من محل واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r1.claim: The closing statement has already been explained and gives the reason Maryam said the sustenance was from God.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r1.anchor: تقدم معناه والجملة تعليل لكونه من عند الله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r2.claim: The apparent reading makes the closing statement Maryam’s words, included within what she said.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r2.anchor: والظاهر أنها من كلام مريم فحينئذ تكون في محل داخله تحت القول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r3.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r3.claim: Al-Tabari says the closing words are God’s narration to the Prophet, not Maryam’s speech; al-Alusi prefers the apparent reading that she said them.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r3.anchor: وقال الطبري : إنها ليست من كلامها بل هي من كلامه تعالى إخبارا لنبيه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r4.speaker: جابر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r4.claim: Abu Yaʿla transmits from Jabir that the Prophet went several days without food; Fāṭima had nothing when he visited, but a neighbor sent two loaves and meat, which she reserved for him despite her family’s hunger.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r4.anchor: وقد أخرج أبو يعلي عن جابر أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أقام أياما لم يطعم طعاما

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r5.speaker: جابر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r5.claim: The food miraculously filled Fāṭima’s bowl; she cited the same words as Maryam, and the Prophet praised her resemblance to the chief of Israel’s women, then shared the meal with his family and distributed its remainder.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142/r5.anchor: فلما نظرت اليها بهتت وعرفت أنها بركة من الله تعالى فحمدت الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r23.speaker: الواسطي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r23.claim: Al-Wasiti interprets Maryam’s good acceptance as her being protected from creatures’ perception.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r23.anchor: قال الواسطي : محفوظ عن إدراك الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r24.claim: Her good growth is being watered by the waters of divine power and made fruitful as a tree of prophethood.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r24.anchor: حيث سقاها من مياه القدرة وأثمرها شجرة النبوة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r25.claim: Zakariya’s guardianship reflects the purity of his inward secret and the attraction of like to like.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r25.anchor: لطهارة سره وشبيه السئ منجذب إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r26.claim: The inward sustenance is spiritual knowledge, realities, sciences, and wisdoms flowing from God; the phrase ‘with Him’ marks it as nobler than bodily food.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p142#2/r26.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد الرزق الروحاني من المعارف والحقائق والعلوم والحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the provision found with Mary as knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال رزقا أي علما

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r7.claim: God's good acceptance represents His choosing Mary for the outpouring of His lights.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r7.anchor: وهو اختصاصه إياها بإفاضة أنواره عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r8.claim: Her good growth is a pure ascent through the stages of completion, unimpeded by obstacles or attachments.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r8.anchor: ورقاها فيما تكمل به نشأتها ترقيا حسنا غير مشوب بالعوائق والعلائق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r9.anchor: الاستعداد ( كلما دخل عليها زكريا ) وتوجه نحوها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r10.claim: Zakariya's entering represents turning toward her in her worship niche, built in the heart's sanctified house.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r10.anchor: في محراب تعبدها المبني لها في بيت مقدس القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r11.claim: The provision is nourishment for spirits in the realm of the unseen dominion.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r11.anchor: تتغذى به الأرواح في عالم الملكوت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r12.claim: Mary's answer means the great provision flows from God, beyond the reach of intellectual thought.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r12.anchor: هو مفاض من عند الله منزه عن الحمل بيد الافكار

ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r13.claim: God gathers the attributes of beauty and majesty, bestows knowledge according to each recipient's capacity, and gives without measure.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p143/r13.anchor: الجامع لصفات الجمال والجلال ( يرزق من يشاء ) ويفيض عليهم من علمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r1.claim: God accepted Mary from Hanna in place of the male child expected for temple service; acceptance means receiving and approving.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r1.anchor: أي تقبل الله مريم من حنة مكان المحرر، وتقبل بمعنى قبل ورضي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r2.claim: Another explanation takes acceptance to mean undertaking her upbringing and care.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r2.anchor: وقيل: معنى التقبل التكفل في التربية والقيام بشأنها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r3.claim: Qabul is the verbal noun of accepting; the source compares it with the uncommon forms wuluʿ and wuzaʿ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r3.anchor: والقبول مصدر قبل يقبل قبولا مثل الولوع والوزوع ولم يأت غير هذه الثلاثة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r4.claim: The wording uses an unmatching verbal noun: God made her grow, and she grew well.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r4.anchor: معناه: وأنبتها فنبتت نباتا حسنا وقيل هذا مصدر على غير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r5.claim: Juwaybir reports from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that God led Mary along the path of the blessed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r5.anchor: وقال جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r6.claim: Another explanation says her body was formed evenly, without excess or deficiency, and she grew in one day what an infant ordinarily grows in a year.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r6.anchor: يعني سوى خلقها من غير زيادة ولا نقصان فكانت تنبت في اليوم ما ينبت المولود في العام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r7.claim: Hanna wrapped Mary and brought her to the temple priests, Aaron’s descendants who managed the sanctuary; they competed to care for her because she was the daughter of their leader and offerer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r7.anchor: أخذت حنة مريم حين ولدتها فلفتها في خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد فوضعتها عند الأحبار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r8.claim: Zakariya claimed her because he had her maternal aunt; the priests instead proposed casting lots, and twenty-nine men went to a flowing river.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r8.anchor: فقال لهم زكريا: أنا أحقكم بها، عندي خالتها، فقالت له الأحبار: لا نفعل ذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r9.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r9.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the river as the Jordan; the pens were cast in water, and whoever’s pen stayed and rose was to have first claim.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r9.anchor: قال السدي: هو نهر الأردن فألقوا أقلامهم في الماء على أن من ثبت قلمه في الماء فصعد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r10.claim: One account says each pen bore the name of one of the competing priests.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r10.anchor: وقيل: كان على كل قلم اسم واحد منهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r11.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31/r11.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others say the priests cast the pens with which they wrote the Torah; Zakariya’s pen stood and rose above the water while the others sank.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r1.claim: One account says Zakariya’s pen ran upstream while the other pens followed the water’s course.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: جرى قلم زكريا مصعدا إلى أعلى الماء وجرت أقلامهم بجري الماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r2.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi and others instead say Zakariya’s pen stood upright in the water as if in clay, while the others flowed with the current; he won the lot.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r2.anchor: وقال السدي وجماعة: بل ثبت قلم زكريا وقام فوق الماء كأنه في طين، وجرت أقلامهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r3.claim: Zakariya was the head priest and their prophet, and the lot selected him to take Mary into his care.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r3.anchor: فسهمهم وقرعهم زكريا، وكان زكريا رأس الأحبار ونبيهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r4.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r4.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and ʿAsim read the verb with a doubled f; Zakariya is accusative, with God assigning Mary to his care through the lot.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وعاصم بتشديد الفاء فيكون زكريا في محل النصب أي ضمنها الله زكريا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r5.claim: The other readers use a light f; Zakariya is nominative as the one who took Mary in and cared for her.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالتخفيف فيكون زكريا في محل الرفع أي ضمها زكريا إلى نفسه وقام بأمرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r6.claim: Zakariya is identified as son of Adhan, son of Muslim, son of Saduq, from the line of Solomon and David.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r6.anchor: وهو زكريا بن آذن بن مسلم بن صدوق، من أولاد سليمان بن داود عليهما السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r7.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r7.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from ʿAsim shorten the name Zakariya; the other readers lengthen it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم: زكريا مقصورا والآخرون يمدونه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r8.claim: After taking Mary in, Zakariya built her a house and arranged a wet nurse; Ibn Ishaq says he placed her with her aunt Umm Yahya until she matured, then built her a chamber in the mosque reached by a ladder.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r8.anchor: فلما ضم زكريا مريم إلى نفسه بنى لها، بيتا واسترضع لها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r9.claim: Mihrab can mean an upper room, the most honored and foremost place in an assembly, or a mosque.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r9.anchor: وأراد بالمحراب الغرفة، والمحراب أشرف المجالس ومقدمها، وكذلك هو من المسجد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r10.speaker: المبرد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrid says a mihrab must be elevated by a step.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r10.anchor: قال المبرد: لا يكون المحراب إلا أن يرتقى إليه بدرجة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r11.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r11.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas says Zakariya locked seven doors when he left Mary in her upper chamber.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r11.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: كان زكريا إذا خرج يغلق عليها سبعة أبواب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r12.claim: The provision was fruit appearing out of season: summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r12.anchor: أي فاكهة في غير حينها، فاكهة الصيف في الشتاء وفاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r13.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains the question as asking where the food came from.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r13.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: معناه من أين لك هذا؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r14.claim: Some object to Abu ʿUbayda: anna asks from what direction, while aina asks about a place.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r14.anchor: وأنكر بعضهم عليه، وقال: معناه من أي جهة لك هذا؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r15.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r15.claim: One explanation says Mary’s food came from the fruit of Paradise.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r16.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r16.claim: Al-Hasan says Mary never suckled; her food came from Paradise, and she spoke while still very young.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p31#2/r16.anchor: قال الحسن: حين ولدت مريم لم تلقم ثديا قط، كان يأتيها رزقها من الجنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r1.claim: God accepted Maryam as a vow in place of a boy, either by accepting her as a suitable offering or by receiving her immediately after birth before she was fit for temple service.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r1.anchor: فرضي بها في النذر مكان الذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r2.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r2.claim: A report says Hanne wrapped the newborn in cloth and brought her to the temple authorities; the priests competed for her because she was the daughter of their leader and keeper of offerings, and Zakariya claimed priority because her aunt was his wife. They drew lots with twenty-seven pens in a river; Zakariya’s floated and the others sank, so he became her guardian.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r2.anchor: روي أن حنة لما ولدتها لفتها في خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد ووضعتها عند الأحبار وقالت: دونكم هذه النذيرة، فتنافسوا فيها لأنها كانت بنت إمامهم وصاحب قربانهم، فإن بني ماثان كانت رؤوس بني إسرائيل وملوكهم فقال زكريا: أنا أحق بها، عندي خالتها فأبوا إلا القرعة، وكانوا سبعة وعشرين فانطلقوا إلى نهر فألقوا فيه أقلامهم فطفا قلم زكريا ورسبت أقلامهم فتكفلها زكريا

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r3.claim: The phrase may be a verbal noun with an implied “possessor of,” or taqabbala may mean “received” from the outset.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا على تقدير مضاف أي بذي قبول حسن، وأن يكون تقبل بمعنى استقبل كتقضي وتعجل

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r4.claim: Her good growing is a metaphor for raising her well in every condition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r4.anchor: مجاز عن تربيتها بما يصلحها في جميع أحوالها

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وعاصم
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r5.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and ʿĀṣim read the verb with a doubled fāʾ and make God the subject who appoints Zakariya as her guardian; Ibn ʿAyyāsh’s ʿĀṣim shortens Zakariya.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r5.anchor: شدد الفاء حمزة والكسائي وعاصم، وقصروا زكريا غير عاصم في رواية ابن عياش على أن الفاعل هو الله تعالى وزكريا مفعول

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r6.speaker: الباقون
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r6.claim: The other readers use a light fāʾ and lengthen Zakariyyāʾ in the nominative, making him the subject and guardian.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r7.claim: The miḥrāb is her chamber, the mosque, or its most honored front section; the name evokes a place for fighting Satan, and she was placed in the sanctuary’s noblest spot.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r7.anchor: أي الغرفة التي بنيت لها، أو المسجد، أو أشرف مواضعه ومقدمها، سمي به لأنه محل محاربة الشيطان كأنها وضعت في أشرف موضع من بيت المقدس

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r8.claim: “He found provision with her” is the response to kullamā and the verb governed by it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r9.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r9.claim: A report says Zakariya was her only visitor and locked seven doors when leaving; he found summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r9.anchor: روي: أنه كان لا يدخل عليها غيره وإذا خرج أغلق عليها سبعة أبواب، وكان يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف وبالعكس

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r10.claim: Zakariya asks where she got provision out of season when the doors were locked; this supports the possibility of a saintly marvel, not a miracle for Zakariya, since that would confuse the matter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r10.anchor: من أين لك هذا الرزق الآتي في غير أوانه والأبواب مغلقة عليك، وهو دليل جواز الكرامة للأولياء. جعل ذلك معجزة زكريا يدفعه اشتباه الأمر عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r11.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r11.claim: One view says Maryam spoke as an infant like Jesus, never nursed, and received food sent down from Paradise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r11.anchor: قيل تكلمت صغيرة كعيسى عليه السلام ولم ترضع ثديا قط وكان رزقها ينزل عليها من الجنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r12.claim: God gives without reckoning either in immeasurable abundance or gratuitously, without the recipient’s entitlement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r12.anchor: بغير تقدير لكثرته، أو بغير استحقاق تفضلا به

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r13.claim: The statement about God’s provision may be spoken by Zakariya and Maryam together or be God’s own speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r13.anchor: وهو يحتمل أن يكون من كلامهما وأن يكون من كلام الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r14.speaker: رُوي
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r14.claim: An incomplete report begins that Fatima gave the Prophet two loaves and some meat, which he brought back to her; the excerpt ends before the Prophet’s saying.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:37/r14.anchor: روي (أن فاطمة رضي الله تعالى عنها أهدت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رغيفين وبضعة لحم فرجع بها إليها وقال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r1.claim: The tafaʿʿul form echoes the mother’s request and suggests acceptance unfolding through successive stages, with blessing renewed as Mary develops.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r2.claim: Calling God her Lord and describing the acceptance as good reveals the inward grace of the answer and extends its meaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r2.anchor: وظهر سر الإجابة في قوله سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r3.claim: The form-IV verb and the verbal noun distinguish hidden nourishment and growth from the visible perfection of Mary’s bodily development.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r3.anchor: وفي ذكر الفعل من ( أفعل ) في قوله : { وأنبتها } والاسم من ( فعل )

BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r4.claim: God’s care vindicates Mary: those who slandered her lied, while those who exalted her son beyond measure fell into unbelief and excess.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r4.anchor: فلقد ضل وافترى من قذفها وبهتها , وكفر وغلا من ادعى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r5.claim: This sura’s account of Mary’s acceptance, growth, and conduct removes confusion about her and her son; repeated Qur’anic stories vary in detail to suit each sura’s purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r5.anchor: من تقبلها وإنباتها وحسن سيرتها بما نفي اللبس في أمرها وأمر ولدها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r6.claim: Since a child ordinarily needs an adult to care for her, God appointed Zakariya as Mary’s guardian.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r6.anchor: ولما كان الصغير لا بد له فيما جرت به العادة من كبير يتولى أمره قال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r7.claim: The root of kafāla conveys encompassing protection, as if the guardian surrounds the one entrusted to him like an enclosing sphere.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r7.anchor: من الكفل وهو حياطة الشيء من جميع جهاته حتى يصير عليه كالفلك الدائر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r8.claim: The reading with a doubled fāʾ indicates that God is Mary’s true guarantor through His acceptance, while Zakariya serves as His deputy.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p72/r8.anchor: وفي قراءة التشديد إنباء بأن الله سبحانه وتعالى هو في الحقيقة كفيلها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r1.claim: The miḥrāb is the front and foremost part of a house, difficult to reach without special strength and effort.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r1.anchor: هو صدر لابيت ومقدمه الذي لا يكاد يوصل إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r2.claim: The repeated visits show Zakariya checking on Mary’s needs, yet God had already supplied her with sustenance from the unseen.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r2.anchor: وفي هذه العبارة أي من أولها إلاحة لمعنى حسن كفالته وأنه كان يتفقدها عند تقدير حاجتها إلى الطعام

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r3.claim: The passage’s provision resembles the cluster of grapes found with Khubayb ibn ʿAdī al-Anṣārī; the author says many such instances occurred in this community.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r3.anchor: كما وجد عند خبيب بن عدي الأنصاري رضي الله تعالى عنه قطف العنب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r4.claim: God’s unseen provision nourishes the one He has Himself cultivated and prepares Mary to receive His spirit and Word, while shielding her from ordinary entanglements.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r4.anchor: فيجد الكفيل الحق قد عاجلها برزق من غيب بما هو سبحانه وتعالى المتولي لإنباتها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r5.claim: Although Zakariya outwardly guarded Mary, she inwardly became his guardian when God disclosed to him through her what he had not previously known.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r5.anchor: وكانت هي مثل ما كفلها كافلها ظاهرا كفلته باطنا حين أبدى الله سبحانه وتعالى له من أمره

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r6.claim: Mary’s placement in the miḥrāb signals her inward completeness; for a devoted recluse, the house itself is a sanctuary for prayer and eating.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r6.anchor: وفي تعيين محلها بالمحراب ما يليح معنى ما ذكر من رجوليتها باطنا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r7.claim: The devoted should remain present-hearted during meals as in prayer: attention at the table enables attention in worship, and vice versa.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r7.anchor: من غفل عند طعامه قلبه لم يستطع أن يحضر في صلاته قلبه , ومن حضر عند طعامه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r8.claim: The indefinite, unqualified word رزق suggests that Mary received various kinds of provision.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r8.anchor: وفي ذكر الرزق شائعا إشعار بأنها أنواع من أرزاق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r9.claim: أنى expresses Zakariya’s wonder at the provision’s unusual timing, location, and manner of arrival.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r9.anchor: كلمة أنى تشعر باستغرابه وجود ذلك الرزق من وجوه مختلفة : من جهة الزمان

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r10.claim: The pronoun هو points to the provision’s full reality rather than its individual items, describing insight of the heart rather than sight of the eye.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r10.anchor: فهو إنباء عن رؤية قلب , لا عن نظر عين لأن هو كلمة إضمار

BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r11.claim: Divine provision is ranked as customary, from God’s presence, or from His innermost presence; عند is the middle rank, beyond ordinary causes but below لدن.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p73/r11.anchor: فهي ثلاث رتب : رتبة لدنية , ورتبة عندية , ورتبة حكمية عادية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r1.claim: The account compares the unusual provision with knowledge from God’s innermost presence, Moses’ description of an astonishing act, and Solomon’s ordinary royal capacity as God’s favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r1.anchor: آتيناه رحمة من عندنا وعلمناه من لدنه علما

BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r2.claim: إمر means a wonder; provision without reckoning is continuous giving that is neither delimited nor enumerated.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r2.anchor: والإمر العجب , ولعلو رتبته عن الرتبة العادية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r3.claim: The phrase names God directly because the provision exceeds customary causal processes; calling it from one’s Lord can suggest familiar material means.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r3.anchor: ولعلو رتبته عن الرتبة العادية جرى النبأ عنه مضافا إلى الاسم العظيم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r4.claim: Repeating the name Allah signals the breadth of the event and that God may grant such provision to Zakariya and whomever He wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r4.anchor: في تجديد الاسم العظيم في النبأ إشعار باتساع النبأ وإيذان وإلاحة بأن ذلك يكون لك ولمن شاء الله

BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r5.claim: Because accounted allotments in this life entail reckoning at return, unreckoned provision heralds release from afterlife accounting; gratitude begins by recognizing that sustenance comes from God.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p75/r5.anchor: كل محسوب في الإبداء محاسب عليه في الإعادة , فكان في الرزق بغير حساب

DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r7.claim: Hinna feared a girl would not be accepted as a consecrated servant, left Mary at the temple among its readers, and they contested custody because she was the daughter of their imam.
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r7.anchor: لما وضعتها خشيت حنة أم مريم أن لا تقبل أنثى محررة فلفتها في الخرقة

DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r8.speaker: زكريا
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r8.claim: Zachariah, head of the temple scholars, claimed Mary because he was her aunt's husband; the others countered that poorer claimants or her father would be more entitled, but she was consecrated and custody would be decided by lot.
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r8.anchor: فقال زكريا - وهو رأس الأحبار - أنا آخذها وأنا أحقهم بها لأن خالتها عندي

DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r9.claim: The scholars drew lots three times with their pens; after a boy first drew Zachariah's pen, they rejected that method and agreed to cast the pens in flowing water, awarding custody to the pen that went with the current and rose.
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r9.anchor: فقرعوا ثلاث مرات بأقلامهم التي كانوا يكتبون بها الوحي {أيهم يكفل مريم}

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r1.claim: The pens were cast into the Jordan; Zachariah's pen traveled with the current and rose, and he took custody of Mary.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r1.anchor: فألقوا أقلامهم فجرى قلم زكريا مع الماء وارتفعت أقلامهم

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r2.claim: God accepted and nurtured Mary well, raising her in worship and obedience until she matured.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r2.anchor: ثم قال {فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وأنبتها نباتا حسنا} يعني رباها تربية حسنة في عبادة وطاعة

DURR-FULL:v2p181/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r3.claim: Zachariah built Mary a niche in the Jerusalem temple with a high doorway reached by a ladder, hired a wet nurse, then after weaning her at age two kept her locked away and brought her needs himself until she grew up.
DURR-FULL:v2p181/r3.anchor: وبنى لها زكريا محرابا في بيت المقدس وجعل بابه في وسط الحائط لا يصعد إليها

DURR-FULL:v2p184/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God accepted the mother's wish that Mary serve in the church and rewarded her for it; Mary's good growth was by nourishment from God.
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن} قال: تقبل من أمها ما أرادت بها الكنيسة

DURR-FULL:v2p184/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r4.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r4.claim: Al-Rabiʿ explains Zachariah's kafala as taking Mary into his care.
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r4.anchor: عن الربيع وكفلها زكريا قال: ضمها إليه

DURR-FULL:v2p184/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Zachariah found out-of-season grapes in a basket in Mary's niche; she said they came from God, leading him to hope that God could give him a child despite his old age and his wife's barrenness.
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كفلها زكريا فدخل عليها المحراب فوجد عندها رزقا عنبا في مكتل

DURR-FULL:v2p184/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r7.claim: Mujahid says Zachariah won the drawing by his pen.
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وكفلها زكريا} قال: سهمهم بقلمه

DURR-FULL:v2p184/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r8.claim: Qatada says the scholars disputed custody because Mary was their leader's daughter; they drew lots, and Zachariah, her aunt's husband, took her into his home and raised her.
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r8.anchor: عن قتادة قال: كانت مريم ابنة سيدهم وإمامهم فتشاح عليها أحبارهم

DURR-FULL:v2p184/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r9.claim: The Torah scribes used lots to choose who would teach a consecrated person; Zachariah was then their best scholar and argued for Mary because her maternal aunt was his wife.
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وناس من الصحابة إن الذين كانوا يكتبون التوراة

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r1.claim: Their account says the scholars cast their writing pens into the Jordan; Zachariah's pen stood on its points as if in clay, so he won Mary.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r1.anchor: قال: فخرجوا إلى نهر الأردن فألقوا أقلامهم التي يكتبون بها أيهم يقوم قلمه

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Zachariah placed Mary with him in his prayer niche.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وكفلها زكريا} قال: جعلها معه في محرابه

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r3.speaker: عاصم بن أبي النجود
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r3.claim: Asim read kaf-falahā with a doubled f, and read Zakariyya as lengthened, hamzated, and accusative, making him the one who took charge of Mary.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r3.anchor: عن عاصم بن أبي النجود أنه قرأها {وكفلها} مشددة {زكريا} ممدودة مهموز منصوب

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the provision as grapes in a basket, out of season.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r4.anchor: عن أبن عباس {وجد عندها رزقا} قال: مكتلا فيه عنب في غير حينه

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies Mary's provision as out-of-season grapes.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد {وجد عندها رزقا} قال: عنبا في غير زمانه

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r6.claim: In another report, Mujahid says the provision was summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {وجد عندها رزقا} قال: فاكهة الصيف في الشتاء وفاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r7.claim: In another report, Mujahid explains the provision as knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد {وجد عندها رزقا} قال: علما

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
