DURR-FULL:v2p185/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the provision was fruit from Paradise, including summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وجد عندها رزقا} قال: وجد عندها ثمار الجنة

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r9.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says Mary had fresh fruit when no one else could find any.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وجد عندها رزقا} قال: الفاكهة الغضة حين لا توجد الفاكهة عند أحد

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r10.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r10.claim: Abu Malik glosses annā as 'from where.'
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r10.anchor: عن أبي مالك {أنى} يعني من أين

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r11.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses Zachariah's question as asking who brought this to Mary.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r11.anchor: عن الضحاك {أنى لك هذا} يقول من أتاك بهذا

DURR-FULL:v2p185/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r12.speaker: جابر
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r12.claim: Jabir recounts that the hungry Prophet found no food at his wives' homes and asked Fatima, who initially had none; a neighbor later brought bread and meat, which Fatima saved for him despite her family's need, and a bowl was found miraculously full when he arrived.
DURR-FULL:v2p185/r12.anchor: عن جابر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقام أياما لم يطعم طعاما حتى شق ذلك عليه

DURR-FULL:v2p186/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p186/r1.speaker: جابر
DURR-FULL:v2p186/r1.claim: In Jabir's account, the Prophet asked Fatima where the full bowl came from; she answered that it was from God, echoing Mary's reply.
DURR-FULL:v2p186/r1.anchor: إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما رآه حمد الله وقال: من أين لك هذا يا بنية

DURR-FULL:v2p186/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p186/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p186/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says Gabriel brought Mary fruit out of season; her answer that God provides as He wills made Zachariah hope God could heal his wife and grant him a child. Three nights before Muharram ended, he bathed and implored the provider of Mary's fruit for a pious child.
DURR-FULL:v2p186/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال: لما وجد زكريا عند مريم ثمر الشتاء في الصيف وثمر الصيف في الشتاء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r1.speaker: شرحبيل بن سعد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r1.claim: Sharḥabīl b. Saʿd says God accepted the female child for the people to place in the church.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r1.anchor: سالت شرحبيل بن سعد عن قوله : فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن فقال : وقبل الله انثاهم ان يجعلوها في البيعة .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r2.claim: Qatāda reports that Mary and Jesus did not commit sins as other children of Adam do.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وانبتها نباتا حسن قال : حدثنا انهما كانا لا يصيبان الذنوب

IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r3.claim: Qatāda also reports that Jesus walked on water as on land through the certainty and sincerity God granted him.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r3.anchor: وان نبي الله عيسى عليه السلام كان يمشي على الماء كمان كان يمشى على البر مما اعطاه الله من اليقين والاخلاص

IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the people competed for Mary and Zachariah won the drawing of lots.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r4.anchor: سالت الحسن فقال : تقبلها ربها بقبول حسن ، وانبتها نباتا حسنا ، وتقارعها القوم فقرع زكريا .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says Zachariah drew lots against the others with his pen; Qatāda also reports that they cast lots to decide who would care for Mary.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد 1 قوله : وكفلها زكريا قال : ساهمهم بقلمه .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r6.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r6.claim: Al-Rabīʿ explains that Zachariah took Mary into his care.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r6.anchor: عن الربيع قوله : وكفلها زكريا يقول : ضمها اليه .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddī relates that after a dispute the people cast their writing pens into the Jordan; Zachariah's pen stood upright as if in clay, so he took Mary into his care.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r7.anchor: عن السدى قال : وكان زكريا افضلهم بومئذ ، وكان نبيهم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r8.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Zachariah cared for Mary after the death of her parents, explaining her orphan status.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p638#2/r8.anchor: قال محمد ابن اسحاق قوله : وكفلها زكريا بعد ابيها وامها يذكرها اليتم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says Zachariah placed Mary in his house while he was in the prayer chamber.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r1.anchor: عن السدى قوله : كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب قال : فجعلها زكريا معه في بيته وهو في المحراب .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r2.speaker: إبراهيم بن المهاجر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm b. al-Muhājir glosses the provision found with her as Mary herself, as the excerpt reads.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r2.anchor: عن مالك بن مغول ، عن ابراهيم بن المهاجر قوله : وجد عندها رزقا يعني : مريم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the provision as grapes in a basket, found out of season.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس وجد عندها رزقا قال : وجد عندها عنبا في مكتل في غير حينه .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says the provision consisted of winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة وجد عندها رزقا قال : فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف ، وفاكهة الصيف في الشتاء .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r5.claim: Mujāhid identifies the provision as out-of-season pomegranates and grapes; the other listed authorities are reported with this view as well.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قول الله عز وجل وجد عندها رزقا قال : الرمان والعنب في غير حينه .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r6.claim: Mujāhid gives another interpretation of the provision as knowledge or a written page containing knowledge.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p639/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد : في هذه الاية وجد عندها رزقا قال : علما أو صحفيا فيها علم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p640/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p640/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p640/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts that Mary had fresh fruit when no one else had fruit, and answered Zachariah that it came from God, who provides without measure.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p640/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : يا مريم اني لك هذا قالت : هو من عند الله فانه وجد عندها الفاكهة الغضة حين لا توجد الفاكهة عند أحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r1.claim: The response follows Mary's mother's prayer and signals how quickly it was answered; the object pronouns refer to Mary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r1.anchor: تفريع على الدعاء مؤذن بسرعة الإجابة ، وضمائر النصب لمريم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r2.claim: God accepted Mary's dedication to serve the Jerusalem sanctuary, treating her as devoted to Him although this had not previously been prescribed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r2.anchor: ومعنى تقبلها : تقبل تحريرها لخدمة بيت المقدس ، أي أقام الله مريم مقام منقطع لله تعالى ، ولم يكن ذلك مشروعا من قبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r3.claim: The باء adds emphasis: the original construction would be فتقبلها قبولا حسنا, while the added preposition makes acceptance seem like an instrument or second entity and expresses special care.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r3.anchor: الباء فيه للتأكيد ، وأصل نظم الكلام : فتقبلها قبولا حسنا ، فأدخلت الباء على المفعول المطلق ليصير كالآلة للتقبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r4.claim: God revealed the acceptance to Zachariah, appointed him Mary's guardian as one of their greatest priests, and disclosed her future sanctuary service.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r4.anchor: وقد عرف هذا القبول بوحي من الله إلى زكرياء بذلك ، وأمره بأن يكفلها زكرياء أعظم أحبارهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r5.claim: Allowing a woman to serve in the sanctuary was new and foreshadowed the messenger who would abrogate many Torah rulings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r5.anchor: ولم يكن ذلك للنساء قبلها ، وكل هذا إرهاص بأنه سيكون منها رسول ناسخ لأحكام كثيرة من التوراة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r6.claim: God raised Mary soundly in body and inner purity, figuratively comparing her growth and youth to the tender growth of a plant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r6.anchor: ومعنى : { وأنبتها نباتا حسنا } : أنشأها إنشاء صالحا ، وذلك في الخلق ونزاهة الباطن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r7.claim: نباتا is a cognate accusative of أنبت, though it is the verbal noun of نبت; this form is used for ease.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235/r7.anchor: ( ونبات ) مفعول مطلق لأنبت وهو مصدر نبت وإنما أجري على أنبت للتخفيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r1.claim: Zachariah's guardianship is listed among Mary's virtues because a foster father passes his own character and virtue to the child he raises.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r1.anchor: عد هذا في فضائل مريم ، لأنه من جملة ما يزيد فضلها لأن أبا التربية يكسب خلقه وصلاحه مرباه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r2.claim: Zachariah was an Israelite priest from the house of Abijah, a prophet who received revelation in old age and the second Israelite prophet of that name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r2.anchor: وزكرياء كاهن إسرائيلي اسمه زكرياء من بني أبيا بن باكر بن بنيامين من كهنة اليهود ، جاءته النبوءة في كبره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r3.speaker: إنجيل لوقا
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r3.claim: Luke names Zachariah's wife Elisabeth, a descendant of Aaron, and says she was Mary's relative; Ibn Ashur rejects the claim that she was Mary's sister and says she was likely her aunt or a maternal relative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r3.anchor: وكان متزوجا امرأة من ذرية هارون اسمها ( اليصابات ) وكانت امرأته نسيبة مريم كما في إنجيل لوقا قيل : كانت أختها والصحيح أنها كانت خالتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r4.claim: After Mary's father died, the priests competed to foster the daughter of their chief priest, and a drawing selected Zachariah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r4.anchor: ولما ولدت مريم كان أبوها قد مات فتنازع كفالتها جماعة من أحبار بني إسرائيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r5.claim: The priests were assigned as Mary's guardians because her dedication to sanctuary service required a suitable upbringing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن جعل كفالتها للأحبار لأنها محررة لخدمة المسجد فيلزم أن تربى تربية صالحة لذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r6.claim: Most readers use a light ف in كفلها, meaning Zachariah undertook Mary's guardianship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { وكفلها زكرياء } بتخفيف الفاء من كفلها أي تولى كفالتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r7.speaker: حمزة، عاصم، الكسائي، خلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r7.claim: Hamza, Asim, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read the verb with a doubled ف, meaning God made Zachariah her guardian.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، وعاصم ، والكسائي ، وخلف : وكفلها بتشديد الفاء أي أن الله جعل زكرياء كافلا لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r8.claim: Most readers pronounce Zachariah's name with a final hamza and a long form, with the hamza nominative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور زكرياء بهمزة في آخره ، ممدودا وبرفع الهمزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r9.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، حفص عن عاصم، خلف، أبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r9.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Hafs from Asim, and Khalaf use the shortened form; Abu Bakr from Asim has a final hamza with accusative case.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p235#2/r9.anchor: وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم ، وخلف : بالقصر ، وقرأه أبو بكر عن عاصم : بالهمز في آخره ونصب الهمزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r1.claim: The narrative implies Mary remained in the Temple’s service and worshiped in a private mihrab; Zakariya visited her and saw out-of-season fruit as a miracle for her.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r1.anchor: فكانت مريم ملازمة لخدمة بيت المقدس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r2.claim: Kullamā combines kull, a noun of generality, with temporal mā and its implied verbal clause: every time Zakariya entered, he found provision.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r2.anchor: الذي هو اسم لعموم ما يضاف هو إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r3.claim: The clause “he found provision with her” can be parsed as a circumstantial clause describing Zakariya in the preceding account of his guardianship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r4.claim: Alternatively, the clause about finding provision can be an appositional complement of the guardianship clause, specifying an aspect of it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r5.claim: A mihrab is a structure made for solitary worship and prayer, usually raised and reached by steps; it is distinct from a mosque.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r5.anchor: بناء يتخذه أحد ليخلو فيه بتعبده وصلاته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r6.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r6.claim: Ibn Abi Rabiʿa uses mihrab expansively for a church’s sanctuary or altar, although a mihrab is not literally where an altar is placed.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r7.claim: An unnamed etymology derives mihrab from ḥarb, treating the worshipper as one who battles Satan in that place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r7.anchor: وقد قيل : إن المحراب مشتق من الحرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r8.claim: Muslims later used mihrab for the prayer niche at the qibla where the imam stands; this was a later, developed usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r8.anchor: ثم أطلق المحراب عند المسلمين على موضع كشكل نصف قبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r9.claim: The first Islamic mihrab was in the Prophet’s Mosque, built under al-Walid ibn ʿAbd al-Malik while ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz governed Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r9.anchor: وأول محراب في الإسلام محراب مسجد الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم صنع في خلافة الوليد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r10.claim: The definite article in “the mihrab” is generic; context identifies it as the worship niche Mary had made for herself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p236/r10.anchor: تعريف الجنس ويعلم أن المراد محراب جعلته مريم للتعبد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r1.claim: Anā asks about place and means “from where”; Mary’s answer, “from God,” directly answers Zakariya’s question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r1.anchor: أي من أين لك هذا ، فلذلك كان جواب استفهامه قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r2.claim: Zakariya asked because the food appeared out of season; one report identifies it as grapes in winter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r2.anchor: قيل : كان عنبا في فصل الشتاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r3.claim: The sentence “God provides for whom He wills” is part of Mary’s quoted speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r3.anchor: وجملة { إن الله يرزق من يشاء }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r4.claim: Ḥisāb here suggests limitation: God provides an amount whose measure is unknown, since it depends on His bounty rather than a counted allotment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r4.anchor: بمعنى الحصر لأن الحساب يقتضي حصر الشيء المحسوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p237/r5.claim: The meaning of rizq was explained earlier in the commentary on God providing whom He wills without measure.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r5.claim: God accepted Maryam for the sanctuary service her mother vowed; the wording implies God informed Zachariah and those present, so they installed her there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فتقبلها إخبار لمحمد عليه السلام بأن الله رضي مريم لخدمة المسجد كما نذرت أمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r6.claim: Qabūl is a verbal noun formed unlike the expected one from taqabbala; nabātan likewise follows anbata.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r6.anchor: وقوله بقبول مصدر جاء على غير الصدر، وكذلك قوله نباتا بعد أنبت،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r7.claim: Her good growth means excellent and rapid development in both physical form and character.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r7.anchor: عبارة عن حسن النشأة وسرعة الجودة فيها في خلقة وخلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r8.claim: Zachariah took Maryam into his care and maintenance; a kāfil is a guardian who raises and shelters someone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r8.anchor: معناه: ضمها إلى إنفاقه وحضنه، والكافل هو المربي الحاضن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r9.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r9.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Zachariah was married to Maryam's maternal aunt; Zachariah and ʿImrān were connected by marriage to two sisters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r9.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: إن زكرياء كان زوج خالتها لأنه وعمران كانا سلفين على أختين،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r10.speaker: السدي وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r10.claim: Al-Suddī and others say Zachariah married another daughter of ʿImrān; the Prophet's description of John and Jesus as maternal cousins supports this account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r10.anchor: وقال السدي وغيره: إن زكرياء كان زوج ابنة أخرى لعمران، ويعضد هذا القول قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r11.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r11.claim: Makkī identifies Zachariah as the son of Ādhan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r11.anchor: قال مكي: وهو زكريا بن آذن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r12.speaker: قتادة وغير واحد من أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r12.claim: Scholars say caretakers competed for the consecrated child and cast lots to win custody of Maryam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r12.anchor: وذكر قتادة وغير واحد من أهل العلم: أنهم كانوا في ذلك الزمان يتشاحون في المحرر عند من يكون من القائمين بأمر المسجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r13.claim: Accounts say they cast Torah-writing pens into a river, or carved wooden lots or staffs; the site is given as the Jordan or a spring.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r13.anchor: فروي أنهم ألقوا أقلامهم التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة في النهر، وقيل أقلاما بروها من عود كالسهام والقداح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r14.claim: In one account Zachariah's pen moved against the current while the other pens went with it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r14.anchor: وروي أن قلم زكرياء صاعد الجرية، ومضت أقلام الآخرين مع الماء في جريته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r15.claim: Another report says the others floated flat on the water while Zachariah's pen remained upright as if planted in clay.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r15.anchor: وروي أن أقلام القوم عامت على الماء معروضة كما تفعل العيدان وبقي قلم زكرياء مرتكزا واقفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r16.speaker: ابن إسحاق عن الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r16.claim: Ibn Isḥāq, as cited by al-Ṭabarī, says that during a famine Zachariah proposed a lottery to find Maryam's provider; the lot fell to Jurayj, who supported her, and Zachariah later visited her.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p425/r16.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن ابن إسحاق: أنها لما ترعرعت أصابت بني إسرائيل مجاعة فقال لهم زكرياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya distinguishes the famine lottery, meant to transfer responsibility, from the first lottery to gain custody; he says most hold that Zachariah won custody by lot.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r1.anchor: قال أبو محمد: وهذا الاستهام غير الأول، هذا المراد منه دفعها، والأول المراد منه أخذها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق; author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r2.claim: In the famine account Zachariah had cared for Maryam from infancy without a lottery because her parents died; Ibn Isḥāq gives the same account, but the prevailing view is that the lot determined custody.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r2.anchor: ومضمن هذه الرواية أن زكرياء كفلها من لدن طفولتها دون استهام، لكن أمها هلكت وقد كان أبوها هلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير; نافع; أبو عمرو; ابن عامر; عاصم; حمزة; الكسائي; أبي بن كعب; مجاهد; المزني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r3.claim: Readers vary in the voice and doubling of kaffala, the case and length of Zachariah's name, and a causative akfalaha; Mujāhid also reads the verbs as prayers, and Ibn Kathīr and al-Muzanī report a light kasra form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص، «كفلها» مشددة الفاء مفتوحة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r4.speaker: أبو علي; الزجاج; أبو حاتم; مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r4.claim: Zachariah is foreign but Arabicized, with long and short forms; Abū ʿAlī and al-Zajjāj analyze its feminine ending and declension, while Makkī reports that grammarians reject Abū Ḥātim's indeclinable Zakarī.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: لما عرب صادق العربية في بنائه فهو كالهيجاء تمد وتقصر، قال الزجاج: فأما ترك صرفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r1.claim: Kullamā is an adverbial expression governed by wajada, “he found.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: كلما ظرف والعامل فيه وجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r2.claim: Miḥrāb is a fine building like a chamber or gallery; the most honored room in a palace gave its name to the imam's place in a mosque.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r2.anchor: والمحراب المبنى الحسن كالغرف والعلالي ونحوه، ومحراب القصر أشرف ما فيه ولذلك قيل لأشرف ما في المصلى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r3.speaker: وضاح اليمن; عدي بن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r3.claim: Waddāḥ al-Yaman uses miḥrāb for an elevated chamber reached by a ladder; ʿAdī ibn Zayd uses its plural in a poetic comparison.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر: [وضاح اليمن] [السريع] ربة محراب إذا جئتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r4.claim: The provision was food Maryam ate, whose source Zachariah did not recognize.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وجد عندها رزقا، معناه طعاما تتغذى به ما لم يعهده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r5.speaker: الربيع; مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r5.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says she was behind seven locked doors; Makkī says she lived in a chamber reached by a ladder.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r5.anchor: وكانت فيما ذكر الربيع، تحت سبعة أبواب مغلقة وحكى مكي أنها كانت في غرفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس; ابن جبير; مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, and Mujāhid say she had out-of-season grapes; another Ibn ʿAbbās report identifies the food as Paradise's fruit, summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: وجد عندها عنبا في مكتل في غير حينه، وقاله ابن جبير ومجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك; مجاهد; قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Mujāhid, and Qatādah say she had winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك ومجاهد أيضا وقتادة: كان يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف، وفاكهة الصيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the food came from heaven, was unavailable to ordinary people, and would not have prompted Zachariah's question had he known its source.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن: كان يجد عندها رزقا من السماء ليس عند الناس ولو أنه علم أن ذلك الرزق من عنده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r9.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r9.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says her guardian Jurayj brought her food, which God multiplied; Zachariah was surprised at its abundance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: هذا الدخول الذي ذكر الله تعالى في قوله كلما دخل عليها إنما هو دخول زكرياء عليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r10.claim: The prevailing account is stronger than Ibn Isḥāq's explanation involving Jurayj.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r10.anchor: والذي عليه الناس أقوى مما ذكره ابن إسحاق،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r11.claim: Annā means “how?” or “from where?”; Maryam's answer indicates that no person brought the provision.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r11.anchor: وقوله أنى معناه كيف ومن أين؟ وقولها: هو من عند الله، دليل على أنه ليس من جلب بشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r12.claim: Zachariah understood the answer as a claim that the provision was not humanly brought; otherwise he would not have been satisfied by it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r12.anchor: وهكذا تلقى زكرياء المعنى وإلا فليس كان يقنع بهذا الجواب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r13.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r13.claim: Al-Zajjāj links the provision to the statement that Maryam and her son were made a sign for all worlds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r13.anchor: قال الزجاج: وهذا من الآية التي قال تعالى: وجعلناها وابنها آية للعالمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r14.claim: A report says Maryam never suckled at a breast.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r14.anchor: وروي أنها لم تلقم ثديا قط،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r15.claim: If these words are Maryam's, they affirm that the provision came from God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r15.anchor: وقولها: إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب تقرير لكون ذلك الرزق من عند الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r16.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r16.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says this is God's report, not Maryam's speech: God's stores are never depleted or counted; applying the phrase to generous people is figurative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p426#2/r16.anchor: وذهب الطبري إلى أن ذلك ليس من قول مريم وأنه خبر من الله تعالى لمحمد عليه السلام، والله تعالى لا تنتقص خزائنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r1.claim: Mujahid reads fa-taqabbalhā with a still lām, rabbahā with fatḥa on the bāʾ, and anbat-hā with a kasra on the bāʾ and still tāʾ as a prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r1.anchor: قرأ مجاهد ﴿ فتقبلها ﴾ بسكون اللام ﴿ ربها ﴾ بنصب الباء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the expected form would be bi-taqabbul, but qabūl is also valid as the verbal noun; qabūlan is also used when the sense is acceptance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج الأصل في العربيه فتقبلها بتقبل حسن ولكن قبول محمول على قبلها قبولا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r3.claim: The phrase means that God gave Mary a good, wholesome growth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج، ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r4.claim: Nabātan differs from the form of anbata; the wording follows the sense “she grew,” since anbata entails nabata.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r4.anchor: وجاء نباتا على غير لفظ أنبت على معنى نبتت نباتا حسنا وقال ابن الأنباري لما كان أنبت يدل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r5.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r5.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line uses raḍat in the sense of training or disciplining, illustrating a verb whose wording is carried by its implied meaning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r5.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس فصرنا إلى الحسنى ورق كلامنا ورضت فذلت صعبة أي اذلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r6.claim: One interpretation of Mary's good growth is full physical development: Ibn Abbas says she grew in a day as much as an ordinary child grows in a year.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r6.anchor: أحدهما أنه كمال النشوء قال ابن عباس كانت تنبت في اليوم ما ينبت المولود في عام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r7.claim: Another interpretation is that Mary was kept from sin, unlike ordinary descendants of Adam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p377#3/r7.anchor: والثاني أنه ترك الخطايا قال قتاده حدثنا أنها كانت لا تصيب الذنوب كما يصيب بنو آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، ابن عامر، أبو بكر عن عاصم، حفص عن عاصم، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿAmir read light kafala-hā with Zakariyyā nominative and long; Abu Bakr from ʿAsim reads heavy with Zakariyyā accusative and long; Hafs reads heavy and short; Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read heavy and short.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابو عمرو وابن عامر وكفلها بفتح الفاء خفيفه وزكرياء مرفوع ممدود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ lists three forms of Zakariya: Hijazi speakers use the short or long form, while Najdis say Zakari, declining it and dropping the alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r2.anchor: فأما زكريا فقال الفراء فيه ثلاث لغات أهل الحجاز يقولون هذا زكريا قد جاء مقصور وزكرياء ممدود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r3.speaker: ابن دريد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r3.claim: Ibn Durayd calls Zakariya a foreign name and gives Zakari, long Zakariyāʾ, and short Zakariyā forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r3.anchor: وقرأت على شيخنا أبي منصور اللغوي عن ابن دريد قال زكريا اسم أعجمي يقال زكري وزكرياء ممدود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r4.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r4.claim: Another grammarian adds Zakari with a light yāʾ; the long form has dual Zakariyāwān and plural Zakariyāwūn, the short form dual Zakariyān, and the light-yāʾ form dual Zakariyān and plural Zakrūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r4.anchor: وقال غيره وزكري بتخفيف الياء فمن قال زكرياء بالمد قال في التثنيه زكرياوان وفي الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says Hanna brought Mary wrapped up; when the people disputed custody, Zakariya claimed her because her sister was with him, but they went to the Jordan and cast their writing pens. His pen stayed fixed while the others ran in the water, so he took charge of her.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r5.anchor: قال السدي انطلقت بها أمها في خرقها وكانوا يقترعون على الذين يؤتون بهم فقال زكريا وهو نبيهم يومئذ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says 27 men cast lots by throwing their pens into the current; the one that rose against the current would win, and Zakariya's did.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس كانوا سبعة وعشرين رجلا فقالوا نطرح أقلامنا فمن صعد قلمه مغالبا للجرية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r7.claim: Muqatil says Zakariya locked the door and kept the key; during Mary's menstruation he sent her to the home of his sister, the mother of Yahya, and returned her to the Temple when she was clean.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل كان يغلق عليها الباب ومعه المفتاح لا يأمن عليه أحدا وكانت اذا حاضت أخرجها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r8.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r8.claim: Most exegetes say Zakariya cared for Mary from infancy after winning a drawing of lots.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r8.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه كفلها منذ كانت طفلة بالقرعة وقد ذهب قوم إلى أنه كفلها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r9.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r9.claim: Another account says Zakariya took Mary as an infant without a lottery because her mother died and her aunt was his wife; the later contest happened when Mary entered the sanctuary as an adult and a drought struck.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r9.anchor: وقد ذهب قوم إلى أنه كفلها عند طفولتها بغير قرعة لأجل أن أمها ماتت وكانت خالتها عنده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r10.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r10.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Zakariya raised Mary until a drought brought hardship; the Israelites drew lots, which fell to the poor carpenter Jurayj, whose meager food multiplied. Zakariya questioned Mary, and she said it came from God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r10.anchor: فقال محمد بن إسحاق كفلها زكريا إلى أن أصابت الناس سنة فشكا زكريا إلى بني إسرائيل ضيق يده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r11.speaker: قتادة وآخرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r11.claim: Qatada and others say the people competed for custody because Mary was the daughter of their master and leader, ʿImran.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r11.anchor: تشاحوا على كفالتها لأنها كانت بنت سيدهم وإمامهم عمران كذلك قال قتادة في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r12.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi prefers the majority account: the people competed for Mary from infancy because of her status, and Zakariya won the lot then.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r12.anchor: والصحيح ما عليه الأكثرون و أن القوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r13.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says miḥrāb is the presiding seat of an assembly, its foremost and most honored place, and likewise a mosque's honored area.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r13.anchor: فأما المحراب فقال أبو عبيدة المحراب سيد المجالس ومقدمها وأشرفها وكذلك هو من المسجد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r14.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r14.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says miḥrāb here means a chamber or room.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r14.anchor: وقال الأصمعي المحراب هاهنا الغرفة وقال الزجاج المحراب في اللغة الموضع العالي الشريف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r15.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines miḥrāb linguistically as an elevated, noble place.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p378/r15.anchor: وقال الزجاج المحراب في اللغة الموضع العالي الشريف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r1.claim: God accepted Mary as her mother’s vowed offering and made her grow beautifully, with a pleasing form and appearance and circumstances that aided her acceptance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r1.anchor: يخبر ربنا (5) أنه تقبلها من أمها نذيرة، وأنه {وأنبتها نباتا حسنا} أي: جعلها شكلا مليحا ومنظرا بهيجا، ويسر لها أسباب القبول،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r2.claim: God placed Mary among righteous servants so she could learn goodness, knowledge, and religion from them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r2.anchor: وقرنها بالصالحين من عباده تتعلم منهم الخير والعلم والدين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r3.claim: A reading with doubled fāʾ and Zakariyya in the accusative makes God the subject: He appointed Zakariyya as her guardian.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r3.anchor: بتشديد الفاء ونصب زكريا على المفعولية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Zakariyya cared for Mary because she was an orphan; others say Israel suffered drought and he took her in for that reason, and Ibn Kathir sees no conflict between the accounts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r4.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وما ذاك إلا أنها كانت يتيمة. وذكر غيره أن بني إسرائيل أصابتهم سنة جدب، فكفل زكريا مريم لذلك. ولا منافاة بين القولين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r5.claim: God assigned Zakariyya as Mary’s guardian for her happiness, so she could gain abundant useful knowledge and righteous practice from him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r5.anchor: وإنما قدر الله كون زكريا كافلها لسعادتها، لتقتبس منه علما جما نافعا وعملا صالحا؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, and others say Zakariyya was married to Mary’s maternal aunt; another view says her sister, consistent with the Sahih report that Jesus and John were maternal cousins.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r6.anchor: ولأنه كان زوج خالتها، على ما ذكره ابن إسحاق وابن جرير [وغيرهما] (7) وقيل: زوج أختها، كما ورد في الصحيح: "فإذا بيحيى (8) وعيسى، وهما ابنا الخالة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r7.claim: The Prophet ruled that Imara daughter of Hamza be placed in her maternal aunt Jaʿfar’s wife’s custody, saying the maternal aunt is like a mother.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r7.anchor: قضى في عمارة بنت حمزة أن تكون في حضانة خالتها امرأة جعفر بن أبي طالب وقال: "الخالة بمنزلة الأم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r8.speaker: مجاهد، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، وأبو الشعثاء، وإبراهيم النخعي، والضحاك، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وعطية العوفي، والسدي، والشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r8.claim: These early authorities say Zakariyya found summer fruit with Mary in winter and winter fruit in summer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r8.anchor: قال مجاهد، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، وأبو الشعثاء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r9.claim: Mujahid also glosses Mary’s provision as knowledge, or scrolls containing knowledge; Ibn Kathir prefers the seasonal-fruit explanation as sounder.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r9.anchor: وعن مجاهد {وجد عندها رزقا} أي: علما، أو قال: صحفا فيها علم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r10.claim: The miraculous provision is evidence for the karamat, or extraordinary favors, granted to God’s saints; the Prophetic Sunnah has similar instances.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r10.anchor: وفيه دلالة على كرامات الأولياء. وفي السنة لهذا نظائر كثيرة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r11.claim: Zakariyya’s question means, From where did this come to you? Mary replies that it is from God, who provides without measure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p35/r11.anchor: فإذا رأى زكريا هذا عندها {قال يا مريم أنى لك هذا} أي: يقول من أين لك هذا؟ {قالت هو من عند الله إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p36/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p36/r1.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p36/r1.claim: Jabir reports that after days without food the Prophet found nothing with his wives; a neighbor supplied Fatima with bread and meat, which multiplied to feed the Prophet’s household and remained blessed for the neighbors. Fatima said it came from God, like Mary’s provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p36/r1.anchor: عن جابر؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقام أياما لم يطعم طعاما، حتى شق ذلك عليه،

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read kaffalahā with a doubled fāʾ; Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim has long ā and accusative Zakariyyā, while Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ use short ā and accusative, meaning God entrusted her to him.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r2.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي كفلها بالتشديد، ثم اختلفوا في زكريا فقرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر بالمد والنصب

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r3.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r3.claim: The remaining readers use the light form and nominative Zakariyyā, meaning he took her into his care; Jishumi prefers this because it fits the later question about her guardian and is the reading of most authorities.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون كفلها بالتخفيف زكريا بالمد والرفع على معنى ضمها زكريا إلى نفسه، وهو الاختيار

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r4.claim: In one narration Ibn Kathir reads kafalaha with kasra on the fāʾ, meaning Zachariah took her into his own care.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r4.anchor: وعن ابن كثير في رواية كفلها بكسر الفاء، أي ضمها إلى نفسه

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r5.claim: Zakariyyā has three forms: lengthened, shortened, and Zakarī with a final yāʾ; their dual and plural forms differ.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r5.anchor: وفي زكريا ثلاث لغات: المد والقصر وزكري بالياء مثل قرشي، وأحكامها مختلفة في التثنية والجمع

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r6.claim: Taqabbala is form V from qabūl, to accept with approval; qabīl also means guarantor.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r6.anchor: التقيل: تفعل من القبول، يقال: قبلت الشيء أقبله إذا رضيته، والقبيل الكفيل

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r7.claim: The verse uses the verbal noun qabūl rather than taqabbul after a form V verb to convey that she was accepted, as in anbattukum nabātan and kallamtuhu kalāman.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r7.anchor: وذكر التقبل، ثم ذكر المصدر من القبول دون التقبل؛ لأن فيه معنى قبلها

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r8.claim: Qabūl occurs with fatḥa and ḍamma; ḍamma follows the regular pattern of verbal nouns like dukhūl and khurūj.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r8.anchor: والقبول مصدره جاء بالفتح والضم، فأما الضم فهو القياس نحو الدخول والخروج

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr b. al-ʿAlāʾ says the fatḥa form has no parallel and that he did not hear the word pronounced with ḍamma.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r9.anchor: وأما الفتح فقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: لا نظير له ولم أسمعهم ضموه

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r11.speaker: سيبويه
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r11.claim: Sībawayh lists qabūl among five verbal nouns on fuʿūl; waqūd is most often ḍamma when a verbal noun.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r11.anchor: وقال سيبويه: خمسة مصادر جاءت على فعول بالنصب: قبول، ووضوء، وطهور، وولوع، ووقود

JISHUMI:v2p1150/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r12.claim: Kafāla means taking responsibility for a person's expenses and being their guarantor.
JISHUMI:v2p1150/r12.anchor: والكفل: تضمن مؤنة الإنسان، كفلته. أكفله كفلا، وأنا كافل إذا تكفلت مؤنته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r2.claim: God accepted Mary in place of the male child her mother had vowed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r2.anchor: رضي بها في النذر مكان الذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r3.claim: Qabūl may name the means of acceptance: God specially chose her to replace a boy in the vow, although no female had previously been accepted for it, or accepted her immediately after birth before she could serve.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r3.anchor: فيه وجهان احدهما ان يكون القبول اسم ما تقبل به الشيء كالسعوط واللدود

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r4.claim: Ḥanna wrapped the newborn Mary, brought her to the Jerusalem temple priests descended from Aaron, and offered her as a vowed child; they competed for her guardianship because of her family’s status.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r4.anchor: وروي ان حنة حين ولدت مريم لفتها في خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد ووضعتها عند الأحبار أبناء هرون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r5.claim: Zakariyyā claimed the right to care for Mary because her maternal aunt was his wife; after the priests refused, twenty-seven men drew lots at a river, and Zakariyyā’s pen floated while theirs sank.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p385/r5.anchor: فقال لهم زكريا أنا أحق بها عندي خالتها فقالوا لا حتى نقترع عليها فانطلقوا وكانوا سبعة وعشرين إلى نهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r1.claim: He also reads fa-taqabbalahā as ‘received her at the outset,’ supported by al-Qaṭāmī’s line on taking an affair at its beginning and the proverb about its first occasions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r1.anchor: قال القطامي ( وخير الأمر ما استقبلت منه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r2.claim: The proverb خذ الأمر بقوابله likewise supports taking Mary in the first moment of her life.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r2.anchor: ومنه المثل ( خذ الأمر بقوابله ) أي فأخذها في اول امرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r3.claim: The good growth is a metaphor for her excellent upbringing, which benefited her in every circumstance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r3.anchor: مجاز عن التربية الحسنة العائدة عليها بما يصلحها في جميع احوالها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r4.claim: A reading has kafalahā on the pattern of ʿamilahā.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r5.claim: With the fāʾ doubled and Zakariyyā accusative, God is the agent: He attached Mary to Zakariyyā and made him responsible for her; Ubayy’s akfilhā supports this reading.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r5.anchor: بتشديد الفاء ونصب زكرياء والفعل لله تعالى بمعنى وضمها اليه وجعله كافلا لها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r6.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r6.claim: Mujāhid reads all three verbs as imperatives, with rabbahā accusative: ‘Accept her, nurture her, and appoint Zakariyyā her guardian.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد فتقبلها ربها وأنبتها وكفلها على لفظ الأمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r7.claim: One view takes the miḥrāb as a chamber Zakariyyā built for Mary in the temple, reached by a ladder.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r7.anchor: قيل بنى لها زكريا محرابا في المسجد أي غرفة يصعد اليها بسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r8.claim: Another view takes miḥrāb to mean the foremost, most honored place, where Mary was situated in Jerusalem.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r8.anchor: وقيل المحراب أشرف المجالس ومقدمها كأنها وضعت في أشرف موضع من بيت المقدس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r9.claim: A further view says their mosques were called maḥārīb.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r10.claim: Zakariyyā alone entered Mary’s chamber and, on leaving, shut seven doors behind him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386/r10.anchor: وروي انه كان لا يدخل عليها الا هو وحده وكان اذا خرج غلق عليها سبعة أبواب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r1.claim: Mary’s provision came down from Paradise; she never suckled, and Zakariyyā found winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r1.anchor: كان رزقها ينزل عليها من الجنة ولم ترضع ثديا قط فكان يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r2.claim: Zakariyyā asks where this unlike-worldly, out-of-season food came from, since the doors were shut and no one could have brought it in.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r2.anchor: من أين لك هذا الرزق الذي لا يشبه أرزاق الدنيا وهو آت في غير حينه والأبواب مغلقة عليك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r3.claim: It is said Mary spoke while still a small child, as Jesus spoke in the cradle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r3.anchor: قيل تكلمت وهي صغيرة كما تكلم عيسى وهو في المهد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r4.claim: In a drought, Fāṭima gave the hungry Prophet two loaves and some meat; he returned with a platter miraculously full, asked her this verse’s question, and praised her resemblance to Israel’s foremost woman.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r4.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 169 انه جاع في زمن قحط فأهدت له فاطمة رضي الله عنها رغيفين وبضعة لحم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r5.claim: The Prophet gathered ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and his household; they ate their fill while the food remained unchanged, and Fāṭima sent some to neighbors.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p386#2/r5.anchor: ثم جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم علي بن أبي طالب والحسن والحسين وجميع اهل بيته فأكلوا عليه حتى شبعوا وبقي الطعام كما هو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r1.claim: The clause ‘God provides’ may continue Mary’s speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r1.anchor: من جملة كلام مريم عليها السلام أو من كلام رب العزة عز من قائل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r2.claim: Alternatively, ‘God provides’ may be God’s own speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r2.anchor: من جملة كلام مريم عليها السلام أو من كلام رب العزة عز من قائل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r3.claim: Without reckoning can mean provision so abundant it cannot be measured.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r3.anchor: بغير تقدير لكثرته أو تفضلا بغير محاسبة ومجازاة على عمل بحسب الاستحقاق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r4.claim: It can also mean gracious provision without accounting or repayment according to earned merit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p387/r4.anchor: بغير تقدير لكثرته أو تفضلا بغير محاسبة ومجازاة على عمل بحسب الاستحقاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r1.claim: God accepted Mary by approving her vow to devote herself to worship in the Jerusalem sanctuary.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r1.anchor: معناه أنه رضيها في النذر الذي نذرته بإخلاص العبادة في بيت المقدس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r2.claim: The good growth means God brought her up well, providing good nourishment and rearing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r2.anchor: يعني أنشأها إنشاء حسنا في غذائها وحسن تربيتها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r3.speaker: أهل الكوفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r3.claim: The Kufans read the verb with gemination, meaning that Zakariya entrusted Mary's guardianship to someone else.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r3.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة { وكفلها } بالتشديد , ومعنى ذلك أنه دفع كفالتها إلى غيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r4.speaker: الباقون
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r4.claim: The other readers use the lighter form, meaning that Zakariya took Mary into his own guardianship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون : { كفلها } بالتخفيف , ومعنى ذلك أنه أخذ كفالتها إليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r5.claim: A mihrab is the honored place in a gathering.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r5.anchor: وهو معروف , وأصله أنه أكرم موضع في المجلس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الضحاك، قتادة، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatada, and al-Suddi say Mary received summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r6.anchor: أن الرزق الذي أتاها فاكهة الصيف في الشتاء , وفاكهة الشتاء في الصيف , وهذا قول ابن عباس , ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r7.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says Mary was never nursed and, until she spoke in the cradle, her food came from Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r7.anchor: وإنما كان يأتيها رزقها من الجنة , وهذا قول الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r8.claim: One view says the food came through Zakariya's prayer for Mary.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r8.anchor: أحدهما : أنه كان يأتيها بدعوة زكريا لها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r9.claim: Another view says the food came because of the prophethood of the Messiah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r9.anchor: والثاني : أنه كان ذلك يأتيها لنبوة المسيح عليه السلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r10.claim: One explanation is that God directly provided Mary's food; the author says this is more fitting than the alternative.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r11.claim: Alternatively, God may have prompted one of His righteous servants to bring Mary food.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r11.anchor: أن بعض الصالحين من عباده سخره الله تعالى لها لطفا منه بها حتى يأتيها رزقها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r12.claim: The closing words may continue Mary's speech after 'it is from God,' or be God's words after her speech ends.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p387/r12.anchor: أحدهما : أنه حكاية عن قول مريم بعد أن قالت هو من عند الله . والقول الثاني : أنه قول الله تعالى

MUJAHID:v1p125#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p125#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p125#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says they cast lots with their pens to determine Mary's guardian, and Zachariah won.
MUJAHID:v1p125#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ وكفلها زكريا ﴾ يقول ساهمهم بقلمه فسهمهم فكان

MUJAHID:v1p125#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p125#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p125#2/r2.claim: The provision Zachariah found with Mary was fruit appearing out of season.
MUJAHID:v1p125#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وكفلها زكريا ﴾ يقول ساهمهم بقلمه فسهمهم فكان ﴿ كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا ﴾ قال يعني ثمرا

MUJAHID:v1p126/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p126/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MUJAHID:v1p126/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that the provision was grapes in a basket out of season; this prompted Zachariah to ask for a child, since God could grant one despite his wife's barrenness.
MUJAHID:v1p126/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله ﴿ وجد عندها رزقا ﴾ قال وجد عندها عنبا في مكتل في غير حينه فهنالك دعا ربه

MUQATIL:3:37-38/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r1.claim: God nurtured Mary well in worship and obedience; Zechariah built her a chamber in Jerusalem’s temple, entered by ladder, and arranged a wet nurse.
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r1.anchor: يقول: رباها تربية حسنة فى عبادة وطاعة لربها

MUQATIL:3:37-38/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r2.claim: Zechariah locked Mary in, trusted no one else with her, brought her food and needs, took her to his home during menstruation, then returned her to the chamber when pure.
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r2.anchor: فكان يغلق عليها الباب ومعه المفتاح

MUQATIL:3:37-38/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r3.claim: Zechariah saw grapes with Mary in the bitter winter; Gabriel had brought them from heaven.
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r3.anchor: وكان زكريا يرى عندها العنب فى الشتاء الشديد البرد، فيأتيها به جبريل

MUQATIL:3:37-38/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r4.claim: Zechariah asks where the out-of-season food came from; Mary says it is from God, who provides without measure to whomever He wills.
MUQATIL:3:37-38/r4.anchor: يعنى من أين هذا فى غير حينه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.claim: God accepted Mary and approved her in the vow in place of a male child.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.anchor: قبل الله مريم ورضى بها فى النذر مكان الذكر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.claim: Qabūl can name the means of acceptance; here it is God’s special favor in assigning Mary the place of a boy, unprecedented for a girl.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.anchor: قيل القبول اسم ما يقبل به الشئ كالسعوط بما يسعط به

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, her acceptance was her mother’s handing her over immediately after birth, before she could grow old enough for sanctuary service.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.anchor: أو بأن تسلمها من أمها عقيب الولادة قبل أن تنشأ وتصلح للسدانة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.claim: The account says Ḥanna wrapped newborn Mary and brought her to the temple priests descended from Aaron; they competed to care for her because she was the imam’s daughter and the Banū Māthān were Israelite leaders.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.anchor: روى أن حنة لما ولدت مريم لفتها فى خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.claim: In the account, Zechariah claimed precedence through kinship; after twenty-seven men cast their pens in a river, his rose above the water while the others sank, so he became her guardian.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.anchor: فارتفع قلم زكريا فوق الماء ورسبت أقلامهم فتكفلها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r6.claim: Another parsing treats qabūl as a verbal noun with an omitted genitive: acceptance by one possessing excellent acceptance, namely God’s special favor.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r6.anchor: فتقبلها بذى قبول حسن أى بمر ذى قبول حسن وهو الاختصاص

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r7.claim: Growing her with good growth is a metaphor for her good upbringing.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says the best growth is that whose fruit was Jesus.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r9.claim: «Nabātan» is either an unconventional verbal noun or an underlying «she grew a growth».
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r9.anchor: ونباتا مصدر على خلاف الصدر أو التقدير فنبتت نباتا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r10.claim: «Kaffalahā» means either that God accepted her or undertook her care.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r11.speaker: أهل الكوفة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r11.claim: The Kufans read the verb with doubled fāʾ, making God the subject who appoints Zechariah as guardian; the other form says Zechariah cared for her.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r11.anchor: وكفلها كوفى أى كفلها الله زكريا يعنى جعله كافلاها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r12.speaker: أهل الكوفة وأبو بكر
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r12.claim: The Kufans except Abū Bakr read Zakariyyā shortened throughout the Qurʾān; Abū Bakr lengthens it and reads it in the accusative here, while others lengthen it in the nominative as at later occurrences.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r12.anchor: بالقصر كوفى غير أبى بكر فى كل القرآن وقرأ أبو بكر بالمد والنصب هنا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r13.claim: The name Zakariyyā means in Hebrew one who constantly remembers and glorifies God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r13.anchor: ومعناه فى العبرى دائم الذكر والتسبيح

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r14.claim: The miḥrāb may be a chamber Zechariah built for her in the mosque, a raised room reached by stairs; it may instead mean the finest, foremost seat, or the name for their mosques.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r14.anchor: قيل بنى لها زكريا محرابا فى السمجد أى غرفة تصعد اليها بسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r15.claim: On the account that Mary was secluded in the sanctuary, only Zechariah entered to see her.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r15.anchor: وكان لا يدخل عليها إلا هو وحده

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r16.claim: Her provision descended from Paradise; she was never nursed, and Zechariah found winter fruit with her in summer and summer fruit in winter.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r16.anchor: كان رزقها ينزل عليها من الجنة ولم ترضع ثديا قط

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r17.claim: Zechariah asks where she obtained this provision, which did not resemble worldly food and arrived out of season.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r17.anchor: من أين لك هذا الرزق الذى لا يشبه أرزاق الدنيا وهو آت فى غير حينه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r18.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r18.claim: It is said that Mary spoke while still a small child, just as Jesus spoke in the cradle.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r18.anchor: قيل تكلمت وهى صغيرة كما تكلم عيسى وهو فى المهد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r19.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r19.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r19.claim: The sentence «God provides for whom He wills» may continue Mary’s speech or be God’s own words.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r19.anchor: من جملة كلام مريم أو من كلام رب العالمين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r20.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r20.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r20.claim: «Without reckoning» can mean provision too abundant to measure, or a gift bestowed without accounting for or recompensing deeds.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p151#2/r20.anchor: بغير تقدير لكثرته أو تفضلا بغير محاسبة ومجازاة على عمل

BURSEVI:v2p22/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p22/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p22/r3.claim: God accepted Mary in place of the boy in Hannah's vow and became her guardian, bringing her to her proper maturity.
BURSEVI:v2p22/r3.anchor: أخذ مريم ورضي بها في النذر مكان الذكر {ربها} مالكها ومبلغها إلى كمالها اللائق

BURSEVI:v2p22/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p22/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p22/r4.claim: The acceptance was gracious because the customary law permitted dedication only of a capable, rational boy, yet God received Hannah's baby girl in response to her plea.
BURSEVI:v2p22/r4.anchor: وهو قبول تلك الأنثى مع أنوثتها وصغرها فإن المعتاد في تلك الشريعة أن لا يجوز التحرير إلا في حق غلام

BURSEVI:v2p22/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p22/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p22/r5.claim: Her good growth is a metaphor for excellent upbringing that suited every circumstance of her life.
BURSEVI:v2p22/r5.anchor: مجاز عن التربية الحسنة العائدة عليها مما يصلح في جميع أحوالها

BURSEVI:v2p22/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p22/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p22/r6.claim: God recounts the acceptance because of Hannah's weakness, sincerity of intention at the beginning, and modesty at the end.
BURSEVI:v2p22/r6.anchor: وذلك لضعفها وصدق نيتها في الابتداء وحيائها في الانتهاء

BURSEVI:v2p22/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p22/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p22/r7.claim: Although four thousand people were dedicated to the sanctuary in that era, Mary's story alone became widely known.
BURSEVI:v2p22/r7.anchor: وكان في ذلك الزمان أربعة آلاف محرر لم يشتهر خبر أحد منهم اشتهار خبرها

BURSEVI:v2p22/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p22/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p22/r8.claim: A servant should see personal shortcoming even after striving, so God may accept the work through visible insolvency and hidden sincerity.
BURSEVI:v2p22/r8.anchor: وفيه تنبيه للعبد على أن يرى من نفسه التقصير بعد جهدها ليقبل الله عملها لإظهار إفلاسها

BURSEVI:v2p22/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p22/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p22/r9.claim: God removes both seekers and those who have arrived from seeing their own works and states, though for different reasons: seekers lack verified sincerity, while the arrived are eclipsed by witnessing God as the true actor and themselves as instruments.
BURSEVI:v2p22/r9.anchor: واعلم أنه سبحانه قطع السائرين له وهم المريدون والواصلين إليه وهم المرادون عن رؤية أعمالهم

BURSEVI:v2p22/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p22/r10.speaker: الواسطي
BURSEVI:v2p22/r10.claim: When Abu ʿUthman al-Maghribi's disciples said their shaykh taught obedience and awareness of its shortcomings, al-Wasiti called this pure Magianism and urged witnessing the One who originates and directs the act instead.
BURSEVI:v2p22/r10.anchor: ولما دخل الواسطي نيسابور سأل أصحاب الشيخ أبي عثمان المغربي بم يأمركم

BURSEVI:v2p22/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p22/r11.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v2p22/r11.claim: Al-Qushayri clarifies that al-Wasiti meant to protect disciples from self-admiration, not to settle them in deficiency or permit neglect of proper conduct.
BURSEVI:v2p22/r11.anchor: قال القشيري وإنما أراد الواسطي صيانتهم عن محل الإعجاب لا تعريجا في أوطان التقصير

BURSEVI:v2p23/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23/r1.speaker: النهرجوري
BURSEVI:v2p23/r1.claim: A sign that God has taken charge of one's deeds is seeing deficient sincerity, heedlessness in remembrance, imperfect truthfulness, slack striving, and poor attention to poverty; one then finds every state unsatisfactory, grows needful of God, and fades from all besides Him.
BURSEVI:v2p23/r1.anchor: قال النهرجوري من علامة من تولاه الله في أعماله أن يشهد التقصير في إخلاصه والغفلة في أذكاره

BURSEVI:v2p23/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23/r2.speaker: الشيخ أبو العباس
BURSEVI:v2p23/r2.claim: Explaining 22:61, Abu al-ʿAbbas says obedience can be tainted by vanity, reliance, contempt for others, and demand for reward, while sin can be surrounded by humility, recourse to God, and esteem for the sinless; seekers should strive without being deceived by worship.
BURSEVI:v2p23/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو العباس رضي الله عنه في إشارة قوله تعالى : {يولج اليل فى النهار ويولج النهار فى اليل}

BURSEVI:v2p23/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23/r3.claim: The alchemy poem likens spiritual effort to burying and spending gold in pursuit of a process that turns copper into pure gold; seekers should expend resources for divine approval and arrival at God's presence, even wealth and life, until the door of spiritual opening is reached.
BURSEVI:v2p23/r3.anchor: ه زرها بخاك سيه دركنند كه باشد كه روزى مسى زركنند

BURSEVI:v2p23/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23/r4.claim: The Persian verse says gold is a good means to buy things, but reaching the Friend's presence is a better purchase, underscoring the goal of spiritual striving.
BURSEVI:v2p23/r4.anchor: زر ازبهر يزى خريدن نكوست ه خواهي خريدن به ازوصل دوست

BURSEVI:v2p23/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23/r5.speaker: الشيخ الشاذلي
BURSEVI:v2p23/r5.claim: Al-Shadhili teaches that each kind of obedience contains lights of the unseen realm; missing a kind means missing its corresponding light, and spiritual inspirations do not replace regular litanies or acts of worship.
BURSEVI:v2p23/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ الشاذلي قدس سره في "لطائف المنن" : واعلموا أن الله أودع أنوار الملكوت

BURSEVI:v2p23/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23/r6.claim: Maintain every form of obedience, then forget one's deeds to avoid vanity: preserving an act is harder than performing it, as brittle glass breaks irreparably and good deeds can be erased by wrongdoing.
BURSEVI:v2p23/r6.anchor: فينبغي للعبد أن يواظب على أصناف الطاعات وينساها بعدما عملها كيلا يبطلها العجب

BURSEVI:v2p23/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23/r7.claim: The verb means God entrusted Mary to Zachariah, made him her guarantor, and charged him with her welfare; a kafīl provides for someone and tends their interests.
BURSEVI:v2p23/r7.anchor: بمعنى وضمنها الله إلى زكريا وجعله كافلا لها وضامنا لمصالحها

BURSEVI:v2p23/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v2p23/r8.claim: A hadith compares the Prophet and the guardian of an orphan to two adjacent fingers.
BURSEVI:v2p23/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث : "أنا وكافل اليتيم كهاتين" وهو زكريا بن أذن

BURSEVI:v2p23/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23/r9.claim: Zachariah is identified as son of Adhan ibn Muslim ibn Sadoon and a descendant of Solomon son of David.
BURSEVI:v2p23/r9.anchor: وهو زكريا بن أذن بن مسلم بن صدون من أولاد سليمان عليه السلام ابن داود عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r1.claim: Hannah wrapped Mary, brought her to the Temple, and presented her to Aaron's descendants, its custodians like the Kaaba's keepers; they competed for the daughter of Israel's leading family, while Zachariah claimed her because her maternal aunt was his wife.
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r1.anchor: روي أن حنة حين ولدت مريم لفتها في خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد ووضعتها عند الأحبار أبناء هارون

BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r2.claim: Twenty-seven priests drew lots at the Jordan by casting pens they used to write revelation; after three rounds Zachariah's pen rose above the water while the others sank, so he received Mary's guardianship.
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r2.anchor: فألقوا فيه أقلامهم التي كانوا يكتبون بها الوحي على أن كل من ارتفع قلمه فهو الراجح

BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r3.claim: Miḥrāb may be a chamber built for Mary that she reached by ladder, the most honored/front part of an assembly, or simply the name for their mosques.
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r3.anchor: قيل : بنى لها محرابا في المسجد أي : غرفة تصعد إليها بسلم

BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r4.claim: Only Zachariah entered Mary's chamber, and after he left it was shut behind seven doors.
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r4.anchor: روي أنها لا يدخل عليها إلا هو وحده فإذا خرج غلق عليها سبعة أبواب

BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r5.claim: Zachariah found unusual food sent from Paradise: summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer; Mary had never suckled at a breast.
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r5.anchor: إذ كان ينزل ذلك من الجنة وكان يجد عندها في الصيف فاكهة الشتاء وفي الشتاء فاكهة الصيف

BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r6.claim: He wondered where food unlike ordinary worldly provisions came from, out of season and despite her locked doors, with no one able to bring it in.
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r6.anchor: من أين يجيء لك هذا الذي لا يشبه أرزاق الدنيا وهو آت في غير حينه

BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r7.claim: Mary was very young and unable to comprehend the question or formulate an answer; reports say she spoke in childhood, as Jesus spoke in the cradle.
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r7.anchor: مريم وهي صغيرة لا قدرة لها على فهم السؤال ورد الجواب قيل تكلمت وهي صغيرة

BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r8.claim: Provision without reckoning means abundant provision, provision without accounting, or provision from an unexpected source; this explains how Mary's food came from God.
BURSEVI:v2p23#2/r8.anchor: بغير تقدير لكثرته أو بلا محاسبة أو من حيث لا يحتسب وهو تعليل لكونه من عند الله

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God led Mary along the path of the fortunate.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r1.anchor: المعنى: سلك بها طريق السعداء عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r2.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r2.claim: Some say acceptance means taking responsibility for Mary’s upbringing and care.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: معنى التقبل التكفل في التربية والقيام بشأنها

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God accepted Mary so that He never punished her by night or day.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: معنى التقبل أنه ما عذبها ساعة قط من ليل ولا نهار

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r4.claim: God gave Mary balanced form; she grew in one day as much as a newborn in a year.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r4.anchor: يعني سوى خلقها من غير زيادة ولا نقصان، فكانت تنبت في اليوم ما ينبت المولود في عام واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r5.claim: Qabūl and nabāt are verbal nouns used instead of expected taqabbulan and inbātan.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r5.anchor: والقبول والنبات مصدران على غير المصدر، والأصل تقبلا وإنباتا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r6.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses ʿaṭāʾ where the sense is iʿṭāʾ, giving.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر: أكفرا بعد رد الموت عني وبعد عطائك المائة الرتاعا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r7.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r7.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses idhlālan where the basic verbal noun is dhull.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r7.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: فصرنا إلى الحسنى ورق كلامنا ورضت فذلت صعبة أي إذلال

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r8.speaker: رؤبة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r8.claim: Ruʾba pairs taṭawwaytu with inwiṭāʾ as equivalent forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r8.anchor: قول رؤبة: وقد تطويت انطواء الحضب الأفعى لأن معنى تطويت وانطويت واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r9.speaker: القطامي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r9.claim: Al-Quṭāmī treats istaqbaltu and tatbaʿu as equivalent in the sense of following.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r9.anchor: قول القطامي: وخير الأمر ما استقبلت منه وليس بأن تتبعه اتباعا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r10.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads وأنزل الملائكة تنزيلا because nazzala and anzala share a meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r10.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود «وأنزل الملائكة تنزيلا» لأن معنى نزل وأنزل واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r11.speaker: المفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r11.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal says God caused her to grow; the author prefers the semantic explanation.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r11.anchor: وقال المفضل: معناه وأنبتها فنبتت نباتا حسنا. ومراعاة المعنى أولى كما ذكرنا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r12.claim: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī say qabūl originally has ḍamma like duḫūl and ḫurūj; fatḥ is rare.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r12.anchor: والأصل في القبول الضم لأنه مصدر مثل الدخول والخروج، والفتح جاء في حروف قليلة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r13.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r13.claim: Al-Zajjāj permits qabūl with ḍamma on qāf, following the original pattern.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r13.anchor: وأجاز الزجاج «بقبول» بضم القاف على الأصل

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r14.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains kafalahā as undertaking responsibility for Mary.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r15.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r15.claim: The Kūfans read with shadda, making God the implied subject who assigned Zakariya to care for Mary.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r15.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون «وكفلها» بالتشديد، فهو يتعدى إلى مفعولين والتقدير وكفلها ربها زكريا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r16.speaker: أبي
