QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r16.claim: Ubayy’s codex has وأكفلها, a hamza form with equivalent transitivity.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r16.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي «وأكفلها» والهمزة كالتشديد في التعدي

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r17.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r17.claim: Other reciters use the light form, making Zakariya subject who cared for Mary.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38/r17.anchor: وخففه الباقون على إسناد الفعل إلى زكريا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r1.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r1.claim: Makkī prefers the light form because God’s assigning Zakariya and Zakariya’s acting by God’s will overlap.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r1.anchor: قال مكي: وهو الاختيار لأن التشديد يرجع إلى التخفيف

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير وأبو عبد الله المزني
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r2.claim: A transmission from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī reads with kasra on fāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r2.anchor: وروى عمرو بن موسى عن عبد الله بن كثير وأبي عبد الله المزني «وكفلها» بكسر الفاء

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r3.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash gives kafala yakfulu and kafila yakfilu, and says he had not heard kafula.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r3.anchor: قال الأخفش: يقال كفل يكفل وكفل يكفل ولم أسمع كفل

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r4.speaker: حفص وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r4.claim: Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī omit lengthening and hamza; other readers lengthen and hamza the name.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ حفص وحمزة والكسائي «زكريا» بغير مد ولا همز، ومده الباقون وهمزوه

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Hijazis lengthen or shorten the name, while Najdis drop its alif and decline it as Zakari.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء: أهل الحجاز يمدون «زكرياء» ويقصرونه، وأهل نجد يحذفون منه الألف

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r6.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash lists four forms: long and short Zakariyyāʾ, declinable Zakari with doubled yāʾ, and Zakar.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r6.anchor: قال الأخفش: فيه أربع لغات: المد والقصر، وزكري بتشديد الياء والصرف، وزكر

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r7.claim: Abū Ḥātim says Zakari is indeclinable as foreign; the author rejects this and explains the distinct declension patterns.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: زكري بلا صرف

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r8.claim: Miḥrāb means the most honored place in an assembly.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r8.anchor: المحراب في اللغة أكرم موضع في المجلس

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r9.claim: A report places Mary in an upper room reached by a ladder.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r9.anchor: وجاء في الخبر: إنها كانت في غرفة كان زكريا يصعد إليها بسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r10.speaker: وضاح اليمين
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r10.claim: Waḍḍāḥ al-Yaman’s poem calls a room reached by a ladder a miḥrāb.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r10.anchor: قال وضاح اليمين: ربة محراب إذا جئتها لم ألقها حتى ارتقي سلما

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r11.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says elderly Hanne’s vow troubled Imran, who feared a girl could not serve; rabbis later cast lots with Torah pens for Mary.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r11.anchor: روى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال: حملت امرأة عمران بعد ما أسنت فنذرت ما في بطنها محررا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r12.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r12.claim: The same account says Zakariya housed Mary in a raised room, hired a wet nurse, and restricted entry as she grew.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r12.anchor: فكفلها زكريا وأخذ لها موضعا فلما أسنت جعل لها محرابا لا يرتقي إليه إلا بسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r13.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r13.claim: Al-Kalbī says Mary’s aunt was Zakariya’s wife.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r13.anchor: فتكون عند خالتها وكانت خالتها امرأة زكريا في قول الكلبي

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r14.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r14.claim: Muqātil says Mary’s sister was Zakariya’s wife and cared for her during menstruation.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r14.anchor: قال مقاتل: كانت أختها امرأة زكريا، وكانت إذا طهرت من حيضتها

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r15.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r15.claim: Some say Mary did not menstruate.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r15.anchor: وقال بعضهم: كانت لاتحيض وكانت مطهرة من الحيض

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r16.claim: Zakariya found seasonal fruit out of season; Mary’s answer that it came from God made him hope for a child.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r16.anchor: وكان زكريا إذا دخل عليها يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في القيظ وفاكهة القيظ في الشتاء

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r17.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r17.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses annā as min ayna, from where.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r17.anchor: ومعنى «أنى» من أين قاله أبو عبيدة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r18.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r18.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says ayna asks location while annā asks from what route or direction.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r18.anchor: قال النحاس: وهذا فيه تساهل لأن «أين» سؤال عن المواضع و «أنى» سؤال عن المذاهب

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r19.speaker: الكميت
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#2/r19.claim: Al-Kumayt’s verse distinguishes annā from min ayna.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#3/r1.claim: Kullamā is an accusative adverb governed by wajada, meaning each entry.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#3/r1.anchor: و «كلما» منصوب ب «وجد»، أي كل دخلة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#3/r2.claim: The statement may be Mary’s speech or independent; it prompted Zakariya to ask for a child.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:37-38#3/r2.anchor: قيل: هو من قول مريم، ويجوز أن يكون مستأنفا فكان ذلك سبب دعاء زكريا وسؤاله الولد

RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r1.claim: Qabul and taqabbul are close in meaning; Razi compares qabul with nabatan meaning inbatan, citing 71:17.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r1.anchor: إنما قال { فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن } ولم يقل : فتقبلها ربها بتقبل لأن القبول والتقبل متقاربان

RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r2.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r2.claim: Sibawayh lists qabul among five verbal nouns on the fu'ul pattern; wuqud is more often pronounced with damma as a verbal noun.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r2.anchor: والقبول مصدر قولهم : قبل فلان الشيء قبولا إذا رضيه ، قال سيبويه : خمسة مصادر جاءت على فعول : قبول وطهور ووضوء

RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج وثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r3.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj allow qabul with damma; Tha'lab transmits both vowelings from Ibn al-A'rabi.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r3.anchor: وأجاز الفراء والزجاج : قبولا بالضم ، وروى ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي

RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r4.claim: Taqabbul can suggest earnest effort, as in tasabbur and tajallud; pairing it with qabul conveys both great care and acceptance as natural and unforced.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r4.anchor: ما كان من باب التفعل فإنه يدل على شدة اعتناء ذلك الفاعل بإظهار ذلك الفعل كالتصبر والتجلد

RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r5.claim: These human-like implications cannot apply literally to God; metaphorically the wording signals great care in Mary's upbringing.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r5.anchor: وهذه الوجوه وإن كانت ممتنعة في حق الله تعالى ، إلا أنها تدل من حيث الاستعارة على حصول العناية العظيمة

RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet's report that Satan touches every newborn, causing its first cry, except Mary and her son; Abu Hurayra links it to Hanna's prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r6.anchor: روى أبو هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( ما من مولود يولد إلا والشيطان يمسه حين يولد

RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r7.claim: Al-Qadi objects that the solitary report conflicts with reason: infants cannot distinguish good and evil, Satan could do greater harm, the exception is unexplained, and the touch should leave lasting crying.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r7.anchor: طعن القاضي في هذا الخبر وقال : إنه خبر واحد على خلاف الدليل فوجب رده

RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r8.claim: Razi says these objections are conjectures and cannot justify rejecting the report.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25/r8.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الوجوه محتملة ، وبأمثالها لا يجوز دفع الخبر والله أعلم .

RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r1.claim: A report says Hanna wrapped Mary, presented her as a dedication to the sanctuary priests descended from Aaron, and after three river-lot trials Zakariyya's pen alone floated each time, so he took her.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r1.anchor: الوجه الثاني : في تفسير أن الله تعالى تقبلها بقبول حسن ، ما روي أن حنة حين ولدت مريم لفتها في خرقة

RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r2.speaker: الحسن عن القفال
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r2.claim: Al-Qaffal transmits from al-Hasan that Mary spoke in childhood like Jesus, never suckled, and received food from Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r2.anchor: الوجه الثالث : روى القفال عن الحسن أنه قال : إن مريم تكلمت في صباها كما تكلم المسيح ولم تلتقم ثديا قط

RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r3.claim: God accepted Mary as an infant, although the Israelite custom ordinarily required a capable boy able to serve the sanctuary.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r3.anchor: الوجه الرابع : في تفسير القبول الحسن أن المعتاد في تلك الشريعة أن التحرير لا يجوز إلا في حق الغلام

RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari supplies an implicit verb: God made her grow, and she grew with a fine growth.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : التقدير أنبتها فنبتت هي نباتا حسنا

RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r5.claim: Some commentators understand her fine growth physically, saying she grew in one day as much as an ordinary child grows in a year.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r5.anchor: أما الأول فقالوا : المعنى أنها كانت تنبت في اليوم مثل ما ينبت المولود في عام واحد

RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r6.claim: Others understand her growth religiously as righteousness, uprightness, chastity, and obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r6.anchor: وأما في الدين فلأنها نبتت في الصلاح والسداد والعفة والطاعة .

RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r7.claim: Kafala means providing for someone and attending to that person's interests; Razi illustrates it with the orphan-care hadith and Quran 38:23.
RAZI-FULL:v8p25#2/r7.anchor: يقال : كفل يكفل كفالة وكفلا فهو كافل ، وهو الذي ينفق على إنسان ويهتم بإصلاح مصالحه

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r1.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r1.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read kaffalaha with a doubled f, meaning God assigned Mary to Zakariyya.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r1.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي { وكفلها } بالتشديد ، ثم اختلفوا في زكريا

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r2.claim: Asim lengthens Zakariyya in the accusative; Hamza and al-Kisa'i shorten the accusative name, meaning God entrusted Mary to him.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r2.anchor: ثم اختلفوا في زكريا فقرأ عاصم بالمد ، وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالقصر على معنى ضمها الله تعالى إلى زكريا

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r3.claim: The remaining readers lengthen Zakariyya and make him nominative, so he took Mary into his care; Razi prefers this, matching 3:44 and the majority reading.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r3.anchor: والباقون قرأوا بالمد والرفع على معنى ضمها زكرياء إلى نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r4.claim: A transmission from Ibn Kathir reads the f of kafalaha with kasra.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r4.anchor: وعن ابن كثير في رواية { * كفلها } بكسر الفاء

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r5.claim: Shortening or lengthening Zakariyya are both Arabic dialect forms, like al-hayja and al-hayja'.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r5.anchor: وأما القصر والمد في زكريا فهما لغتان ، كالهيجاء والهيجا

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r6.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r6.claim: Mujahid reads the three verbs as imperatives and makes “her Lord” accusative, as if Hanna prayed: accept her, nurture her, appoint Zakariyya her guardian.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد { فتقبلها ربها وأنبتها وكفلها } على لفظ الأمر في الأفعال الثلاثة ، ونصب { ربها }

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r7.claim: Most commentators say Zakariyya became Mary's guardian in infancy, supported by transmitted reports.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r7.anchor: اختلفوا في كفالة زكريا عليه السلام إياها متى كانت ، فقال الأكثرون : كان ذلك حال طفوليتها

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r8.claim: Some say Zakariyya took custody after Mary was weaned.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل إنما كفلها بعد أن فطمت

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r9.claim: The after-weaning view takes growth before custody as chronological; the majority reply that waw does not require order, so growth and care could coincide.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r9.anchor: وهذا يوهم أن تلك الكفالة بعد ذلك النبات الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r10.claim: The after-weaning view says Mary had stopped nursing when Zakariyya found provisions; the other view says this visit happened near the end of his guardianship.
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r10.anchor: وأما الحجة الثانية : فلعل دخوله عليها وسؤاله منها هذا السؤال إنما وقع في آخر زمان الكفالة .

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r11.claim: Mihrab means an elevated and honored place.

RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r12.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
RAZI-FULL:v8p26/r12.claim: Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a's verse uses mihrab for a place one approaches by climbing a ladder.

RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r1.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r1.claim: Razi's school uses Mary's provision as evidence that saintly wonders are possible: ordinary food would not distinguish her.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r1.anchor: احتج أصحابنا على صحة القول بكرامة الأولياء بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r2.claim: If ordinary, the food would not demonstrate Mary's elevated rank, honor, or special distinction, which is the passage's purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r2.anchor: لا يكون حصول ذلك الرزق عند مريم دليلا على علو شأنها وشرف درجتها وامتيازها عن سائر الناس

RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r3.claim: The next verse says Zakariyya prayed for offspring; seeing an extraordinary provision encouraged hope despite his and his wife's old age.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r3.anchor: أنه تعالى قال بعد هذه الآية { هنالك دعا زكريا ربه قال رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة }

RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r4.claim: The indefinite rizqan magnifies the provision as strange and marvelous, supporting the argument only if it was extraordinary.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r4.anchor: أن التنكر في قوله { وجد عندها رزقا } يدل على تعظيم حال ذلك الرزق

RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r5.claim: Mary and her son are called a sign for the worlds in 21:91; Razi argues that this designation presupposes wonders.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى قال : { وجعلناها وابنها ءاية للعالمين } ( الأنبياء : 91 )

RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r6.claim: Al-Asma'i cites 38:21, where people scale the mihrab, to argue it is an upper chamber; it can also mean the most honored, elevated seat.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r6.anchor: واحتج الأصمعي على أن المحراب هو الغرفة

RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r7.claim: A report says Zakariyya built Mary an elevated room in the sanctuary, reached by stairs, and locked seven doors when he left.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27/r7.anchor: بنى زكريا عليه السلام لها غرفة في المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r1.claim: Mary's being born without a father is not by itself the sign: that claim needs a sign to authenticate it; the provision attests her truth and purity.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r1.anchor: قلنا : ليس هذا بآية ، بل يحتاج تصحيحه إلى آية ، فكيف نحمل الآية على ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r2.claim: Razi cites mutawatir reports that Zakariyya found winter fruit with Mary in summer and summer fruit in winter.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r2.anchor: ما تواترت الروايات به أن زكريا عليه السلام كان يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف ، وفاكهة الصيف في الشتاء

RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r3.claim: The wonder was not Zakariyya's miracle: as the only prophet then, he would have known a miracle performed through his prayer, and Mary informed him of the source.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r3.anchor: والأول باطل لأن النبي الموجود في ذلك الزمان هو زكريا عليه السلام ، ولو كان ذلك معجزة له لكان هو عالما

RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r4.claim: Since Zakariyya learned of the wonders from Mary rather than as their prophet's miracle, they were a karama of Mary or Jesus, establishing saintly wonders.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r4.anchor: فلم يبق إلا أن يقال : إنها كانت كرامة لعيسى عليه السلام ، أو كانت كرامة لمريم عليها السلام

RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r5.claim: Al-Jubba'i argues the wonders might be Zakariyya's miracles: he may have prayed for provision without knowing details, or seen heavenly food and asked whether someone sent it.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r5.anchor: اعترض أبو علي الجبائي وقال : لم لا يجوز أن يقال إن تلك الخوارق كانت من معجزات زكريا عليه السلام ، وبيانه من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r6.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r6.claim: Al-Jubba'i's first explanation is that Zakariyya prayed generally for provision, did not know the details, and recognized a miracle when a specific food appeared.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r6.anchor: اعترض أبو علي الجبائي وقال : لم لا يجوز أن يقال إن تلك الخوارق كانت من معجزات زكريا عليه السلام ، وبيانه من وجهين الأول

RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r7.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r7.claim: His second explanation is that Zakariyya saw ordinary food delivered from heaven and asked if another person sent it.
RAZI-FULL:v8p27#2/r7.anchor: اعترض أبو علي الجبائي وقال : لم لا يجوز أن يقال إن تلك الخوارق كانت من معجزات زكريا عليه السلام ، وبيانه من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r1.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r1.claim: Al-Jubba'i's alternative denies that any wonder appeared: God arranged provisions through believers who supported ascetic worshippers, and Zakariyya asked whether their source was improper.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r1.anchor: هذا مجموع ما قاله الجبائي في ( تفسيره )

RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r2.claim: Razi says an authorized miracle prayed for by Zakariyya would be certain to him, so he would not ask Mary; this also answers al-Jubba'i's second proposal.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r2.anchor: لأنه لو كان ذلك معجزا لزكريا عليه السلام كان مأذونا له من عند الله تعالى في طلب ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r3.claim: Ordinary donations would not distinguish Mary; if Zakariyya suspected an illicit source, Mary's answer alone could not dispel the suspicion.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r3.anchor: فإن كان في قلبه احتمال أنه ربما أتاها هذا الرزق من الوجه الذي لا ينبغي

RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r4.claim: The Mu'tazilites deny saintly wonders because extraordinary signs establish prophets' truth, and a proof of prophethood cannot occur in a non-prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r4.anchor: أما المعتزلة فقد احتجوا على امتناع الكرامات بأنها دلالات صدق الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r5.claim: A wonder confirms its claimant's truth: it indicates prophethood for a claimant to prophethood and sainthood for a claimant to sainthood.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r5.anchor: ظهور الفعل الخارق للعادة دليل على صدق المدعي

RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r6.claim: One response distinguishes orders: prophets are instructed to display miracles, while saints are instructed to conceal their wonders.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : الأنبياء مأمورون بإظهارها ، والأولياء مأمورون

RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r7.claim: A prophet claims a miracle and is certain of it, whereas a saint cannot claim such certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r7.anchor: النبي يدعي المعجز ويقطع به ، والولي لا يمكنه أن يقطع به

RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r8.claim: A prophetic miracle must be beyond challenge, whereas a saintly wonder need not be beyond challenge.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28/r8.anchor: أن المعجزة يجب انفكاكها عن المعارضة ، والكرامة لا يجب انفكاكها عن المعارضة

RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r1.claim: The closing statement that God provides without account may be Mary's speech or God's own speech.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r1.anchor: فهذا يحتمل أن يكون من جملة كلام مريم ، وأن يكون من كلام الله سبحانه وتعالى

RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r2.claim: “Without account” may mean without measure due to abundance, or without a request that would ordinarily lead to it; Razi compares 65:3.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r2.anchor: أي بغير تقدير لكثرته ، أو من غير مسألة سألها على سبيل يناسب حصولها

RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r3.claim: Razi closes Hanna's story and introduces the next account as the story of Zakariyya, quoting the opening of 3:38.
RAZI-FULL:v8p28#2/r3.anchor: وههنا آخر الكلام في قصة حنة . القصة الثانية واقعة زكريا عليه السلام
